```markdown
# Lawn Chair Refurbishing System

## Summary
The system described is a method for refurbishing an old lawn chair using duct tape, specifically for the purpose of entering the 3M Duct Tape Contest. The process involves cleaning the chair, repainting it, and applying layers of duct tape to create new straps that are both strong and aesthetically pleasing in a "Stars and Stripes" style.

## Step-by-Step Process

### START:
- Begin the lawn chair refurbishing process.

### PROCESS: Prepare the Chair
- INPUT: Old lawn chair, damp rag.
- Remove all old straps from the chair.
- Wipe off the aluminum frame of the chair with a damp rag.

### PROCESS: Repaint the Chair
- INPUT: Rust-proof hammered bronze spray paint.
- Apply several thin coats of spray paint to the chair frame.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the paint running?
  - Yes: Correct the application to prevent runs.
  - No: Continue to the next step.

### PROCESS: Measure Tape Length
- INPUT: Measuring tape.
- OUTPUT: Required tape length.
- Measure the width of the chair.
- Add approximately 3 inches to the measured width for tape overlap.

### PROCESS: Prepare Tape Strips
- INPUT: Duct tape.
- OUTPUT: Prepared tape strips.
- Secure two ends of a duct tape strip, sticky side up, to a stable surface (not on the chair).
- DECISION [IF]: Is the tape tight and secure?
  - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
  - No: Re-secure the tape until it is tight.

### PROCESS: Layer Tape for Strength
- INPUT: Additional duct tape strips.
- OUTPUT: Layered tape strips.
- Place another layer of tape on top of the first strip, sticky side down, leaving an inch and a half on each end uncovered.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the tape aligned correctly?
  - Yes: Press down to stick the layers together.
  - No: Realign the tape before sticking layers together.

### PROCESS: Remove Air Bubbles
- OUTPUT: Smooth layered tape strips.
- Run your finger along the tape to remove air bubbles.
- DECISION [IF]: Are there air bubbles remaining?
  - Yes: Continue to smooth out the tape.
  - No: Proceed to the next step.

### PROCESS: Repeat for Desired Strength
- OUTPUT: Desired number of tape layers.
- Repeat the layering process to reach the desired strength.
- STORE: Number of layers (e.g., three for this project).

### PROCESS: Create Straps
- INPUT: Red, white, and blue duct tape.
- OUTPUT: Completed woven straps.
- Apply the red horizontal strips first across the chair frame.
- Weave the white and one blue strip through the red strips.
- DECISION [IF]: Are the straps tight and evenly spaced?
  - Yes: Secure the straps to the chair frame.
  - No: Adjust the straps to ensure tightness and even spacing.

### PROCESS: Attach Straps to Chair
- OUTPUT: Refurbished chair with new straps.
- Ensure all vertical straps go under the metal bar at the back of the chair.

### END:
- Present the refurbished "Stars and Stripes" style lawn chair to grandmother on the 4th of July.
```

instruct00819.title: How to Start a Fire
instruct00819.text: What You Will Need Small Sticks Dry Grass/Leaves Lighter/Matches (Optional) Knife (Optional) Logs Water Large Rocks/Fire pit (Optional) Axe (Optional) Shovel (Optional) Protective Gloves/ GlassesPrecautionsWARNING: Building a fire is dangerous and should be done with caution. Kids under the age of 15 should not handle fire, it is not a game and it is never okay to play with fire. Never burn plastic in a fire because harmful chemicals will be released in the air. Do not throw fireworks of any sort in a fire because it can hurt people, and damage property. Keep children and pets away from the fire, and never leave the fire unattended. Before You Start Tie up any long hair Wear protective gear (glasses, gloves, and shoes) Keep a bucket of water nearby Keep extremely flammable items away Have a first aid kit handy just in case Find an open area away from fences, sheds, and trees to build a fire Make sure there are no cables or telephone wires above the selected area Dig up any grass with the shovel so the circle is mainly dirt. The circle size depends on how big the desired fire is. For a large fire, clear a larger space and gather more logs, sticks, and dry grass/leaves. For a small fire, clear a smaller space and gather less supplies. This helps to contain the fire, as well as keeping it insulated within the wall of rocks.EXCEPTION: IF A MANMADE FIRE PIT IS AVAILABLE, USE THAT. The twigs and sticks are the kindling for the fire. This is the base for the fire and will catch a flame after the tinder gets a spark. The dry grass and leaves act as tinder for the fire. Tinder is the first thing that catches a spark when lit. The tinder then transfers the spark to the kindling and starts a flame. Gradually add more kindling to the fire and blow on it to create more heat. EXCEPTION: IF A LIGHTER OR MATCHES AREN'T AVAILABLE USE A KNIFE OR OTHER SHARP TOOL TO CUT A "V" IN A FLAT PIECE OF WOOD. PLACE BITS OF BARK IN THE V-SHAPED NOTCH TO CATCH AN EMBER. FIND A ROUND STICK, PLACE IT IN THE NOTCH, AND USING YOUR FLAT PALMS SPIN THE STICK BACK AND FORTH IN THE NOTCH WHILE GENTLY PUSHING DOWN ON THE WOODEN PLANK. WHEN THE PLANK BEGINS TO SPARK, TRANSFER IT TO THE TINDER PILE AND BLOW ON IT TO CREATE A FIRE. For this example, we will build a square of logs stacked about two logs high. In the middle of the square, construct a teepee shape with other logs. This arrangement allows a lot of airflow through the structure. It is important that oxygen can get through because it is needed to keep the fire going.EXCEPTION: USE AXE TO CHOP UP LOGS IF NEEDED. When putting out the fire, throw some water on it to fully extinguish any hot embers that could possibly start another flame.

instruct00066.title: Turn Empty Water Bottles Into Alcohol Fueled Rockets
instruct00066.text: Not long ago I was challenged to create a project using a water bottle that could be displayed in a one minute long video. While I missed the one minute mark, I think I still managed to make a pretty entertaining device. The rocket and launcher featured in the above video function off of a very simple concept of igniting aflammablevapor using a replacementbarbecueigniter topropelthe bottle through the air. The parts for this project should cost no more than $15, with the igniter taking up the majority of that price tag at about $10. The bottles can be reused many times until the heat from repeated shots eventually warps the plastic. Be sure to check out my other Instructables, and take a moment to subscribe to my YouTube channel:http://www.youtube.com/user/Nighthawkinlight Thanks for reading!

instruct00248.title: T-shirt Designs With Stencils and Bleach (updated With Robot Image for Download)
instruct00248.text: Make your own awesome t-shirt designs using stencils and a simple solution of bleach and water. This project requires minimal tools, and it comes together fairly easily.**update** The robot stencil shown is now available for download Enough talk, let's get started! Here's what I used for this shirt (really you can use just about anything for the stencil): - Sharp hobby knife - Sheets of cardboard (flattened cardboard boxes work well) - Spray bottle (got mine from the Dollar Store, though they charged $1.67, what a crock!) - Bleach (again Dollar Dollar, but was more. Seriously guys, change your name) - A fun shape (any object will work so long as its silhouette is easily recognizable) - Plain t-shirts Mix the bleach and water 50/50, you're going to need a bit so I'd recommend a minimum of 250ml (1 cup) of each. Now is a good time to wash your shirts to get the shrinking out of the way. Do some homework, figure out what images work, and which ones don't. You can use something from a magazine like people, or maybe something from the internet. Again we are looking for simple shapes that are easily recognizable in silhouette. An easy way to check is to cut out your image and flip it over, if you can still make out what it is without seeing the internal detail you're golden! For this shirt I used a blue whale I found on the www. Yup it's time to play with knives! So once you've cut out your image, you can stick hum to the cardboard and cut it out, or trace and then cut. If you're feeling super creative why not try drawing directly on the cardboard then cut it out. A word of caution is not to make the shapes too detailed, as this method tends to let the bleach bleed a little and fine detail will not show up. So for this shirt we are going with a whale in the ocean, no aside from the whale I'm going to need something that looks like a waterline for the ocean. Find a well ventilated area to do your spraying in. I'd suggest the garage, or some place outside. Remember folks, you're spraying bleach onto fabric, so doing this on your nice new rug isn't such a hot idea. Place a sheet of cardboard inside the shirt to stop the bleach from stenciling the image on the other side. Composite your cut outs as you want them on your shirt. For this image I chose to do the wave portion first, then placed the negative cut out of the whale afterwards. This is a little more complex than just one spray, but it looks good. Wait until the fabric starts to turn the colour intensity that you desire, then quickly rinse the shirt thoroughly to stop the bleaching process and remove any excess. Your t-shirt is now done! Wash again to remove that awesome bleach smell, and you're ready to show off your new shirt to your friends down at the library, falconeering enthusiast club, or just wear it around the lab. I decided to embelish these guys a little more. The one on the left is done with fabic paint applied with a brush, and the one on the right has fabic squares sewed to it with fabric paint directly applied to the squares. Now you're ready to show off your neat-o new custom t-shirts! You're sure to be the talk of where ever you go! Remember to make sure your designs are not too intricate so your bleach spray doesn't bleed and ruin the crisp edges of your design. Pros of this method: Fading effect, and some crisp edges where the spray meets the card. Cons of this method: Potential for the bleach to bleed under the card, so be careful.**update**- September 6, 2010 Uploaded the robot image, feel free to download the PDF and make your own!

```markdown
# T-Shirt Designing System Using Stencils and Bleach

## System Overview
This system outlines the process of creating custom t-shirt designs using stencils and a bleach solution. The process involves preparing the materials, creating the stencil, applying the bleach, and finalizing the t-shirt design.

## System Requirements
- Sharp hobby knife
- Sheets of cardboard
- Spray bottle
- Bleach
- Plain t-shirts
- A silhouette shape for the stencil (e.g., blue whale)
- Access to a well-ventilated area

## System Process

### START:
- Begin the t-shirt designing process.

### INPUT: Gather Materials
- Sharp hobby knife
- Sheets of cardboard
- Spray bottle
- Bleach
- Plain t-shirts
- Selected silhouette shape for the stencil

### PROCESS: Prepare Bleach Solution
- Mix bleach and water in a 50/50 ratio.
- OUTPUT: Bleach solution ready for use.

### PROCESS: Pre-Wash T-Shirts
- Pre-wash plain t-shirts to avoid shrinkage.
- OUTPUT: Pre-shrunk t-shirts ready for design.

### PROCESS: Select and Prepare Stencil Design
- Choose a simple, recognizable silhouette shape.
- PROCESS: Create Stencil
  - Use a hobby knife to cut out the silhouette from cardboard.
  - OUTPUT: Stencil ready for use.

### DECISION: Is the selected area well-ventilated? [IF YES] [ELSE NO]
- IF YES:
  - Continue to the next step.
- ELSE NO:
  - Find a well-ventilated area before proceeding.
  - END: Cannot proceed without a proper area.

### PROCESS: Protect T-Shirt from Bleed-Through
- Place a sheet of cardboard inside the t-shirt.
- OUTPUT: T-shirt protected from bleach bleed-through.

### PROCESS: Arrange Stencil on T-Shirt
- Position the stencil on the t-shirt as desired.
- OUTPUT: T-shirt ready for bleach application.

### PROCESS: Apply Bleach Solution
- Use the spray bottle to apply the bleach solution onto the stencil.
- OUTPUT: Bleach applied to t-shirt.

### DECISION: Has the fabric reached the desired color intensity? [IF YES] [ELSE NO]
- IF YES:
  - Proceed to rinse the shirt.
- ELSE NO:
  - Continue to monitor and spray if necessary.

### PROCESS: Rinse the T-Shirt
- Rinse the t-shirt thoroughly to stop the bleaching process.
- OUTPUT: Bleached t-shirt with design.

### PROCESS: Post-Design Wash
- Wash the t-shirt to remove any remaining bleach smell.
- OUTPUT: Finalized t-shirt ready to wear.

### END:
- The custom t-shirt design process is complete.

## Additional Options (Post-Process Embellishments):
- Apply fabric paint with a brush for extra detail.
- Sew fabric squares and apply fabric paint for a unique look.
- Download and use the provided robot stencil PDF for additional designs.

## System Notes
- Ensure designs are not too intricate to prevent bleach from bleeding under the stencil.
- Pros: Fading effect and crisp edges where the spray meets the card.
- Cons: Potential for bleach to bleed under the card, requiring caution during application.
- Update: Robot stencil available for download.
```

instruct00746.title: How to Make Paper Speakers From Scratch
instruct00746.text: How to Make paper Speakers From Scratch This is a speaker i made from scratch useing scraps i found around my home. The goal of this project was to make a speaker for free out of scrap. The other thing was that i did not use a pre made speaker to make this. I will show how to make it, so you can build your own :) Heres a video of the sound of my speaker.https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iAmdezxojSg Tools soldering iron solder scissorsParts construction paper card board card board tube audio jack wire coated copper magnetwire (This must be atleast 8 ohms to protect your devices) tape magnet PAPER cup paperclip Make a copper wire coil a little bit bigger than the diameter of your magnet. Place the wire in the center of the bottom of the cup. Now build a bracket to hold the magnet. The magnet must be placed in the center of the wire coil. To make the bracket make the paper clip straight. Then tale it io a peice of card board. Then flip it over and tape the magnet on the back side of the bracket. Make shure you tape secureley because this part must resist the vibrations from the magnetisim when the speaker is on. Now tape the bracket to the bottom of the cup. Make shure the magnet is placed in the center of the coil. Also make shure to secureley tape this on. You now havea barespeaker with no way to connect to the music player. Now you have a ugly cup with card board on it. Now make it look a little better by adding a case! Because this is supposed to be a paper speaker i made the case out of cardboard and paper. First make a front plate out of card board. Trace the diameter of the top of the cup on to a peice of cardboard and then cut it out. Now make a support to make the cup level. Made out of a card board tube and taped to the cup. Make a bottom panel. Make shure you leave some room in the back for the wires. Now make a back pannel. Tape it soit willopen like a door. Also cut a hole so the audio jack wires can come out. Solder the 2 coil wires to the audio jack wires. It does not matter which way they are connected. Now cover the card board with paper so it would look nice. The speaker may require some fine tuneing of the coil to get some sound out of it. The volume of it will come from the streingth of the magnet and the coil. The speaker quality is pretty good considering that its made of paper and hand made. If all works well, Enjoy your speakers!!!

```markdown
# How to Make Paper Speakers From Scratch

## System Overview
The system described is a method for constructing a functional speaker using commonly found household items. The final output of the system is a paper speaker capable of playing audio from a music player.

### Inputs:
- Construction paper
- Cardboard
- Cardboard tube
- Audio jack
- Wire
- Coated copper magnet wire (minimum 8 ohms)
- Tape
- Magnet
- Paper cup
- Paperclip

### Tools:
- Soldering iron
- Solder
- Scissors

### Outputs:
- Homemade paper speaker

### Process Steps:

**START:**
1. **PROCESS:** Begin by gathering all required materials and tools.

2. **INPUT:** Make a copper wire coil. The coil should be slightly larger than the diameter of your magnet.
   - **SUBPROCESS:** Measure and cut the copper wire.
   - **OUTPUT:** Copper wire coil.

3. **PROCESS:** Place the wire coil in the center of the bottom of the paper cup.

4. **PROCESS:** Construct a bracket to hold the magnet using a straightened paperclip and a piece of cardboard.
   - **SUBPROCESS:** Straighten the paperclip and tape it to the cardboard.
   - **OUTPUT:** Bracket for magnet.

5. **PROCESS:** Tape the magnet securely to the back side of the bracket.
   - **DECISION [IF]:** Is the magnet taped securely?
     - **YES:** Proceed to step 6.
     - **NO:** Re-tape the magnet until secure.

6. **PROCESS:** Tape the bracket with the magnet to the bottom of the cup, ensuring the magnet is centered within the coil.
   - **DECISION [IF]:** Is the magnet centered and taped securely?
     - **YES:** Proceed to step 7.
     - **NO:** Adjust the bracket and re-tape as necessary.

7. **PROCESS:** The basic speaker structure is now complete but lacks connectivity to a music player.
   - **OUTPUT:** Basic speaker assembly.

8. **PROCESS:** Enhance the appearance of the speaker by constructing a case from cardboard and paper.
   - **SUBPROCESS:** Create a front plate, support structure, bottom panel, and back panel with an opening for wires.
   - **OUTPUT:** Speaker case.

9. **PROCESS:** Solder the two wires from the coil to the audio jack wires.
   - **DECISION [IF]:** Is the soldering complete and secure?
     - **YES:** Proceed to step 10.
     - **NO:** Resolder the connections.

10. **PROCESS:** Cover the cardboard structure with paper for an aesthetically pleasing finish.
    - **OUTPUT:** Finished speaker casing.

11. **PROCESS:** Fine-tune the coil if necessary to improve sound output.
    - **DECISION [IF]:** Does the speaker produce sound after tuning?
      - **YES:** Proceed to step 12.
      - **NO:** Continue adjusting the coil and testing.

12. **OUTPUT:** If all steps are successful, enjoy your homemade paper speakers.

**END.**
```

instruct00023.title: Geeky Crochet Hooks! Made With Polymer Clay!
instruct00023.text: Geeky Crochet Hooks! Made with polymer clay. If you crochet or know someone who does...and they are geeky... they will love these! Great gift idea! The Elder Wand from Harry Potter Lothlorien leaf and the One Ring from Lord of the Rings King Arthur's Excalibur from Merlin/Arthurian Legend Sonic Screwdriver from Doctor Who Lightsaber from Star Wars You'll need crochet hooks. You can use any size hook...I recommend the metal ones, but I am sure the plastic ones would work too...after all, I've made lightsabers and sonic screwdrivers out of plastic pens. You'll need bake hard polymer clay too...like fimo or sculpey. (I used a combo of both, since I am running low on stock!) "And desire for the Elder Wand, the Deathstick, unbeatable, invincible, swallowed him once more." I began making Prof. Dumbledore's Elder Wand from Harry Potter. I started with some brown...I swirled it with some white to give it sort of a marbled "wood-grain" texture. Take a thin "snake" and twirl it around the handle. Then roll it between your hands to smooth it out. Then add some "knots"...Awesome. "Okay, this can function as a sonic blaster, a sonic cannon, and a triple-fold sonic disruptor. Doc, what you got?" For the Sonic Screwdriver: Begin with the same technique of twirly clay around the handle and smoothing it out by rolling it between hands. Added silver features and a blue ball on the end. A flat shape with cut-outs, fits tightly around the tip... And a slim black line... A Sonic Screwdriver worth of the Doctor himself. The Lord of the Rings inspired... Lothlorien Leaf and the One Ring. "One Ring to rule them all, One Ring to find them, One Ring to bring them all and in the darkness bind them." Same start as the others. With a twirl of green like a vine. To make the ring, I just pressed a piece of gold clay and inscribbled some markings on it. And just wrapped it around the end. instruct00659.title: How to Burp Your Car's Cooling System
instruct00659.text: This instructable will walk you through the simple process of "burping" or getting all of the trapped air out of your cars cooling system. This works for ALL Vehicles If you have had any parts replaced on your cars cooling system (radiator, waterpump, new hoses, ect) then there is a chance that your cooling system has air trapped in it and this could make your cars cooling system operate poorly, or in worst cases minic the symptoms of a cracked head. So BEFORE you spend thousands of dollars at the mechanics having this done, try this and see if your cooling system operates normal (temp stays within normal , does not get hot or overheat). AnitFreeze or Dex cool, I used the 50/50 water dexcool mix Spill free funnel ($20.00 on Amazon.com) Rag to wipe area clean Time and Patience Make sure that your overflow tank is at the level of coolant where the line marked "COLD" is, make sure that you car is cold, do not try this with a engine that has been running. Open your radiator cap, insert the angled peice of the spill free funnel into the correct cap for you car, then the main peice of the funnel on that, Make sure that you have all conections on sung so that there are no leaks. Now fill the funnel a little past half way, the reason for this is when your cars thermostat opens up the level will rise and drop with the opening and closing of it and with the escaping of the trapped air. YOUR CAR SHOULD BE OFF, DO NOT START YOU CAR YET!! Go to your car, and set the climate controll settings to the hot or heat setting but make sure that the fan/heater is in the OFF posistion. NOW you can start you car. This is where the waiting happens, your car has to get up to temp so that the thermostat opens up to cool your engine, one this happens you will see the coolant level drop in the funnel, and a few to a large amount of air bubbles comming up from the coolant, this is the trapped air escaping your cooling system. Sit back and watch this happen while enjoying a cold one, cuase in order to fully Burp your system the engine has to go through SEVERAL COOLING CYCLES........ I gave it the standard hour of running, if you still see air bubble comming out after that, check your overflow tank and make sure it has coolant in it. If it does not add some so the level is at the HOT line (becase you have now been running your car for awhile now). The bubbles should stop and when it does turn your car off. Now you will use the plug that came with the Funnel and plug the hole in the funnel so you can recycle or put the unused collant back in its container, do this with the plug in the funnel , put the funnel in the opening of your coolant container and lift up to remove the plug. Take the funnels cap off of your radiator and put your cap back on, use the rag to wipe any coolant off of your car. Now when you drive your car you should see a big differance in how it cools your engine. If you are still getting high temp readings you might want to check to make sure that your thermostat is working and replace it if needed.

```markdown
# Comprehensive Structured Summary of Vehicle Cooling System Burping

## START:
- Ensure the car is cold and has not been running.

## INPUT: Required Materials
- Antifreeze or Dex Cool (50/50 water mix recommended)
- Spill-free funnel
- Rag for cleaning
- Time and patience

## PROCESS: Preparing the Cooling System
1. Verify the overflow tank coolant level aligns with the "COLD" line indicator.
2. Open the radiator cap.

## PROCESS: Setting Up the Spill-Free Funnel
1. Insert the angled piece of the funnel into the correct cap for your car.
2. Attach the main piece of the funnel onto the angled piece.
3. Ensure all connections are secure to prevent leaks.

## PROCESS: Filling the Funnel
1. Fill the funnel a little past halfway with the antifreeze mixture.

## PROCESS: Climate Control Settings
1. Set the car's climate control to the hot or heat setting.
2. Ensure the fan/heater is in the OFF position.

## PROCESS: Starting the Car
1. Start the car with the spill-free funnel in place and climate control set.

## PROCESS: Burping the Cooling System
1. Wait for the car to reach operating temperature so the thermostat can open.
2. Observe the coolant level drop and air bubbles escape as the system burps.

## DECISION [IF]: Has the engine gone through several cooling cycles?
- [IF YES]: Proceed to the next step.
- [IF NO]: Continue running the engine and observing until several cycles complete.

## PROCESS: Monitor and Adjust Coolant Level
1. After an hour, check for continuous air bubbles.
2. If no bubbles, proceed to the next step.
3. If bubbles persist, check and adjust the overflow tank coolant to the "HOT" line.

## OUTPUT: End of Burping Process
- If no more air bubbles are observed, the burping process is complete.

## PROCESS: Recycling Unused Coolant
1. Use the plug that came with the funnel to seal the funnel.
2. Transfer the unused coolant back to its container.

## PROCESS: Finalizing the Process
1. Remove the funnel from the radiator.
2. Replace the radiator cap with the original cap.
3. Wipe away any spilled coolant with a rag.

## OUTPUT: Expected Result
- The vehicle should exhibit improved cooling efficiency.

## DECISION [IF]: Is the vehicle still experiencing high temperatures?
- [IF YES]: Check and potentially replace the thermostat.
- [IF NO]: End the process.

## END:
- The process is completed once the car cools efficiently or the thermostat is checked/replaced.
```

instruct00291.title: Cookie Bra
instruct00291.text: Surprise the man of your heart with this sweet and easy to make, cookie-bra! Sure to be appreciated :)IF YOU LIKE THIS INSTRUCTABLE FEEL FREE TO VOTE FOR IT :) use plasterstrips to get an imprint of your chest - you want the bra the right size. I'm not showing that step, due I don't want to see my chest on the internet ;) - i'm sure you'll figure out how to do that. Instructions are found on the package of the plasterstrips. When the imprint is dry cover it with aluminiumfoil. you can use all cookie doughs that can be used with cookiecutters. the recipe I used: 0,5 egg 125g flour 62g sugar 62g butter 1Tablespoon Cocoapowder 1 teaspoon vanillasugar 1 little bit bakingpowder and for flavour 2 tablespoons of instant cappuccino Form the cups of the bra on your covered mold. make sure to make it evenly thick - about 0,5 cm bake it on 200C for about 10minutes ( may vary with another recipe) at this point you can get as creative as you want :) Here's what I did: melt some white choclate in the still warm oven spread it with a clean brush on the warm bra. mix some white chocolate with cacoa-powder and paint whatever you like :) brush some chocolate on the edge of the bra and sprinkle it with chocolate-pieces let everything cool down. carefully peel the foil of the mold take a corkskrew and make holes to join the two cups in the middle - be very careful! tie the cups together with a nice lace or string. Your done! Now surprise your beloved one and have a nice cup of tea! - Or whatever you like :D

```markdown
# Cookie-Bra Creation Process

## START:
  - Begin the process of creating a cookie-bra.

## PROCESS: Create the Mold
  - INPUT: Plaster strips to create a chest imprint.
  - PROCESS: Follow instructions on the plaster strip package to create the mold.
  - OUTPUT: A chest imprint mold.

## PROCESS: Prepare the Mold
  - INPUT: Aluminum foil.
  - PROCESS: Cover the dry chest imprint mold with aluminum foil.
  - OUTPUT: Aluminum foil-covered mold ready for cookie dough.

## PROCESS: Make Cookie Dough
  - INPUT:
    - 0.5 egg
    - 125g flour
    - 62g sugar
    - 62g butter
    - 1 tablespoon cocoa powder
    - 1 teaspoon vanilla sugar
    - A little bit of baking powder
    - 2 tablespoons of instant cappuccino (for flavor)
  - PROCESS: Combine ingredients to form cookie dough.
  - OUTPUT: Cookie dough ready to be shaped.

## PROCESS: Form the Bra Cups
  - PROCESS: Use the cookie dough to form cups on the mold.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the dough evenly thick, approximately 0.5 cm?
    - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
    - No: Adjust the dough thickness before proceeding.

## PROCESS: Bake the Bra Cups
  - INPUT: Preheated oven at 200°C.
  - PROCESS: Bake the dough-formed bra cups for about 10 minutes.

    - No: Continue baking until done.
  - OUTPUT: Baked bra cups.

## PROCESS: Decorate the Bra Cups
  - INPUT: White chocolate, cocoa powder, brush, chocolate pieces.
  - PROCESS: Melt some white chocolate in the still-warm oven.

  - PROCESS: Mix some white chocolate with cocoa powder to paint designs.

  - PROCESS: Let everything cool down.
```

instruct00518.title: Puppet Climbing Chalk Bag
instruct00518.text: Chalk bags are how you show your personality at the gym or local bouldering area. Make sure everyone and their brother knows you're a boss with this DIY chalk bag! To make your chalk bag you'll need your favorite puppet or golf club head cover and a bunch of felty material. The material I used was left over and found in our scrap materials bin. You'll want something a little nappier than suede but not quite as nappy as felt. It should hold the chalk in the bag but not absorb all the chalk, feel the inside of a store bought chalk bag if you're really stuck. You'll need about a yard per bag unless you are a super high efficiency cutter. You'll also need a length of string and a little clamp end to tighten the string like a draw string. For the puppet just try not to pick something too bulky as you'll be carrying it when you climb. The idea here is to make a little can shaped bag that fits on the inside of the puppet. - Measure the circumference of the opening of the puppet and cut a circle of material with a similar circumference. - Measure the depth of your puppet and cut a rectangle of felt with the depth as length of one side and the circumference as the length of the other. (This depth should not be greater then 2/3 the height of your hand.) - Sew ends of the rectangle together that are the length of the depth. - Next sew the circular piece of material to the bottom of your loop and be sure that the material you want to feel is on the inside of the bag. - Finally, flip the edge of the bag over and sew it to the bag leaving a little opening to feed the string into and out of. The idea here is to create a little sleeve to put a draw string through. Feed the string through and cut it at an appropriate length and attach the string clamp. Here you're going to put your new bag into the puppet and pick out some thread that matches the color of your puppet. Sew the bag to the puppet below your drawstring section so that there is enough material to make a closed 'lid' over the puppet when the drawstring is pulled tight. The last thing you need is a way to attach the bag to your harness. I found some of my sister's hair ties around the house that matched the color of my puppets and sewed them on. You could also use a bit more string or a wider piece of material if you want to attach a belt to use it for bouldering so it won't spin. Take your pick! Finally, attach a carabiner and get climbing!

instruct00712.title: How to Create an MTV-like Music Video W/ Photos in 5 Mins
instruct00712.text: When someone sends us a 284 photo slideshow, we pretty much want to shoot ourselves. 32 minutes of near-fatal boredom.A few of us computer geeks and tv/film producers locked ourselves in a room for a year and set out to build a tool to help people out there save people like us from "death by slideshows". (Plus we think slideshows are so 1992.)So we built animoto.com. Think of it as a little black box filled with film & TV producers, tech nerds, robots, and indie rockers. You basically put your photos and a piece of music in one end, shake it up, and a photo music video pops out the other end -- all magically orchestrated to the music and with professional post-production technique. And it only takes a few steps. The robots pretty much do all the hard work. And creating Shorts (30 second videos) is free. You can make, remix, and share as many as you want.You need three things:1. Digital photos or images2. Some Music (although you can also choose from their library)3. Computer w/ Internet Connectionhttp://www.animoto.comCreate a video HERE or click on the steps above for more details.Here a DEMO VIDEO.Here a 60 second overview of what the black box technology does: First, choose the type of video you want to create. Either (1) an Animoto Short or (2) a Full-Length Extended Video. An Animoto Short is 30-seconds or less and is free. Full-length videos require a credit. You can either UPLOAD images from your computer or RETRIEVE them from another site. When you choose to UPLOAD images from you computer, use your CTRL or SHIFT key to choose multiple photos from your browser. When RETRIEVING images from another site, choose from Flickr, Facebook, Smugmug, Picasa, or Photobucket to import from. You will be asked to GRANT ACCESS to allow Animoto to access your photo albums. Then, choose the album you want to animate. Once your project is populated with your images, you can add/delete, drag to rearrange, rotate,or "spotlight" the ones you want to emphasize in your video. You can either SELECT a song from the Animoto collection or UPLOAD one from your computer. If you choose to SELECT a song from Animoto, you will be asked to choose a genre of music. You will then be given a list of soundtracks which you can preview, learn more about and/or select for your music video. Once you select a song, use the slider tool to choose the entry point of the song. Finalize your video by entering the video information that will appear as credits at the end of the video -- video title, video description, your name. Then click CREATE VIDEO . After a few minutes, voila! You will receive an email with a link to your music video! Review and if you want to put your images and music back through the render engine again to see what Animoto comes up with, just click the REMIX button and choose ONE-CLICK REMIX. If you want to edit the photo selection or music, click the REMIX button and choose EDITING REMIX. You now have your own personal music video!

instruct00836.title: The Awesomest Coolest Easiest Water Bowl for DOGS & CATS!
instruct00836.text: This is a water bowl for dogs or cats. It is super EASY! In a few simple steps you could have a water bowl that you only have to fill up once in a while, and it holds twice as much water for later on. In this project you don't need to buy a whole new bowl, you just reuse your dog's regular bowl. If you are worried that you have to drill, nail, or put glue on the bowl, don't be concerned. This project doesn't do anything to the bowl. One important thing though, make sure you KEEP THE TOP OF THE 2L BOTTLE!NOTE: This Watering Bowl was designed, built, and written-up to share on Instructables, by my 11-year old daughter. It's important that I give credit where credit is due, so any and all praise goes to her... the suggestions and critiques as well. It turned out really well, and I'm quite proud of the fact that she wanted to share how she did it here. Nice work super girl! What's your next invention going to be? #proudDad For this project you will need: -2 by 4 piece of wood about 16 inches long -1 by 6 piece of wood about 12 inches long -2L bottle -Dog dish -Velcro tape (2 pieces of fuzzy sided, 2 pieces of hooked sided) -Nails (3) -Hammer -Wood glue -Wood clamp -Spray paint or stain (optional) Take the 2 by 4 and position it in the middle of the end of the 1 by 6. When you found the spot you like, outline around the outside of the 2 by 4 with a pencil. You are marking where the boards are going to attach to each other. Once you outline the bottom of the 2 by 4, glue it onto the 1 by 6 in the spot that you picked. The outline should help you line it up. Once you do that, clamp it! Nail the 2 by 4 to the 1 by 6. After that, stick the 2 soft piece of Velcro on the 2 by 4 piece of wood. Look at the pictures to see how I placed them. Suggestion: Use the 2L bottle to measure where to put the soft Velcro (Hint: make sure that one piece of soft Velcro is almost to the top of the 2L bottle so it stay). The end of it should stick into the bowl at the height you want the water to fill up to. Once done with that, stick the hard Velcro to the soft Velcro. Put the 2L bottle on the sticky side of the Velcro and you are DONE!!! Remember: Wherever the tip of the 2L bottle is that is how high the water will be. I have had to move the bottle down because so much water was spilling. This step is optional. You can spray paint or stain your piece. What I did was first spray paint it green. Then I took craft paint and painted cool designs. Have FUN! It's for you pet after all! Fill up the 2L bottle and the put the cap on on it. Line up the velcro so that the top of the water bottle is facing down. Unscrew the cap and WHOOSHHH! The water comes down! Now it may come down fast but as soon as the water reaches the tip of the 2L bottle it stops. As the water reaches underneath the tip of the 2L bottle, more water comes out to fill the bowl back up. One tip: Don't fill up the bottle all the way it makes it too heavy, and it falls ( I would fill it up at the most half way for the bottle). Make sure you also fill the water bowl. Remember: Wherever the tip of the 2L bottle is that is how high the water will be. I have had to move the bottle down because so much water was spilling. Hope you find the project useful!

```markdown
# Automated Pet Water Bowl System

## System Overview
The system allows for the creation of an automated pet water bowl that refills itself from a 2L bottle. The system requires no drilling, nailing, or gluing to the pet's existing bowl, and is designed to be easy to assemble and use.

## Materials
- 2 by 4 piece of wood (16 inches long)
- 1 by 6 piece of wood (12 inches long)
- 2L bottle
- Dog dish
- Velcro tape (2 pieces of fuzzy sided, 2 pieces of hooked sided)
- Nails (3)
- Hammer
- Wood glue
- Wood clamp
- Spray paint or stain (optional)

## System Steps

### START
START: Begin the process of creating the automated pet water bowl system.

### PROCESS: Preparing the Wooden Base
1. INPUT: Take the 2 by 4 piece of wood and position it in the middle of the end of the 1 by 6 piece of wood.
2. PROCESS: Outline around the outside of the 2 by 4 with a pencil to mark where the boards will attach.
3. INPUT: Apply wood glue on the outlined area of the 1 by 6 piece of wood.
4. PROCESS: Place the 2 by 4 onto the glued area of the 1 by 6, using the outline for alignment.
5. PROCESS: Use a wood clamp to hold the pieces together.
6. INPUT: Hammer in 3 nails to secure the 2 by 4 to the 1 by 6.

### PROCESS: Attaching Velcro for Bottle Support
7. PROCESS: Stick the 2 soft pieces of Velcro on the 2 by 4 piece of wood at positions that match the height of the 2L bottle.
8. PROCESS: Stick the hard Velcro to the corresponding soft Velcro pieces.

### DECISION: Painting or Staining the Base [IF] [ELSE]
9. DECISION [IF]: Is painting or staining desired?
   - Yes: PROCESS: Apply spray paint or stain to the wooden base and add optional designs.
   - No: OUTPUT: Proceed without painting or staining.

### PROCESS: Setting Up the Water Bottle
10. INPUT: Fill the 2L bottle up to half-way to avoid making it too heavy.
11. PROCESS: Attach the 2L bottle to the Velcro on the wooden base with the top facing down.
12. PROCESS: Align the tip of the 2L bottle where the desired water level should be in the bowl.

### PROCESS: Activating the Water Dispenser
13. INPUT: Unscrew the cap of the 2L bottle to allow water to flow into the bowl.
14. PROCESS: Observe as the water stops flowing when it reaches the tip of the 2L bottle.
15. DECISION [IF]: Does the water level exceed the desired height?
    - Yes: PROCESS: Adjust the position of the 2L bottle down to reduce water flow.
    - No: OUTPUT: The system is functioning correctly.

### END
16. OUTPUT: The automated pet water bowl system is now complete and operational.
END: The process of creating the automated pet water bowl system is concluded.
```

instruct00101.text: Phono-Horn. A paper sound dock for your smart phone! Play your phone through the Phono Horn and the sound output is richer and clearer with improved bass response. This model was originally published on robives.com a website full of paper animations to download and make. NEW: Base for Galaxy S3, free download. # Phono-Horn Assembly System

```markdown
## START:
- Begin the Phono-Horn assembly process.

## INPUT:
- Coloured card (230 micron / 67lb).
- Access to a printer.
- Scoring tool.
- Scissors or cutting tool.
- Glue.
- Phono-Horn template sheets (including the appropriate base template for iPhone 4S, Samsung Galaxy S2/S3/S4).

- Carefully cut out all the parts.

## PROCESS: [Assemble Horn]
- Fold and glue the wide ends of the horn pieces to create triangular tubes for rigidity.
- Glue two horn pieces with tabs at the end together, aligning parts accurately.
- Alternate gluing pairs of horn pieces, two with tabs and two without.
- Roll and glue the horn's end into a circle.
- Progressively glue each row along the horn up to its end.

- Attach the end pipe to the horn.

- Fold and glue the horn holder, ensuring the small hole aligns with the phone's loudspeaker.
- Glue the five base parts together, maintaining a square shape for stability.
- Attach the horn holder to the base.

## OUTPUT:
- The completed base structure ready to receive the horn.

## PROCESS: [Fit the Horn]
- Fit the horn onto the base without gluing it.

## DECISION [IF iPhone version]:

- Assemble and glue the two back cross pieces.

- Glue the two back cross pieces.
- Fold and glue together the base front.
- Glue the base front into place.

## PROCESS: [Final Assembly for Galaxy]

- Assemble and glue the two back cross pieces.
- Fit the horn holder using the grey areas for alignment.
- Glue the two back cross pieces.
- Fold and glue together the base front.
- Glue the base front into place.

## OUTPUT:
- The completed Phono-Horn model ready for use.

## PROCESS: [Usage]
- Place the iPhone or Galaxy on the stand.
- Align the loudspeaker with the hole in the horn holder.

## OUTPUT:
- Enhanced sound quality when playing audio through the Phono-Horn.

## END:
- The assembly and usage of the Phono-Horn are complete.
```

instruct00040.title: Make a Super PaperJet and Fly Over a 5-story Building
instruct00040.text: The Super PaperJet is a paper airplane that can fly over a 5-story building. It's launched with a rubber band.The construction is really simple, you just need:- A sheet of paper (letter or A4 size)- A knife and cutting board (or scissors)- A rubber bandLet's get started! Start by folding the sheet of paper in half width-wise, and cut it in two pieces. We just need one of them. Open the paper back up and fold the top two corners inward. Keeping a little gap where they meet along the crease will help the folding later and keep the paper layers flat. Fold both sides so the corners meet again in the center line. Repeat the folding of both sides to the center line. This starts looking like a very fast jet! To shape the wings keep the plane folded along the crease, and fold along a line parallel to the bottom edge of the plane. To cut the anchor where the rubber band will hook into, I'd recommend using a knife. You can use scissors too, you just need to be careful so the to cuts meet in one sharp point, otherwise the rubber band may get stuck in it. Choosing the right rubber is key to get your Super PaperJet fly very far. For maximum reach, we want the rubber band to be long, with good stretch and strength. Try stretching the rubber band - if it returns to the same length that's good, if it becomes longer after the stretch that's not good.You can also use a longer rubber band, e.g. from a file folder. That's what I was using at school and I was close to reach the length of a soccer field! You can experiment with this, but that's my choice on using the rubber band: - Create a triangle with the pinkie, the index finger and the thumb.- Stretch the rubber band from the pinkie.- Pass the rubber band around the index finger and the thumb.This way there is not rubber on the way of the plane, and all the length and strength of the rubber band is on the plane side. Find an open space for the test launch so you get a sense of how fast and far this plane can go - a park, a baseball field, etc.If you think you've got a Super PaperJet that can beat the record, make a video and post it to the comments!

```markdown
# Super PaperJet Construction and Launch System

## START:
- Begin the process of constructing and launching the Super PaperJet.

## INPUT: Gather Materials
- Sheet of paper (letter or A4 size)
- Knife and cutting board (or scissors)
- Rubber band

## PROCESS: Prepare Paper
- Fold the sheet of paper in half width-wise.

## PROCESS: Cut Paper
- Cut the folded paper into two pieces using a knife and cutting board or scissors.

## DECISION [IF]: Is there more than one piece of paper?
  - Yes: Proceed with one piece.
  - No: END.

## PROCESS: Initial Folds
- Open the chosen piece of paper.
- Fold the top two corners inward, creating a small gap at the crease.

## PROCESS: Additional Folds
- Fold both sides so the corners meet again at the center line.
- Repeat the folding of both sides to the center line.

## PROCESS: Shape the Wings
- Keep the plane folded along the crease.
- Fold along a line parallel to the bottom edge of the plane to form the wings.

## PROCESS: Cut the Anchor
- Use a knife or scissors to cut the anchor for the rubber band.
- Ensure the cuts meet at a sharp point to avoid the rubber band getting stuck.

## INPUT: Select Rubber Band
- Choose a long rubber band with good stretch and strength.

## DECISION [IF]: Does the rubber band return to original length after stretching?
  - Yes: Good rubber band.
  - No: Find another rubber band.

## PROCESS: Rubber Band Setup
- Create a triangle with the pinkie, index finger, and thumb.
- Stretch the rubber band from the pinkie.
- Pass the rubber band around the index finger and thumb, ensuring no rubber interferes with the plane.

## INPUT: Find Launch Space
- Locate an open space for test launching the Super PaperJet (e.g., park, baseball field).

## PROCESS: Test Launch
- Launch the Super PaperJet using the rubber band setup to test its performance.

## OUTPUT: Assess Flight
- Observe the distance and speed of the Super PaperJet.

## DECISION [IF]: Does the Super PaperJet perform well?
  - Yes: Proceed to record a video.
  - No: Adjust the construction or rubber band setup and retest.

## PROCESS: Record and Share
- Record a video of the Super PaperJet if it beats personal records.
- Share the video in the comments for others to see.

## END.
```

instruct00369.text: One of my go to orders at Panera has always been the Mediterranean Veggie Sandwich. It's full of zesty flavor and with all the vegetables, it's one of the healthier options on the menu. The lettuce and cucumbers give this sandwich a great crunch, while the creamy hummus and feta add so much flavor. I really hope you enjoy this Instructable, and let me know if you try it out for yourself!- Carolyn Copycat Panera Mediterranean Veggie Sandwich IngredientsMakes 1 Sandwich2 Slices of Tomato Basil Bread (You can buy a loaf from Panera directly, if you are lucky enough to live near one, or you can check your local supermarket for Panera brand bread. I found mine at Stop and Shop!)Hummus, choice of flavor (Panera uses a cilantro/jalapeno blend, but I don't like too much heat, so I use regular classic hummus)Tomato, slicedCucumber, slicedRed Onion, slicedLettuceCrumbled Feta CheeseRoasted Peppers (Panera uses Peppadew Peppers, which is a specific brand, not type. I couldn't find them at the store, so I am using roasted red peppers. They work great in this sandwich! 1. Take 2 slices of the Tomato Basil bread and smear each with the hummus of your choice.2. On of piece of bread, add lettuce and sliced tomatoes. 3. On the other piece of bread, add sliced cucumbers and red onions.4. Add the feta cheese and peppers on top of the onions. 5. Press the two sides together, stick a toothpicks in to keep everything together, slice down the middle.6. Enjoy!

instruct00170.title: Easy Way to Smooth PLA | No Sanding
instruct00170.text: First of all, Thank you for checking out my tutorial! You are awesome.Second, I put a lot of time into the YouTube video so watch it too, it explains it all.So currently, there is no easily accessible chemical to smooth PLA the same way acetone does to ABS.But here I will show you how I fill in the layered build lines.Video: You will need:A 3D printed model with visible layer lines.Any can of spray paint that bonds well to plastic.Fast Drying Polyurethane - Clear Satin.If you like this skull you can download it here: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:2951822Do read and follow all safety warnings on all spray cans and 3D printers. First clean the model of any dust and make sure it's clean.Next spray the model with your selected color of spray paint. Then quickly spray a layer of Polyurethane.Then place it under a fan to prevent drips and to make dry faster.The paint and Polyurethane will mix and fill the layers, any holes, and printed flaws.The thinner each layers and the longer you let each layer dry the better. I waited 20 minutes between layers and then waited an entire day before spraying the final coat of spray paint to cover any discoloration. And that's really it! I like this method because you can print in larger layer lines without worrying and it will print much faster,you can print in any color and paint the final color you want, it doesn't need sanding, it can fill holes or flaws, and its pretty easy to do.Note: I did print the skull at a layer height of 0.3 which means detail was lost during printing. A height 0.1 would have been better and taken less time to smooth but I needed an extreme layer height to show how much this method can do!The final result looks much cleaner and more professional. People wont believe it's 3D printed!Feel free to check out my YouTube channel - 3DSage. I create lots of different and fun videos!Thank you and see you next time!www.youtube.com/c/3dsage

```markdown
# Summary Representation of PLA Smoothing Blog Post

## START:
- Begin the process of smoothing PLA 3D-printed models.

## INPUT:
- A 3D printed model with visible layer lines.
- A can of spray paint that bonds well to plastic.
- Fast Drying Polyurethane - Clear Satin.
- Access to a fan.

## PROCESS: Clean the Model
- Clean the model thoroughly to remove any dust and ensure it's clean.

## PROCESS: Apply Spray Paint
- Spray the model with the selected color of spray paint.

## PROCESS: Apply Polyurethane
- Quickly spray a layer of Polyurethane over the painted model.

## PROCESS: Drying
- Place the model under a fan to prevent drips and to facilitate faster drying.

## DECISION [IF]: Is the paint and Polyurethane mixture filling in the layers and flaws?
  - Yes: Proceed to the next layer application.
  - No: Reapply spray paint and Polyurethane as needed.

## PROCESS: Apply Additional Layers
- Apply thin layers, allowing 20 minutes of drying time between each layer.

## PROCESS: Final Drying Time
- After the last layer, wait an entire day before applying the final coat of spray paint.

## DECISION [IF]: Has the final coat been applied to cover any discoloration?
  - Yes: Proceed to the final result evaluation.
  - No: Apply the final coat of spray paint.

## OUTPUT:
- The final result is a smooth, professional-looking 3D-printed model.

## END:
- The PLA smoothing process is complete.

## STORE/DATABASE SUBROUTINE:
- If desired, download the skull model from Thingiverse for practice (https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:2951822).
- Follow all safety warnings on spray cans and 3D printers.
- Note that printing at a higher layer height (e.g., 0.3) will lose detail but show the effectiveness of the smoothing method.

## OUTPUT:
- Viewers are encouraged to check out the 3DSage YouTube channel for more videos and tutorials.

## END:
- The tutorial and encouragement to visit the YouTube channel conclude the summary.
```

instruct00863.title: Mini Wave Model
instruct00863.text: A little wave goes a long way! The mini wave model is small but mighty. With just a few minutes of set-up, it's just as good at demonstrating as its bigger siblings. This is a great model for waves that move, reflect, stand, and wiggle, perfect for a starter project in classrooms learning about waves and motion. What: Mini Wave ModelConcepts: waves, propagation, physicsTime: ~15 minutes to set upCost: ~$1.50Materials:Bolts x 2 (with nuts that fit)Nuts x 40 (or so)Sticks (I used candy sticks, but cut dowel or other sticks work great, too)StringBlock of wood (2x4 works great) Tools:DrillHot glue gun / hot glueRulerScissorsMakeHop on the wave! Let's dive in! Grab a drill bit that's a little narrower than your bolt, and drill halfway through your block of wood. Add a nut and twist it in. Repeat on the other side, too. If you want, you can add to posts on each side that are evenly spread apart. This can make the finished wave model a little more stable if you're having trouble with it. Starting with one post, tie your string, wrap around the other, and tie back to that original post. You want it about as tight as you can manage without needing to strain. Cut off the extra bit and add a little hot glue to keep all ends in place. Make the world's smallest weight set!Start by lining up your sticks, and marking the center of each one. You can do this quickly down a line once you got them all lined up. Add a nut to either end of each of your sticks. Add a little hot glue to each and repeat for your entire line. The weights will help the wave's momentum and propagation. Choose a spacing for your dumbbells, and mark your string accordingly. I marked every 1/2" but decided to glue dumbbells every inch along the way. Apply glue to both strings and place the dumbbell over to fit snugly. When you reached the line, it's time to give a wave! Your wave model is ready for action! Here are some things to try and notice: Tapping - give a light tap to different sticks. What's the difference between a tap in the middle and on the end. Reflection - watch a wave as it gets to the end and comes back. Which way does it go? Does it wave the same way as on the way there?Standing Waves - take a stick and wave it back and forth trying to get in beat with its reflected self. You can create nodes that move only small amounts.There is so much more to learn about waves! For a quick primer, try this out. If you want to mega-size this project, you can try out the GIANT wave model, too! Have fun, wave on, and keep exploring.

```markdown
# Mini Wave Model System Summary

## START:
- Begin the process of constructing a mini wave model.

## INPUT: Materials and Tools
- Bolts x 2 (with nuts that fit)
- Nuts x 40 (or so)
- Sticks (candy sticks or similar)
- String
- Block of wood (e.g., 2x4)
- Drill
- Hot glue gun / hot glue
- Ruler
- Scissors

## PROCESS: Preparing the Block of Wood
1. Select a drill bit slightly narrower than the bolts.
2. Drill halfway through the block of wood at two points.

## DECISION [IF]: Are additional stability posts needed?
- Yes: Add two stability posts evenly spread apart on the block of wood.
- No: Continue to the next step.

## PROCESS: Setting Up the String
1. Tie one end of the string to one bolt/post.
2. Wrap the string around the other bolt/post.
3. Tie the string back to the first bolt/post, making it as tight as possible without straining.
4. Trim the excess string and secure the ends with hot glue.

## PROCESS: Creating Weights
1. Line up the sticks and mark the center of each.
2. Attach a nut to each end of the sticks using hot glue.
3. Repeat until all sticks have nuts glued on both ends.

## PROCESS: Attaching Weights to String
1. Decide on spacing for the weights on the string (e.g., every inch).
2. Mark the string accordingly.
3. Apply hot glue to the string at each mark.
4. Attach the weighted sticks (dumbbells) to the string at the marked intervals.

## OUTPUT:
- Completion of the mini wave model assembly.

## PROCESS: Experimenting with the Wave Model
1. Tap different sticks to observe wave propagation.
2. Observe wave reflection at the ends of the model.
3. Try to create standing waves by moving a stick in sync with its reflection.

## END:
- The system outputs a functional mini wave model ready for wave demonstrations and experiments.
```

instruct00134.title: Pallet Table
instruct00134.text: This instructable will show you how you can make a table out of old pallets First you need to get pallets Next gather up supplies-2 hammers -drill-saw -screw, nails-drill bits -sander-tape measure -level - pencil Tear down the pallets so you have individual boards. Don't get to aggressive or you will split the boards Before they come off Lay you boards out so you know the pattern you want the table to be and cut them to fit ***i also added a picture of another table I made showin the pattern on it so you can get different ideas Then cut the bottom side frame boards of the table and I found it is easier to sand these down while they are still apart( sand with rough grit, then fine grit, then extra fine fine grit) after cuttin and sanding them, screw them together and start puttin the table pieces on there. I put other pieces of pallet underside of the table to eliminate screws on the top side of the table. You could also spend a little more money and cut a piece of plywood and put the pallet boards on top of that but I didn't want to spend the extra money. once you have the table screwed together it is time to sand the pallet boards down. Top,bottom, and sides (rough, fine, extra fine grit) make sure it is smooth all over and you can rub you hand everywhere and not get splinters ***when puttin in screws, drill a pilot hole first to avoid splitting wood *** rough grit=60 grit Fine grit =120 grit Extra fine=220 grit Now it's time to install legs for the table. First, figure out how high you want it. In this case the lady wanted the table a little taller than her counters so I made it a little more than 3 foot tall. Then cut the legs, put it supports on the bottom to add stability. And finally make sure it is level and doesn't wobble. If it wobbles find the legs that are to long and make small cuts on them to even them out.( the cuts might only be 1/8 and inch being cut) I found it's easier to sand the leg pieces individually to before assembling them Now that the table is assembled and sanded down its time for stain! I choose a light color stain to match the persons counter tops. Put a coat of stain on the whole table make sure you don't put to much or it will make run marks. And then let dry. After it has dried you can sand it down with some 320 grit sand paper and put on a second coat( each time you add a coat it makes the color a little darker and richer looking) once you finish staining the table is complete! Have fun! Vote for contest!

```markdown
## START:
- Begin the process of creating a table from old pallets.

## PROCESS: Dismantling the Pallets

- Cut the boards to fit the chosen pattern.

## PROCESS: Preparing the Bottom Frame
- Cut the bottom side frame boards for the table.
- Sand down each board with rough, fine, and extra fine grit in sequence.

## PROCESS: Assemble the Bottom Frame
- Screw the bottom frame boards together.

## PROCESS: Tabletop Assembly
- Begin attaching the table pieces to the bottom frame.
  - DECISION [IF]: Do you want to avoid screws on the top side?

## PROCESS: Sanding the Tabletop
- Sand down the pallet boards on top, bottom, and sides with rough, fine, and extra fine grit.

## PROCESS: Preparing for Legs Installation
- Determine the desired table height.
- Cut the legs to the appropriate length.
- Add supports on the bottom for stability.
- Ensure the table is level and does not wobble.

## PROCESS: Sanding the Legs
- Sand down each leg piece with rough, fine, and extra fine grit before assembly.

- Choose a stain color to match the desired aesthetic.
- Apply the first coat of stain to the table.

## PROCESS: Apply Additional Stain Coats
- After drying, lightly sand with 320 grit sandpaper.
- Apply a second coat of stain for a darker, richer color.

## OUTPUT: Completion of the Table
- The stained table is now complete.

- The table-making process is finished.
```

instruct00455.title: Ultimate Step by Step Sprouting Guide
instruct00455.text: This is the ultimate step by step guide to sprouting, seeds, legumes, grains and nuts all year round. Sprouts are nutritional powerhouses and are delicious, fresh and very versatile. Sprouting is so super easy, requires minimal equipment and they will add a great crunch and new dimension to all of your dishes. You can then use your sprouts on everything from, salads and toast to tacos and sandwiches. The possibilities are endless once you start sprouting. Read on to discover the simple step by step guide to growing sprouts at home as well as a "sprouting chart", detailing a large list of seeds, legumes, grains and nuts you can sprout as well as soaking and growing times for each. STEP 1 SOAKIn a glass sprouting jar or a mason jar (with cheesecloth and an elastic on the top). Place your seeds, grains, nuts or legumes in your jar and cover completely with water. The exact measurement of water is not essential here as this is just for soaking purposes.Let the nuts, seeds, grains or legumes soak for the allocated time (refer to the sprouting guide in this link http://www.lapetitepoire.com/en/ultimate-step-step-guide-sprouting ). These times vary amongst the different types of nuts, seeds, grains or legumes used. STEP 2 RINSEAfter you have reached the necessary soaking time, its time to thoroughly rinse them. Rinse under running water until the water is running clear. Make sure you fill your jar with clean, fresh water. Then tip it up at a 45 degree angle or lean your jar against something and let the water filter out. The reason I use a sprouting jar is that they are simple and fast to use as they come with a mesh lid and a stand to tilt it up to drain. STEP 3 RINSE, RINSE, RINSE..SPROUTNow once again refer to my sprouting guide (follow the link below) as to approximately how long it will take before you have edible sprouts. Now all that is needed is to rinse and drain your seeds, nuts, grains or legumes twice a day until they have sprouted!http://www.lapetitepoire.com/en/ultimate-step-step-guide-sprouting/ STEP 4 GROW You will know when your sprouts are ready as they will develop a small tail or they have sprouted into green little sprouts! Again this is in the sprouting guide in the link below it will tell you what you need to look out for depending on what you are sprouting.http://www.lapetitepoire.com/en/ultimate-step-step-guide-sprouting/ STEP 5 EAT & STORAGEI keep my new sprouts in glass jars in the fridge. They will generally keep for 3 4 days. Use them on all salads, toast, in tacos or on their own as a snack. The possibilities are endless with these little vitamin packed wonders!!!!!

```markdown
# Ultimate Step-by-Step Guide to Sprouting

## START:
### Step 1: Preparation for Sprouting
- **INPUT**: Obtain seeds, grains, nuts, or legumes for sprouting.
- **INPUT**: Have a glass sprouting jar or a mason jar with cheesecloth and elastic ready.

### Step 2: Soaking
- **PROCESS**: Place the selected seeds, grains, nuts, or legumes into the jar.
- **PROCESS**: Cover completely with water. The exact measurement of water is not critical.
- **PROCESS**: Refer to the sprouting guide for specific soaking times. [Sprouting Guide Link](http://www.lapetitepoire.com/en/ultimate-step-step-guide-sprouting)
- **OUTPUT**: Soaked seeds, grains, nuts, or legumes ready for rinsing.

## PROCESS:
### Step 3: Rinsing After Soaking
- **PROCESS**: After the soaking time is up, rinse under running water until clear.
- **PROCESS**: Fill the jar with clean water and then drain by tipping the jar at a 45-degree angle or by leaning it against something.

### DECISION [IF]: Is a sprouting jar with a mesh lid and stand being used?
- **Yes**: Proceed with the draining as the jar is designed for this purpose.
- **No**: Ensure the cheesecloth is secured and properly allows water to drain without losing contents.

### Step 4: Rinse, Rinse, Rinse... Sprout
- **PROCESS**: Continue to rinse and drain the seeds, nuts, grains, or legumes twice a day.
- **PROCESS**: Refer back to the sprouting guide for the estimated time until the sprouts are edible. [Sprouting Guide Link](http://www.lapetitepoire.com/en/ultimate-step-step-guide-sprouting)

### Step 5: Growth Monitoring
- **DECISION [IF]**: Have the sprouts developed a small tail or turned into green little sprouts?
  - **Yes**: Move to the next step.
  - **No**: Continue the rinse and drain process twice a day.

## OUTPUT:
### Step 6: Harvesting
- **PROCESS**: Once sprouts are ready, stop the rinsing process.
- **STORE**: Keep the sprouts in glass jars in the refrigerator.

### Step 7: Storage and Usage
- **PROCESS**: Sprouts will generally keep for 3-4 days in the fridge.
- **OUTPUT**: Use the sprouts in various dishes such as salads, toast, tacos, or as a snack.

## END:
### Step 8: Enjoy Your Sprouts
- **OUTPUT**: Enjoy the vitamin-packed sprouts in your meals.
```

instruct00468.title: Adjustable Glass Bottle Cutter
instruct00468.text: I have wanting to make a bottle cutter for a while now, just because I really like the idea of making glasses from bottles. I found a lot of designs online, but one thing they all had in common, is that none of them are adjustable. Now I want to be able to cut different types and sizes of bottles, so I came up with this design that can be adjusted for different bottles. Cutting glass bottles can be really fun, and drinking out of a glass you made is also satisfying. Plus you get to repurpose an ordinary glass bottle into something new and useful. For this project I used:- 1x4 Scraps- Glass Cutter- Polyurethane- 1/4"x2" Bolts- Wing Nuts- Epoxy- Wood Glue- Screws- Glass Bottles After I decided how I was going to build it, I cut out the pieces and sanded them. I joined up the corners by adding some wood glue, then driving in some screws. I began by drilling the two holes the size of the bolts on the sliding block. Then I put the block in place at each of the furthest ends and used the same drill bit through the original holes to make marks. I then drilled the rest of the holes through and drew lines connecting them for the slots. I used the jigsaw to cut out the slots along the lines. Since I would only be needing part of the glass cutter, I used the Dremel to cut off the part I would need. I cleaned that up with a file and sanding block, so it looked better. Then I lined it up on the side of the board with a bottle, so I could find out where it should go. I finished it with some more sanding, I used some files to sand in the slots. I glued the bolts into the holes in the sliding block with epoxy. Finally, I tested the sliding block with the wing nuts, and screwed on the glass cutter. Also this glass cutter can be adjusted too, by screwing it into a different spot. At this point, I decided to give the cutter a try. First I adjusted the sliding wall to where I wanted the cut, and scored the cut on the glass. Next I heated up some water just to boiling, and slowly poured it over the score for about 30 seconds. Next, I quickly switched to cold water over the score for about the same time. Lastly, I slightly twisted the bottle, and it popped apart. I smoothed the cut up using some sandpaper and Dremel. Now that I have finished and tested it I decided to give it a polyurethane finish. This is actually the first time I have used polyurethane, so I wanted something to give it a try on. When it was dry, I put all the parts back on and I was done. I also added a set of rubber feet on the bottom for traction and stability. Cutting bottles actually turned out even more fun and easy than I thought it would be. It's and interesting process, and very satisfying when the bottle pops in half in your hands. So far I have only broken a few bottles in the process, and I am looking forward to cutting many more bottles in the future. By the way something I noticed, almost all the colored bottles(green, brown) I have tried to cut have broken, opposed to all of my clear bottles have been a success. Maybe the colored ones are made cheaper, or the clear ones are thicker glass, I don't know. Hope you enjoyed and have fun cutting bottles! REMEMBER TO BE SAFE, GLASS CAN BE VERY DANGEROUS.

```markdown
# Comprehensive Summary of DIY Adjustable Bottle Cutter Blog Post

## System Overview:
The system described in the blog post is an adjustable bottle cutter designed for cutting various types and sizes of glass bottles to repurpose them into new items, such as drinking glasses. The system is manually operated and involves a construction process followed by a cutting process. The construction process includes preparing materials, assembling the cutter, and applying a finish. The cutting process involves scoring, heating, and cooling the bottle to make a clean cut.

## Materials and Tools Input:
- 1x4 Scraps
- Glass Cutter
- Polyurethane
- 1/4"x2" Bolts
- Wing Nuts
- Epoxy
- Wood Glue
- Screws
- Glass Bottles
- Tools: Saw, Drill, Jigsaw, Dremel, File, Sanding Block, Sandpaper

## Construction Process:
START:
- Cut and sand 1x4 scraps to desired dimensions for the cutter base and sliding block.

PROCESS: Joining the Base
- Apply wood glue to join corners of the base.
- Use screws to secure the corners.

PROCESS: Preparing the Sliding Block
- Drill two holes in the sliding block for the bolts.
- Place the block at the ends of the base and mark drill points through the holes.
- Drill holes through the base to match the sliding block.

PROCESS: Creating Slots for Adjustment
- Draw lines connecting the drilled holes on the base.
- Use a jigsaw to cut out the slots along the lines.

PROCESS: Preparing Glass Cutter
- Use a Dremel to cut the necessary part of the glass cutter.
- Clean up the cut portion with a file and sanding block.
- Align the glass cutter on the side of the base with a bottle to determine placement.

PROCESS: Final Assembly
- Sand the base and slots for a smooth finish.
- Glue the bolts into the sliding block using epoxy.
- Attach the sliding block with wing nuts.
- Screw the glass cutter onto the base.

PROCESS: Applying Finish
- Apply polyurethane to the cutter for protection.
- Allow the finish to dry.

OUTPUT: Completed Adjustable Bottle Cutter

END: Construction Process Completed

## Cutting Process:
START:
- Adjust the sliding wall to the desired cut position on the bottle.

PROCESS: Scoring the Bottle
- Use the glass cutter to score the bottle where the cut is desired.

PROCESS: Heating and Cooling
- Heat water to boiling and pour it over the score line for 30 seconds.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the hot water applied for 30 seconds?
  - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
  - No: Continue applying hot water until 30 seconds are reached.
- Quickly switch to pouring cold water over the score line for 30 seconds.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the cold water applied for 30 seconds?
  - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
  - No: Continue applying cold water until 30 seconds are reached.

PROCESS: Separating the Bottle
- Twist the bottle gently to pop it apart along the score line.

PROCESS: Smoothing the Edge
- Use sandpaper and a Dremel to smooth the cut edge of the bottle.

OUTPUT: Cut and Smoothed Glass Bottle

END: Cutting Process Completed

## Observations and Additional Steps:
- Colored bottles often break during cutting, while clear bottles tend to cut successfully.
- Safety precautions are emphasized due to the dangers of working with glass.

## Final Touches:
- Reassemble the cutter if disassembled during the cutting process.
- Add rubber feet to the bottom of the cutter for traction and stability.

END: System Ready for Future Use
```

instruct00306.title: TYE-DYE Made With Sharpies
instruct00306.text: Tye-dye is often messy, but neat to look at. Why should you have to deal with the mess when you can do with a few cool sharpies, some rubbing alcohol, and of course something to tie-dye. It takes about 15 minutes to make, and another 15 or so to dry. For this craft you will need at least two sharpies (they come in a LOT of cool colors now), a lot of rubber bands, a couple of tennis balls or a few ping-pong balls, a spray bottle set on fine mist with alcohol, and of course something to tie-die, preferably bandanna or a T-shirt. Take the bandanna, tennis\ping-pong balls, and rubber bands. By the way to have one ring use one tennis ball, if you want two rings use two tennis balls and so on. If you are planning to use more than three balls, I would recommend ping-bong balls. Put the ball(s) in the middle if you are using one, or put the balls at least two inches apart. Then grab the fabric around the ball and tie the rubber band really close to the ball, if there is enough room put more rubber bands every two inches or so. If there are more balls do the same thing to them. Choose a sharpie. Color a/the ball. Then color the piece of fabric on the opposite side of the rubber band with a different color. And so on. Make sure when you color you don't have the same color on the opposite sides of the rubber band. Take the mister with the rubbing alcohol in it. Hold it by the ends of the fabric. Spray the bandanna. Make sure you spray the whole thing. If you don't it won't look lie tie-dye. Finally, let it dry naturally, until completely dry. Here is an example of a bandanna that I did.

```markdown
# Sharpie Tie-Dye System Summary

## System Overview:
The Sharpie Tie-Dye system is a process that allows one to create tie-dye patterns on fabric using Sharpies, rubber bands, balls (tennis or ping-pong), and rubbing alcohol. The system requires setting up the fabric with balls and rubber bands, coloring with Sharpies, applying alcohol, and allowing the fabric to dry. This process is designed to be less messy than traditional tie-dye methods.

### Process Steps:

#### START:
- Begin the Sharpie Tie-Dye process.

#### INPUT:
- Gather materials:
  - At least two different colored Sharpies.
  - A lot of rubber bands.
  - A couple of tennis balls or a few ping-pong balls (depending on the number of rings desired).
  - A spray bottle filled with rubbing alcohol, set to a fine mist.
  - A fabric item to tie-dye (bandanna or T-shirt).

#### PROCESS: Prepare the Fabric
- Place the ball(s) in the center or at least two inches apart on the fabric.
- Grab the fabric around each ball and secure it with a rubber band close to the ball.
- Add additional rubber bands every two inches if there is enough room.

#### PROCESS: Color the Fabric
- Choose a Sharpie color to start with.
- Color the fabric around a ball and the fabric on the opposite side of a rubber band with different colors.
- Repeat the coloring process, ensuring not to have the same color on opposite sides of the rubber bands.

#### PROCESS: Apply Rubbing Alcohol
- Hold the fabric by the ends.
- Use the spray bottle to mist the fabric with rubbing alcohol, covering the entire item to ensure a tie-dye effect.

#### DECISION [IF]: Is the fabric thoroughly sprayed?
- Yes: Proceed to the drying step.
- No: Continue spraying until the fabric is fully covered.

#### PROCESS: Dry the Fabric
- Let the fabric dry naturally until it is completely dry.

#### OUTPUT:
- The final output is a tie-dyed fabric item with a unique pattern created by the Sharpie and alcohol technique.

#### END:
- The Sharpie Tie-Dye process is complete.
```

instruct00104.title: Cookie Dough Frosting
instruct00104.text: This is a different take on my edible cookie dough recipe - cookie dough frosting! This recipe makes enough frosting for 24 cupcakes, so you'll be very popular after you make it. :DThese cookie dough frosted cupcakes were gone in about a minute when I made them and shared them with the office here at Instructables... so I think I can safely say they're DELICIOUS. 1/2 cup unsalted butter, room temp3/4 cup packed light brown sugar 1 teaspoon vanilla extract 1 cup + 2 tablespoons all purpose flour1/2 teaspoon salt 1/4 cup milk 1 cup mini chocolate chipsYou can use dark brown sugar as well - just whatever you've got on hand!Any type of milk works too - soy, nut, or regular.I recommend using cupcake liners so when you frost you don't manhandle the cupcakes too much. P.S. I just used box cake mix for the cupcakes - Duncan Hines devil's food mix tastes great without the extra work of making them yourself. :D Add the softened butter and brown sugar into a large bowl and cream with a hand mixer. It should lighten in color and be nice and fluffy when you're done. Add in the flour and salt and mix well. The mixture will be very crumbly at first, so don't worry. Once you have a nice crumb, pour in the milk and vanilla slowly while mixing on low speed. This will give you a lovely creamy frosting. If the frosting seems thick, feel free to add a little extra milk! Just don't go overboard because you want it have a little stiffness for easier frosting. Mix in the mini chocolate chips using a spatula. To frost, scoop between 1-2 tablespoons onto each cupcake and use a spatula to press it down into place. Because it's a chunky frosting, you can't really smooth it out, so try to pile it high instead of worrying about a smooth top. This frosting is best stored in the fridge, so make sure to pop your cupcakes in there if they don't all get eaten immediately. ;)
