```markdown
# Cookie Dough Frosting Recipe System

## Summary:
This system details the process of making cookie dough frosting sufficient for 24 cupcakes. It includes creaming butter and sugar, adding dry ingredients, incorporating milk and vanilla for creaminess, and adding chocolate chips. The frosting is applied to cupcakes and is best stored in the refrigerator.

## Process Steps:

START:
- Begin the cookie dough frosting preparation process.

INPUT: Gather Ingredients
- 1/2 cup unsalted butter, room temperature
- 3/4 cup packed light brown sugar (dark brown sugar is an acceptable alternative)
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 1 cup + 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 cup milk (any type, including soy, nut, or regular)
- 1 cup mini chocolate chips
- Cupcake liners (recommended for ease of frosting)
- Prepared cupcakes (suggestion: Duncan Hines devil's food mix)

PROCESS: Cream Butter and Sugar
- Add the softened unsalted butter and brown sugar into a large bowl.
- Use a hand mixer to cream the butter and brown sugar until the mixture is light in color and fluffy.

PROCESS: Add Dry Ingredients
- Add the all-purpose flour and salt to the creamed butter and sugar.
- Mix well until the mixture becomes crumbly.

PROCESS: Incorporate Milk and Vanilla
- Pour in the milk and vanilla extract slowly while mixing on low speed.
- Continue to mix until a creamy frosting texture is achieved.

DECISION [IF]: Is the frosting too thick?
- IF Yes: Add a little extra milk to adjust consistency.
- IF No: Proceed to the next step.

PROCESS: Mix in Chocolate Chips
- Use a spatula to fold in the mini chocolate chips into the frosting.

PROCESS: Frost the Cupcakes
- Scoop between 1-2 tablespoons of the frosting onto each cupcake.
- Use a spatula to press the frosting down into place, piling it high rather than smoothing it out.

OUTPUT: Cookie Dough Frosted Cupcakes
- The final product is cupcakes topped with cookie dough frosting.

DECISION [IF]: Are there any leftover frosted cupcakes?
- IF Yes: Store the cupcakes in the refrigerator.
- IF No: End the process as the cupcakes are served immediately.

END:
- The cookie dough frosting preparation process is complete.
```

instruct00636.title: The Single Most Effective Way to Get Rid of a Sunburn
instruct00636.text: This is my first instructable, and is only going to be short because its an extremely easy and effective method to removing a painful sunburn. This method was recommended to me by my friends mother, who is a nurse. I hope this helps many a painful sunburn to recede or disappear quickly.EDIT: 6/26/16As this instructable has seen over 6mm views since I first published it, I've decided to edit it for more clarity & for safety concerns. You will need a total of six things. A bathtub to do this in (preferably ceramic, so it wont stain) A pitcher A rag that you don't mind getting stained Water Three bags of black tea (I use Earl Grey)Ice First things first, strip down, because you don't want to get any of your clothes wet. Fill the pitcher with lukewarm water and soak the tea bags in it - the water should be just warm enough to help the tea brew. When you have the water almost black, like the picture, then move on to step 3.DO NOT use hot water! As a sunburn is a first degree burn, adding more heat to a burn will exacerbate the effects and cause further damage to your skin. Use only lukewarm water at most. Once the water has cooled to a warm/lukewarm temperature (add your ice now to speed this)Dunk the rag into the tea, and dab it onto the sunburn. Do not wipe it off! Leave it on and let it be absorbed into your skin. Once its dry, re-apply as necessary, but never wash it off. If you do this process before bedtime, you can go to sleep and give it time to work its magic. In the morning you can wash it off in your shower. Hopefully, your sunburn will be substantially subdued, but remember: the sooner you can apply the tea after you get the burn, the quicker and more effective it will be.Note: I had a severe sunburn and I also used the tea bags straight up, dabbing them directly onto my skin. You may use as many "coats" of tea as you want, but the more the better.

```markdown
# Sunburn Relief Using Black Tea

## Summary Representation of the Process

### START:
- Begin the process to relieve sunburn using black tea.

### INPUT:
- Gather the following items:
  - A bathtub (preferably ceramic to avoid staining)
  - A pitcher
  - A rag (one that you don't mind getting stained)
  - Water
  - Three bags of black tea (e.g., Earl Grey)
  - Ice

### PROCESS: [Prepare for Treatment]
- Strip down to avoid getting clothes wet.

### PROCESS: [Prepare Tea Solution]
- Fill the pitcher with lukewarm water.
- Soak the three bags of black tea in the water.

### DECISION [IF]: [Is the water almost black?]
  - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
  - No: Continue steeping the tea bags until the desired color is achieved.

### PROCESS: [Cool the Tea Solution]
- Once the tea is almost black, begin cooling the water to warm/lukewarm temperature.
- Add ice to speed up the cooling process if necessary.

### PROCESS: [Apply Tea to Sunburn]
- Dunk the rag into the tea solution.
- Dab the tea-soaked rag onto the sunburned skin.
  - Do not wipe off the tea; allow it to be absorbed.

### DECISION [IF]: [Is the tea dry on the skin?]
  - Yes: Re-apply tea as necessary.
  - No: Wait until the tea has dried before deciding to reapply.

### PROCESS: [Allow Tea to Work]
- If this process is done before bedtime, leave the tea on the skin overnight.

### OUTPUT:
- Expectation that the sunburn will be substantially subdued by morning.

### PROCESS: [Wash Off Tea]
- In the morning, wash off the tea during a shower.

### PROCESS: [Additional Application for Severe Sunburn]
- If the sunburn is severe, consider dabbing the tea bags directly onto the skin for additional relief.
- Apply as many "coats" of tea as desired, with more coats potentially offering better results.

### END:
- Complete the sunburn relief process.
```

instruct00195.title: DIY Decorative Shell Dresser Knobs
instruct00195.text: A quick way to revamp an old dresser is to change out the knobs for some new decorative ones. Here's an easy and budget-friendly way to make your very own DIY dresser knobs using shells perfect if you're looking to add a little bit of the beach to your decor. What you'll need: shells (I got mine from the Dollar Store), nuts & washers, bolts (about 1 to 1.5 inches longer than the thickness of the shell), scrap rigid cardboard, rubber bands and epoxy glue. Cut a piece of rigid cardboard so that it's the width of the shell and extends past it by about an inch, and make a hole in the middle. It will act as the flat surface of the dresser drawer to set the bolt in place. Insert the bolt in the hole of the cardboard Pour epoxy glue into the shell cavity, making sure to have enough glue to cover the head of the bolt. Place the head of the bolt so that it touches the bottom of the shell cavity, while making sure the cardboard is flush to the back of the shell. Then move the bolt around so it is perpendicular to the cardboard. When the bolt is placed properly, use a rubber band to secure the cardboard in place, double check that the bolt is still touching the bottom of the shell cavity and still straight (it doesn't have to be perfect but the straighter the better), then place the cardboard on the edge of 2 glasses. This will allow the epoxy to settle on the bottom and cover the head of the bolt. Let the epoxy harden. And voila, you have beautiful shell knobs ready to give a new look to your dresser!

```markdown
# DIY Dresser Knobs Using Shells

## System Overview
The following system represents the process of creating DIY dresser knobs using shells. The process involves preparing materials, setting up the assembly, applying epoxy glue, and attaching the knobs to the dresser.

### Required Materials
- Shells
- Nuts & Washers
- Bolts (1 to 1.5 inches longer than the thickness of the shell)
- Scrap Rigid Cardboard
- Rubber Bands
- Epoxy Glue

### Process Steps

#### START: Begin DIY Dresser Knobs Creation

#### PROCESS: Gather Materials
1. INPUT: Acquire shells, nuts & washers, bolts, rigid cardboard, rubber bands, and epoxy glue.

#### PROCESS: Prepare Cardboard Base
2. PROCESS: Cut rigid cardboard to the width of the shell and extend past it by about an inch.
3. PROCESS: Make a hole in the middle of the cardboard.

#### PROCESS: Assemble Knob Base
```

instruct00372.title: Homemade Nutella
instruct00372.text: This chocolate and hazelnut spread needs no introduction. To make about 3 small jars, you will need: 7 oz ofhazelnuts 1 can of sweetened condensed milk 9 oz of dark chocolate 1/2 cup of milk Other materials: food processor pan mixing bowl spatula double boiler cans On a medium flame, dry roast your hazelnuts for about 10-15 minutes. The nuts should smell toasty, not burnt. Once done, set aside and let cool completely. Place hazelnuts in food processor and pulse away. This step takes some time, but you'll be done once the hazelnuts have the texture of peanut butter. In a double boiler, melt the chocolate until smooth and just melted. You can add a pinch of salt here if you wish. Remove from heat, and pour into a mixing bowl. Add sweetened condensed milk and mix thoroughly. Mmm, just look at those sweet tasty swirls. Now pour your hazelnut butter into your chocolate mixture, and combine. You will have a very thick dough-like chocolate mixture. Add tiny pours of warm milk until you reach your desired consistency. Take your Nutella through another round in the food processor if you wish, just to smooth things up a bit. Pour into your jar (or right into your mouth), and enjoy! Pairs well with just about everything.

instruct00133.title: Make Your Own Notebooks!
instruct00133.text: Stop buying Moleskine or Field Notes notebooks and start making your own! It's super easy and saves you money and a trip to the store. This project uses a pamphlet stitch to bind a cute notebook. You will need: - 5 sheets of blank printer paper, 8.5" x 11" - a ruler - a pencil - an X-acto knife - decorative paper for covers - string - needle Optional book making tools: awl and bone folder Cut your printer paper in half to make 10 sheets of 8.5" wide by 5.5" tall paper. Using a bone folder, fold each new sheet into half to make them 4.25" wide by 5.5" tall. If you don't have a bone folder, use your fingers to crease the paper. Cut a 8.5" wide by 5.5" tallcover from a piece of decorative paper, and fold it in half. Place printer paper inside of the cover and, using the awl, poke three holes in the spine: one in the center and one about two inches from the center hole on each side. If you don't have an awl, you can use your needle or X-acto knife to poke these holes. Be careful not to cut yourself with the awl and X-acto; both are really sharp! String your needle with enough string as three times the height of your notebook, about 16.5". I'm using waxed linen thread, but you can use any type of string or ribbon to bind the notebook. Starting on the outside, pull the string three-fourths of the way through the middle hole, leaving the rest of the thread hanging without a knot. Take the needle through the top hole, pulling tight but without pulling the extra thread through. Take the needle back through the middle hole. Finally, take the needle through the bottom hole. Tie a bow with the beginning string and the extra string, pulling tightly. Cut off any extra string. You've made your own beautiful notebook! If you want a true Field Notes feel, use a corner rounder punch and use kraft cardstock for the covers. The possibilities are endless with the types of papers you can use for the inside and cover and the different types of string you can use to bind it!

```markdown
# DIY Notebook System

## Summary
This system guides you through the process of creating your own notebook using a pamphlet stitch. It requires basic materials such as printer paper, a ruler, pencil, X-acto knife, decorative paper, string, and a needle. Optional tools include an awl and bone folder.

## Process Steps

### START:
- Begin the DIY Notebook creation process.

### INPUT: Gather Materials
- 5 sheets of blank printer paper (8.5" x 11")
- Ruler
- Pencil
- X-acto knife
- Decorative paper for covers
- String
- Needle
- Optional: Awl and bone folder

### PROCESS: Prepare the Paper
- Cut the printer paper in half to create 10 sheets (8.5" x 5.5").

### PROCESS: Fold the Paper Sheets
- IF [you have a bone folder]:
  - Use the bone folder to fold each sheet in half to 4.25" x 5.5".
- ELSE:
  - Use your fingers to crease the paper.

### PROCESS: Prepare the Cover
- Cut the decorative paper to 8.5" x 5.5".
- Fold the decorative paper in half.

### PROCESS: Assemble the Paper and Cover
- Place the folded printer paper inside the folded cover.

### PROCESS: Poke Holes in the Spine
- IF [you have an awl]:
  - Use the awl to poke three holes along the spine (one center, two 2 inches apart).
- ELSE:
  - Use the needle or X-acto knife to poke these holes.

### DECISION [Is the user being careful with sharp tools?]:
- IF [Yes]:
  - Continue to the next step.
- ELSE [No]:
  - Remind the user to be careful to avoid injury.

### INPUT: Prepare the Thread
- Cut a length of string three times the height of the notebook (approximately 16.5").

### PROCESS: Thread the Needle
- Thread the needle with the cut string.

### PROCESS: Begin Stitching
- Start from the outside and pull the string through the middle hole, leaving some thread hanging.

### PROCESS: Continue Stitching
- Take the needle through the top hole and pull tight.
- Go back through the middle hole.
- Proceed through the bottom hole.

### PROCESS: Secure the Stitch
- Tie the starting string and the extra string into a bow, pulling tightly.
- Trim any excess string.

### OUTPUT: Completed Notebook
- The user now has a handcrafted notebook.

### DECISION [Does the user want a Field Notes style notebook?]:
- IF [Yes]:
  - Use a corner rounder punch on the covers.

  - The process is complete.
```

instruct00526.title: Fatoush - a Zesty Middle-eastern Salad
instruct00526.text: This is a very well known salad dish, in the Middle-East, and is particularly associated with Egypt and the Lebanon. Its really easy to prepare, needing some coarse chopping and then mixing. The only thing is, it benefits from "marinading" in the lemon juice for an hour or so. The final flourish, the addition of a spice called sumac is optional, but authentic. Our supply is Iranian sumac, bought in Tehran from THEmost amazing spice shop, and supplied by really friendly people. Ingredients: 4 tomatoes - a nice fresh sweet variety for preference. 1 cucumber 4 spring onions (scallions) 3 cloves of freshly crushed/ chopped garlic Broad leaf parsley (a good bunch) Garden mint ( a couple of sprigs) Juice of 2 lemons 3-4 pita breads Sumac, if available. Into one bowl, throw all the ingredients 1.) Cut cucumber into 4 length-ways, chop into 6mm / 1/4" chunks. 2.)Chop tomato into similar slices, and chop into thumbnail sized pieces (don't bother peeling tomatoes, lifess too short) 3.) Chop scallions into short chunks 4. Chop garlic, or use a garlic press 5. )Coarsely chop parsley, strip mint leaves off stalk, and chop and add to bowl. 7.) Juice 2 lemons (nuke 'em for 15 seconds first, to make 'em juicy) Pour over contents of bowl... Mix thoroughly, make sure the veggies are nicely covered with the lemon juice. Put aside in refrigerator for an hour. Toast 3 or 4 pita breads and chop into bite sized pieces. Just before serving, mix in pita bread If you're familiar with sumac, add some sprinkling to the dish before serving - it adds a further lemony flavour which is very refreshing. Otherwise, serve sumac in a pepper shaker with the salad. Serve and enjoy. We're serving the salad in pitta bread, with sea-bass cooked with paprika and lime

```markdown
# Middle-Eastern Salad System

## Ingredients:
- 4 fresh, sweet tomatoes
- 1 cucumber
- 4 spring onions (scallions)
- 3 cloves of freshly crushed/chopped garlic
- Broad leaf parsley (a good bunch)
- Garden mint (a couple of sprigs)
- Juice of 2 lemons
- 3-4 pita breads
- Sumac (optional)

## Steps:

### START:
- Begin the salad preparation process.

### PROCESS: Prepare the Ingredients
- INPUT: Gather all the ingredients required for the salad.

### PROCESS: Cut the Cucumber
- Cut the cucumber lengthwise into 4 parts.
- Chop the cucumber parts into 6mm / ¼" chunks.

### PROCESS: Chop the Tomatoes
- Chop the tomatoes into thumbnail-sized pieces without peeling.

### PROCESS: Chop the Spring Onions
- Chop the spring onions into short chunks.

### PROCESS: Prepare the Garlic
- Chop the garlic finely or use a garlic press.

### PROCESS: Prepare the Herbs
- Coarsely chop the broad leaf parsley.
- Strip the mint leaves off the stalk and chop them.

### PROCESS: Combine Vegetables and Herbs
- Combine the cucumber, tomatoes, spring onions, garlic, parsley, and mint in a bowl.

### PROCESS: Juice the Lemons
- Microwave the lemons for 15 seconds to make them juicier.
- Juice the 2 lemons.

### PROCESS: Add Lemon Juice to Salad
- Pour the lemon juice over the contents of the bowl.
- Mix thoroughly to ensure the vegetables are nicely covered with the lemon juice.

### PROCESS: Marinate the Salad
- Store the salad in the refrigerator for about an hour to marinate.

### PROCESS: Toast and Prepare Pita Breads
- Toast 3-4 pita breads until crispy.
- Chop the toasted pita breads into bite-sized pieces.

### DECISION: Is it time to serve the salad?
- IF Yes: Go to the next step.
- IF No: Continue to marinate until serving time.

### PROCESS: Finalize the Salad
- Just before serving, mix the toasted pita bread pieces into the salad.

### DECISION: Using Sumac?
- IF Yes: Sprinkle sumac over the salad for an authentic lemony flavor.
- IF No: Optionally, serve sumac in a pepper shaker alongside the salad.

### OUTPUT: Serve the Salad
- Serve the Middle-Eastern salad with the optional sumac and enjoy, possibly with pitta bread and sea-bass cooked with paprika and lime.

### END:
- The salad preparation process is complete.
```

instruct00722.title: Clean a Knife
instruct00722.text: In this instructable, I will show my way of easily cleaning a hunting knife, swiss army knife, whittling knife, etc... Remember to give me a +1! First thing, after using a knife and it gets dirty, don't close it (if its a closing knife). The reason is because stuff like dirt, tree sap, what ever is on the blade might get stuck in the base of the knife, dulling the blade every time it is closed. This will assure your knife a long happy life. The picture is of my knife after doing my other instructable, Whittle a Staff / Walking Stick. Turn a tap on hot and wait for it to heat up. Once it is as hot as it gets, place the blade under the water for 30 seconds, rotating it. Take an old electric tooth brush, and brush all along the blade, with some pressure. Do the same thing with both sides. Rinse the blade the same way you did in step 2, to make sure it's immaculately clean. Dry the blade with a towel making sure that the sharp edge is facing away from the towel, not towards. Any make SURE that the blade is fully dried. Your blade should now be as shiny as new! Remember to give this instructable a +1!

instruct00270.title: Easy No Egg Ravioli/Perogi Dough
instruct00270.text: A quick and easy way to make your own ravioli/perogi dough. No need for a grocery listor fancy kitchenskills for this recipe as only three ingredients are needed! A perfect dough if you are needing an eggless pasta. This recipe will yield about 48 raviolis or10 large 6"perogies. I include instructions to make the dough by hand or with a food processor. For this Instructable,the photos will show themaking oflarge dinner size perogies with the dough. 3 cups of all purpose flour 2 Tablespoons of Olive oil (melted butter/margarine may be substituted) 1 cup of water 1 teaspoon salt (optional) A large bowl and fork orA food processor 1. Put three cups of flour into a large bowl, making a well in the center. or Put three cups of flour into a food processor - secure the lid. 2. Add the wet ingredients to the well and very slowly mix together with a fork incorporating a little flour at a time. Knead by hand for about ten minutes, rest covered for half an hour. Repeat kneading until the dough is smooth and silky/slightly sticky. orAdd the wet ingredients to the processor's fill tube pulsing until well mixed. A ball of dough should form and pull away from the edges of the bowl. Continue to pulse for about one minute kneading the dough. Let rest in the bowl for at least one half an hour tohelprelax the gluten.3. The pasta can nowrolled with a pin or it can be shaped with a machine. Roll out the dough to the desired shape and thickness. I use a 6" perogi/pie press. Cut out, fill and seal the pasta. The filling that I am using is a mash potatoe,sour cream, chives and buttermix. Optional - Freeze on a lined cookie sheet for theleast chance of leakage during boiling. If freezing for later use, remove frozen pastafrom the cookie sheet and put into a sealable freezer bag. The frozen ravioli/perogiesshould keepwell for up to threemonths. Heat water to boiling in a 4-6 quart pot; add the pasta carefully to the water. Frozenpasta (20-30minutes in the freezer) is less likely to open up while boiling than fresh. Boiling fresh pasta takes significantly less time than dry pasta. Depending on the shape and size, cook for30 seconds to 2 minutes, double the time if using filledpasta that has been frozen. Saute in butter to lightly brown (optional.) Top with favorite sauce, serve and enjoy.

```markdown
# Ravioli/Perogi Dough Recipe System

## Ingredients and Tools
- INPUT: 3 cups of all-purpose flour
- INPUT: 2 tablespoons of olive oil (or melted butter/margarine)
- INPUT: 1 cup of water
- INPUT: 1 teaspoon salt (optional)
- INPUT: A large bowl and fork or a food processor

## Dough Preparation
- START: Begin ravioli/perogi dough preparation.
- PROCESS: Place 3 cups of flour into a large bowl and make a well in the center.
- DECISION [IF]: Is a food processor being used?
    - Yes: PROCESS: Put 3 cups of flour into the food processor and secure the lid.
    - No: Continue with the bowl method.

### Mixing Wet Ingredients
- INPUT: Add wet ingredients (olive oil and water) and salt if using, to the flour.
- DECISION [IF]: Is a food processor being used for mixing?
    - Yes: PROCESS: Add wet ingredients to the processor's fill tube, pulsing until well mixed.
    - No: PROCESS: Slowly mix together with a fork, incorporating a little flour at a time.

### Kneading the Dough
- DECISION [IF]: Is a food processor being used for kneading?
    - Yes: PROCESS: Pulse for about one minute until a ball of dough forms.
    - No: PROCESS: Knead by hand for about ten minutes until the dough is smooth and silky/slightly sticky.

### Resting the Dough
- PROCESS: Let the dough rest, covered, for at least one half an hour to relax the gluten.

## Shaping the Dough
- PROCESS: Roll out the dough to the desired shape and thickness.
- INPUT: Use a 6" perogi/pie press if available.
- OUTPUT: Cut out the dough into the desired shapes for ravioli or perogies.

## Filling the Pasta
- INPUT: Prepare the filling (mash potato, sour cream, chives, and butter mix).
- PROCESS: Fill and seal the pasta with the prepared filling.

## Optional Freezing
- DECISION [IF]: Will the pasta be frozen for later use?
    - Yes: PROCESS: Freeze on a lined cookie sheet to minimize leakage during boiling.
        - PROCESS: Once frozen, transfer pasta to a sealable freezer bag.
        - STORE: Keep frozen ravioli/perogies for up to three months.
    - No: Continue to boiling step.

## Cooking the Pasta
- PROCESS: Heat water to boiling in a 4-6 quart pot.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the pasta frozen?
    - Yes: PROCESS: Carefully add frozen pasta to the water, cook for 1 to 4 minutes depending on size.
    - No: PROCESS: Carefully add fresh pasta to the water, cook for 30 seconds to 2 minutes depending on size.

## Optional Sauteing
- DECISION [IF]: Will the pasta be sautéed?
    - Yes: PROCESS: Saute in butter to lightly brown.
    - No: Continue to serving step.

## Serving
- OUTPUT: Top the cooked pasta with your favorite sauce.
- OUTPUT: Serve and enjoy the homemade ravioli/perogies.
- END: Ravioli/Perogi preparation and cooking process is complete.
```

instruct00240.title: Hemming Jeans the Easy Way
instruct00240.text: I can't even begin to tell you how many needles I've broken while trying to hem jeans. At one point I was going to don safety glasses to protect my eyes from flying needles! But no more! I thought there has to be a better way and today I will show you just what I do. I consider this my 12 Step Program to Hemming Jeans. Start out by measuring from the inner crotch to how many inches long the legs need to be. My husband has short legs and needs his pants to be 27 inches. I need one inch to fold up so I mark 28 inches with a Sharpie. Mark straight across with a ruler. Cut and save the piece. Use it to measure the second leg, mark and cut it. If the only reason I bought my serger was to hem jeans then it was money well spent! Serge all the way around, just barely trimming. Yes I know it's white thread, and I know I should change it to blue, but I hate changing it and besides who's going to see the inside of Hubby's pants? If you don't have a serger I'm sure you could do a zig-zag stitch using your sewing machine. We just want to stop the fray. Remember that extra inch when you measured? Fold the jeans up one inch and pin. Pin all the way around. Make sure everything lays flat. Use your sewing machine, and with blue thread, stitch all the way around. I like to follow the serger line. Iron everything flat. This step is purely optional but it will look more professional if you do it. Change your thread to gold and, using your sewing machine, sew around about a 1/2 inch from the edge. Because the hem is only doubled over you can even backstitch over the seams, something I could never do if I had them folded up twice without risking a broken/bent/flying needle. Finished. After a few washes the hem looks even more authentic, and if you're impatient you can rub sandpaper or a nail file over the hem for that original look. I'm sure there are a zillion different ways to hem jeans but this is what works for me. I hope you enjoyed the tutorial :)

```markdown
# 12 Step Program to Hemming Jeans

## Step-by-Step Representation Summary

### START:
- Begin the process of hemming jeans.

### INPUT:
- Gather jeans, measuring tape, Sharpie, ruler, scissors, serger (or sewing machine), pins, blue thread, gold thread, iron, optional sandpaper or nail file.

### PROCESS: [Measure the Length]
- Measure from the inner crotch to the desired length of the jeans.
  
### STORE:
- Store the measurement value for the leg length (e.g., 27 inches for the example).

### PROCESS: [Mark for Cutting]
- Add one inch to the measured length for hemming (e.g., 28 inches in the example).
- Use a Sharpie and a ruler to mark straight across the leg at the new length.

### OUTPUT:
- A marked line on the jeans for cutting.

### PROCESS: [Cut the Excess Fabric]
- Cut the jeans across the marked line.
- Save the cut-off piece.

### OUTPUT:
- The jeans are cut to the correct length with an extra inch for hemming.

### PROCESS: [Measure Second Leg]
- Use the cut-off piece from the first leg to measure and mark the second leg.

### PROCESS: [Cut Second Leg]
- Cut the second leg of the jeans.

### STORE:
- Store the cut-off piece from the second leg.

### DECISION [IF]: [Do you have a serger?]
- IF Yes:
  - PROCESS: [Serge Edges]
    - Serge around the cut edge of the jeans, barely trimming with white thread.
- IF No:
  - PROCESS: [Zig-Zag Stitch]
    - Use a zig-zag stitch on a sewing machine to prevent fraying.

### OUTPUT:
- The edges of the jeans are finished to prevent fraying.

### PROCESS: [Fold and Pin Hem]
- Fold up the jeans one inch from the bottom.
- Pin the fold all the way around, ensuring it lays flat.

### PROCESS: [Sew Hem with Blue Thread]
- Use a sewing machine with blue thread to stitch all the way around, following the serger or zig-zag line.

### OUTPUT:
- The hem is sewn with blue thread.

### PROCESS: [Iron the Hem]
- Iron the hem flat for a professional look.

### DECISION [IF]: [Do you want a professional finish?]
- IF Yes:
  - PROCESS: [Sew with Gold Thread]
    - Change the thread to gold and sew around the hem about 1/2 inch from the edge using a sewing machine.
- IF No:
  - END: [Finish without Gold Stitching]

### OUTPUT:
- The jeans are hemmed with an optional gold stitch for a professional finish.

### PROCESS: [Create Authentic Look]
- Optionally, use sandpaper or a nail file over the hem to create an authentic worn look.

### OUTPUT:
- The completed hemmed jeans with an authentic look.

### END:
- The process of hemming jeans is complete.
```

instruct00808.title: Pixelated Popup Card
instruct00808.text: I'd been scratching my head trying to come up with a card for my hubby {AKA the non-romantic type}. I finally decided to make him this pixely popup heart card! I've seen similar styledpop-upsbefore and thought a heart would work really well. The card is also really minimal (which I love) and take about 20 minutes to make (that includes the card, insert and envelope). Download the popup insert template and print out on to a sheet of paper or thin card. I used pink paper but you can use any color you want. Using some scissors trim around the edge of the template. Place your piece of paper on a cutting mat (or a scrap piece of cardboard). Using a craft knife and ruler cut along the black lines (highlighted in yellow) andscorealong the grey lines. You can score the card with your craft knife (justdon'tpress too hard).Alternatelyyou can use a compass point or even a pin! Make the four valley folds as show in the image below (marked with thin yellow lines). Make sure your card is still resting on a flat surface and s-l-o-w-l-y fold the top of the card inwards and the bottom half of the heart should begin to push out. (You don't need to tape it to the tableI just did because I was taking pictures at the same time!) Make outer card and glue/tape popup insert inside. I just used a plain piece of paper which measured 9.5cm x 19cm and then folded it in half. I left mine blank (I really dig the minimal look) however if you want to decorate the outside then you can! Print out the envelope template. Cut, score and fold! I also made some paper pixel confetti to add to the card! Pop the card in the envelope and stick down. You can use glue or tape (or even some pretty washi tape). Happy valentines day everyone!!

instruct00223.title: Creating Instructables Using the Instructables IOS App
instruct00223.text: Hello and welcome to Instructables! In this Instructable, we'll be going over how to create an Instructable through our iOS App. (Now available on iPad!) Let's get started! Open up the application. You will now be viewing the homepage of the app. Click on the icon labeled "share" at the bottom. You will now see 4 different tabs: New Instructable, Drafts, Published, and Help. We will be clicking onNew Instructable.New Instructable - Create a new instructableDrafts - View your unpublished & saved instructables. Remember, you can save your projects straight to your mobile device orthe websitePublished - View your published projectsHelp - this will guide you step-by-step through the process we will be going over in this Instructable Choose a title and category for your Instructable. Make sure your project is under the right category! Clicking on theTitle orCategorytab will open up the keyboard. You can now start to add descriptions, steps, and images. A good Instructable should contain photos that are clear enough for everyone to see, along with thorough and detailed descriptions. You can also create new steps by dragging images in between step titles. You can also drag images from the top bar to steps, between steps, or back to the top. Make sure your photos are always well lit and clear! You have the option of taking a photo right on the spot or choosing existing images from your camera roll. Presseditto remove and rearrange steps. You can drag the step title rightto enlarge image viewing area,leftto revert. You can also swipe back and forth between steps! How cool is that? You're now ready to publish your Instructable! Keep in mind that once uploaded, you can always edit your Instructable. Now that you know the app like the back of your hand, go out there and make something awesome!

```markdown
### START:

### OUTPUT: Access to Creation Options

### INPUT: Provide Title and Category

- Begin adding descriptions for each step of the Instructable.

- Drag images between step titles to create new steps.

- Drag images from the top bar to steps, between steps, or back to the top.

- Edit the Instructable after uploading if necessary.

- The process of creating an Instructable through the iOS App is complete.
```

```markdown
# Paper Boomerang Creation System

## Inputs
- A4 sheets or any other type of paper
- Scissors
- Plaster
- Broomsticks
- Cardboard

## Outputs
- Completed paper boomerang

## Process Steps

START:
- Begin with the construction of the paper boomerang.

PROCESS [Prepare Materials]:
- INPUT: Gather all necessary materials.

PROCESS [Create Square Paper]:
- INPUT: Take an A4 sheet or other paper.
- OUTPUT: Square paper piece.

PROCESS [Fold Corners]:
- Fold all corners of the square paper towards the center.
- OUTPUT: Folded paper with corners towards center.

PROCESS [Fold Opposite Corners]:
- Fold 2 opposite corners towards the center (refer to images or video for clarity).
- OUTPUT: Paper with opposite corners folded.

PROCESS [Fold Bottom Flap]:
- Fold the bottom flap backwards.
- OUTPUT: Paper with the bottom flap folded backwards.

PROCESS [Join Flaps]:
- Join the left and right flaps together.
- OUTPUT: One completed boomerang piece.

DECISION [IF]: Have 15 pieces been made?
- Yes: Proceed to connect all pieces.
- No: Repeat PROCESS [Create Square Paper] to PROCESS [Join Flaps] until 15 pieces are made.

PROCESS [Connect Pieces]:
- Insert the opposite sides of the two flaps of each piece into each other (refer to images or video for clarity).
- OUTPUT: All pieces connected.

PROCESS [Plaster Pieces]:
- Plaster all connected pieces on both sides.
- OUTPUT: Normal boomerang structure.

PROCESS [Reinforce Structure]:
- Stick broomsticks to each edge of the boomerang.
- Fill the gap in the middle with cardboard.
- Plaster broomsticks and cardboard to secure.
- OUTPUT: Realistic-looking and sturdy paper boomerang.

END:
- The paper boomerang is now complete.

- For best results, watch the provided instructional video or refer to the images.
- The video includes instructions on how to throw the paper boomerang.

- A link to the instructional video is provided for further assistance.
```

instruct00177.title: Embroidered Corner Bookmarks
instruct00177.text: This is a quick walkthrough on how to make an embroidered corner bookmark out of felt. It's more of a no-recipe recipe than a full tutorial, so have fun with it! Stiff felt (soft felt will do, but your bookmark will be a little harder to use)Embroidery FlossEmbroidery NeedleScissorsWater soluble penEmbroidery hoop sized for your feltTemplate (linked below Stretch your felt on the hoop. Print the template at 100% (use the 1 inch box to make sure it is sized correctly). Cut out the triangle and trace it on to your stretched felt. Draw your embroidery pattern onto the triangle. You can find a free pattern online, pay for one, or do what I did here and just freehand something. Your stitching will be small, so keep that in mind when you plan your piece. Using a variety of stitches, embroider your design. For this piece I used satin stitch for the mushroom cap, stalk and grass, french knots for the flourishes and mushroom spots, and a fern stitch for the plants on the side. You can use any combination of stitches you find appealing. Be creative! Cut out your finished embroidery piece, and a second triangle using the same template for the back. Stitch the two pieces together. I chose a blanket stitch for mine, but a running or backstitch, or even machine sewing the pieces together would work. When you've stitched everything together, run your piece under cool water to dissolve any visible ink. Let your bookmark dry completely before testing it. You don't want to wet your book pages! Happy reading!

```markdown
# Embroidered Corner Bookmark Creation Process

## START:
- Begin the process to create an embroidered corner bookmark.

## INPUT:
- Gather materials:
  - Stiff felt (or soft felt if unavailable)
  - Embroidery floss
  - Embroidery needle
  - Scissors
  - Water-soluble pen
  - Embroidery hoop
  - Bookmark template

## PROCESS: [Stretching the Felt]
- Stretch the felt on the embroidery hoop to prepare for the embroidery process.

## PROCESS: [Template Preparation]
- Print the bookmark template at 100% scale, using the 1-inch box on the template to confirm correct sizing.

## PROCESS: [Cutting the Template]
- Cut out the triangle from the printed template.

## PROCESS: [Tracing Template onto Felt]
- Trace the triangle template onto the stretched felt using a water-soluble pen.

## PROCESS: [Drawing Embroidery Pattern]
- Draw the desired embroidery pattern onto the traced triangle.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is a free pattern available online?
    - Yes: Use the free pattern.
    - No: Move to the next decision.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is there a willingness to pay for a pattern?
    - Yes: Purchase and use the pattern.
    - No: Freehand draw a custom pattern.

## PROCESS: [Embroidering the Design]
- Using selected embroidery stitches, embroider the drawn design.
  - Example stitches:
    - Satin stitch for mushroom cap, stalk, and grass.
    - French knots for flourishes and mushroom spots.
    - Fern stitch for plants on the side.

## PROCESS: [Cutting Out Embroidered Piece]
- Cut out the embroidered felt triangle.

## PROCESS: [Cutting Out Back Piece]
- Cut out a second triangle from felt using the same template for the bookmark's back.

## PROCESS: [Stitching Pieces Together]
- Stitch the two felt triangles together.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is a specific stitch type preferred?
    - Yes: Use the preferred stitch type (e.g., blanket, running, backstitch).
    - No: Default to a simple stitch or machine sewing.

## PROCESS: [Dissolving Ink]
- Run the stitched bookmark under cool water to dissolve any visible ink from the water-soluble pen.

## PROCESS: [Drying the Bookmark]
- Allow the bookmark to dry completely.

## OUTPUT:
- A handmade embroidered felt corner bookmark is ready for use.

## DECISION [IF]: Is the bookmark dry?
  - Yes: Proceed to test the bookmark.
  - No: Continue drying until completely dry.

## PROCESS: [Testing the Bookmark]
- Test the bookmark on a book corner to ensure functionality.

## END:
- Enjoy the new bookmark with happy reading!
```

instruct00718.title: How to Convert a Mini Fridge to a Chest Refrigerator
instruct00718.text: It's just awful that when I open my refrigerator, all the cold air falls out. This makes me sad. So, I turned my refrigerators word upside down, or at least 90 degrees. Now, when I open the door, more cold air stays inside and this makes me happy - it increases my quality of life in fact. For the rest of you with a large refrigerator.... I, and my partner in crime have something cooking for you. But, it's going to take a month or so as I want data showing this big refrigerator modification works. As you read meters are whizzing and collecting :) This particular model was discovered in the annals of the UCF dumpsters during dorm move-out. The funny thing is, it was found, in the dumpster, with ice inside. To speed up production time, the compressor is assembled on a compressor mount separately from the rest of the unit. So, unscrew the compressor assembly from the fridge. Firmly grasp the compressor and rotate it 90 degrees so that the top of the compressor faces what will become the bottom of the refrigerator. Try not to move it too much to prevent damage to the lines coming in and out the compressor. Please note, it will take a fair amount of force to rotate the compressor assembly. This is normal. If your refrigerator is designed like mine, the compressor assembly will not fit back into the space provided by the fridge manufacturer. I scrounged up 4 1/2 inch PVC couplings to act as spacers. I'm also using a spare bit of 1/2" PVC pipe and two 90 degree elbows to make feet. I used 5 minute epoxy ($1 from harbor freight) to secure the feet and coupling risers. And by upright I mean on it's back - the new bottom :) Before turning on, you'll probably want to let the compressor sit upright for a few hours, to make sure any oil settles back at the base. I'm not quite sure this is completely necessary as I believe the lubrication is in the refrigerant itself, but perhaps its best to play on the side of caution. Now, plug your chest refrigerator in and turn it on :) For those wanting to turn a refrigerator into a freezer, it shouldn't be too hard. The only thing you'll need is a new thermostat that is connected to your compressor. As mine will be used, for now, as the beer fridge with spirits locker - I will not be converting to a freezer.

```markdown
# Refrigerator Modification System

## Start
START: Begin the process of modifying a refrigerator to retain more cold air.

## Process: Assessing the Refrigerator
PROCESS: Locate a refrigerator, such as the one found in the UCF dumpsters during dorm move-out.

## Decision: Is the Refrigerator Functional?
DECISION [IF]: Check if the refrigerator is in working condition, evidenced by ice found inside.
    - Yes: Proceed with the modification.
    - No: END: Do not proceed with modification.

## Process: Preparing the Compressor
PROCESS: To modify the refrigerator, first, remove the compressor assembly from the fridge.
INPUT: Tools to unscrew the compressor assembly.

## Process: Rotating the Compressor
PROCESS: Firmly grasp the compressor and rotate it 90 degrees to reorient its position.
    - Note: It requires significant force to rotate the compressor assembly. This is normal.
INPUT: Compressor assembly.

## Decision: Does the Compressor Fit?
DECISION [IF]: Check if the rotated compressor assembly fits back into the space provided.
    - Yes: Proceed to secure the compressor.
    - No: Go to the next step to create spacers.

## Process: Creating Spacers and Feet
PROCESS: If the compressor doesn't fit, use 4 1/2 inch PVC couplings as spacers, and create feet using 1/2" PVC pipe and two 90-degree elbows.
INPUT: PVC couplings, PVC pipe, 90-degree elbows, and 5-minute epoxy.

## Process: Securing the Compressor
PROCESS: Use 5-minute epoxy to secure the feet and coupling risers, setting the fridge upright on its back.
INPUT: 5-minute epoxy.

## Process: Letting the Compressor Settle
PROCESS: Allow the compressor to sit upright for a few hours to ensure any oil settles back at the base.
    - Note: This may or may not be necessary but is recommended as a precaution.

## Process: Turning on the Refrigerator
PROCESS: Plug the modified chest refrigerator in and turn it on.
OUTPUT: Modified refrigerator now functions with better cold air retention.

## Decision: Converting to Freezer
DECISION [IF]: Decide if you want to convert the refrigerator into a freezer.
    - Yes: Install a new thermostat connected to the compressor.
    - No: Use as is for the intended purpose, such as a beer fridge with spirits locker.

END: The refrigerator modification process is complete.
```

instruct00004.title: Make Your Own Top Water Minnow Fishing Lures
instruct00004.text: Inspired by msolek's instructable and looking for a simple excuse to use my lathe, I decided to knock out some fishing lures. These are alternately know as"Stickbaits" and "Cigar baits". You'll want to select a fairly low density soft wood for your lures, Spanish Cedar is a classic choice, but any cedar or pine should work fine. Start by ripping the wood into 3/4 inch square by 6 inch pieces. Use your lathe to turn the wood into a nice piscatorial spindle shape. If you don't have a lathe, I suggest you build one. Since we're going to get these wet, it is necessary to seal the wood. If you have a particularly pretty grain pattern you could use a clear finish. I choose Krylon spray paint, since it was at hand. The thumbtack was used as a handle for painting. Hint: Stick the tack somewhere where the hardware will mask the hole. I purchased my hardware from Penn State Industries. I've had nothing but positive experiences with them. The location of the hardware was eyeballed and the screw holes started with an awl, since the wood is soft, pre-drilling is unnecessary. You'll notice I only used one hook, that's just a personal preferences, but lures with masses of treble hooks that tangle in the tackle box annoy me, yeah I'm talking about you, Helin Flatfish. If you don't want to buy special hardware, I'd suggest just using screw eyes and maybe some ballast to achieve neutral bouyancy. Okay, so I'm the worlds worst painter. ;-) But grab some of your wife's nailpolish (uummm Yeah, it's the wife's) and decorate your lure. I used silver and some glow in the dark OPI I got clearanced at Ulta. Umm, okay, where's the pic of a big fish? Yeah, so I got skunked today, 3 hours of flailing the water with artificials and naturals and nadda, let's blame it on the cold front. On the other hand, they ran very true, the only tuning was to bend the lip up which made them dive deeper and wiggle tighter. If I catch a big fish, I'll add a pic ;-)

```markdown
- Paint the lure with nail polish or other decorative paints.
```

instruct00609.title: How to Balance a Chemical Equation
instruct00609.text: A chemical equation is the chemical formula that provides the information of the elements and molecules that are reacting as well as the molecules that are being produced from that reaction. The Law of Conservation of Mass states that the mass of the reactants must balance the mass of the products. To balance a chemical equation, the atoms of both the elements and molecules on the reactant side (left side) and product side (right side) must be equal to each other.In this instructable, you will understand and learn how to balance a chemical equation.This instructable should take no longer than ten minutes. The unbalanced chemical equation is given to you. Aluminum reacts with oxygen to produce aluminum oxide. Rewrite the equation as shown above. First, identify the elements on the reactant side(left side) and the elements of the compound are on the product side (right side).make a list of all of the elements on each side under the equation for both the reactants and products as shown aboveUnder the reactant's side, list Al and Ounder the product's side, list Al and O An atom is the smallest component of an element that contains chemical properties of that element. The atom of each element's contains the protons, neutrons, and electrons of that element.The list made of each element on both the reactant and product side will further help you identify the number of atoms each element contains.Next to each element of the list, put the number of atoms that are in each of the elements. on the reactants side, next to Al, put 1 next to O, put 2apply these same rules to each element on the product side Notice how the number of atoms next to each element is different from the number of atoms next to that same element on the product side.In order to balance the chemical equation, you need to make sure the number of atoms of each element on the reactant side is equal to the number of atoms of each element on the product side. In order make both sides equal, you will need to multiply the number of atoms in each element until both sides are equal. As shown above, the multiplication of the atoms on the reactant side will affect both elements on the product side. After you have multiplied the number of atoms of each element until both sides are equal, you will put the number, the coefficient, of how much you multiplied the element by and place in front of that element or compound in the equation as shown above.On the product side, although both elements did not get multiplied, still place the number that was multiplied as the coefficient in front of the compound. After you have placed the coefficients in front of the molecules, make the list of elements again and check to see if multiplying the coefficient with the subscript will give you atoms equal on both the reactant and product sides.If they are not equal, rework your multiplication. After you have reworked your multiplication, make the list of elements again to check to make sure the equation is balanced. If both sides are equal, you have now balanced the chemical equation!

```markdown
# Structured Summary of Balancing a Chemical Equation

## Start of the Process
START: Begin with an unbalanced chemical equation provided.

## Input the Unbalanced Equation
INPUT: Unbalanced equation - Aluminum reacts with oxygen to produce aluminum oxide.

## Rewrite the Equation
PROCESS: Rewrite the equation to clearly show reactants and products.

## Identify Elements on Both Sides
PROCESS: Identify and list all elements on the reactant side and the product side under the equation.

## List Elements
- STORE: Under reactants, list Al and O.
- STORE: Under products, list Al and O.

## Understanding Atoms
PROCESS: Understand that an atom is the smallest component of an element that contains its chemical properties.

## Count Atoms in Elements
PROCESS: Next to each element on both sides, list the number of atoms present.

## List Number of Atoms
- STORE: On the reactant side, next to Al, put 1; next to O, put 2.
- PROCESS: Apply the same rule to the product side.

## Check for Imbalance
DECISION [IF]: Are the number of atoms of each element equal on both sides?
- No: Continue to the next step to balance the equation.
- Yes: Skip the balancing steps; the equation is already balanced.

## Balance the Equation
PROCESS: Multiply the number of atoms in each element until both sides are equal.

## Adjust Coefficients
PROCESS: Place the coefficient indicating the multiplication in front of the corresponding element or compound in the equation.

## Update Equation with Coefficients
PROCESS: On the product side, place the coefficient even if the element did not get multiplied.

## Verify Balance
PROCESS: Make a new list of elements and check if the coefficients multiplied by the subscripts yield equal atoms on both sides.

## Check for Balance Again
DECISION [IF]: Are both sides equal after applying coefficients?
- No: Go back and rework your multiplication.
- Yes: Proceed to confirm the balanced equation.

## Confirm Balanced Equation
OUTPUT: If both sides are equal, the chemical equation is now balanced.

## End of the Process
END: The process of balancing the chemical equation is complete.
```

instruct00551.title: Beachcomber Weathervane
instruct00551.text: First instructable - give me a break. Over the years I have improved a personal model of weathervane. Today Strolling on the beach with the grandkids, I built one for the Nth time and decided tto share. Gather your materials: 1 seagull feather and various sized pieces of bamboo Start with the propeller. Take a flat piece of bamboo, make a hole big enough to force the spacer in. If it splits, the hole wasn't big enough. If it wobbles, the hole is too big. Carve away a strip about 5mm wide on both sides of the propeller, one on the top-left and the other on the bottom-right.. Shave the blades in alternate inclination. Split a piece of bamboo to make the axis. Leave it ticker on the side of the notch, to retain the propeller. Trim the other side to fit loosely in the spacer. Insert the axis in the spacer and balance the propeller. If one side tends to swing down, it is heavier than the other. Carve away some shavings on the back, until both sides compensate each other. Make one hole through the top of the base. Insert the axis in the spacer and then in the hole on the base. Cut off the tip of the feather and insert the axis in the hollow of the feather. Sharpen the tip of the stem and place the base with the propeller and feather on it. Final notes: For windy days, use heavier, thicker pieces of bamboo. It will outstand months in the wind and rain. Fragile bamboo and lowest tech. handicraft amaze me every time. While combing the beach for the materials, it's a good idea to keep the knife closed, for safety. It's not an excuse if there are no drift bamboo pieces on your beach, or beach in your area.. Look around improvise. And, have fun

```markdown
# Weathervane Construction Process

## START:
- Begin the process of constructing a weathervane.

## INPUT:
- Gather materials:
  - 1 seagull feather
  - Various sized pieces of bamboo

## PROCESS: Propeller Creation
- Take a flat piece of bamboo.
- Make a hole in the center of the bamboo piece to insert the spacer.

## DECISION [IF]: Is the bamboo split after making a hole?
  - Yes: 
    - OUTPUT: The hole wasn't big enough.
    - END.
  - No: 
    - Continue to the next step.

## DECISION [IF]: Does the propeller wobble after inserting the spacer?
  - Yes: 
    - OUTPUT: The hole is too big.
    - END.
  - No: 
    - Continue to the next step.

## PROCESS: Carving the Propeller
- Carve away a strip approximately 5mm wide on both sides of the propeller, one on the top-left and the other on the bottom-right.
- Shave the blades to have alternate inclinations.

## PROCESS: Axis Preparation
- Split a piece of bamboo to make the axis.
- Leave the side of the axis thicker near the notch to retain the propeller.
- Trim the other side of the axis to fit loosely in the spacer.

## PROCESS: Assembly Part 1
- Insert the axis into the spacer.
- Balance the propeller on the axis.

## DECISION [IF]: Does one side of the propeller swing down?
  - Yes: 
    - PROCESS: Balance Adjustment
      - Carve away shavings on the back of the heavier side until both sides are balanced.
  - No: 
    - Continue to the next step.

## PROCESS: Assembly Part 2
- Make a hole through the top of the base.
- Insert the axis with the propeller into the newly made hole in the base.

## PROCESS: Feather Attachment
- Cut off the tip of the seagull feather.
- Insert the axis into the hollow of the feather.

## PROCESS: Final Assembly
- Sharpen the tip of the stem.
- Place the base with the propeller and feather onto the sharpened stem.

## OUTPUT:
- A completed weathervane.

## PROCESS: Adjustments for Wind Conditions
- For windy days, use heavier, thicker pieces of bamboo to ensure durability.

## END:
- The weathervane construction process is complete.

## STORE/DATABASE SUBROUTINE:
- Final notes and safety:
  - Use caution and keep the knife closed when combing the beach for materials.
  - If no drift bamboo is available, improvise with other materials.
  - Have fun with the construction process.
```

instruct00858.title: Survival Bracelet II
instruct00858.text: You may have seen my first survival bracelet instructable on the cobra braid. After receiving a comment from lightchaser mentioning the chain sinnet braid, I thought that was a great idea. This is truly a Survival Bracelet, if you are in need of some rope or cord, you can just pull both ends and then you have one full piece of 8 ft cord. Give it a try and see how simple it really is. In order to make a survival bracelet you will need -About 8 feet of 550 Parachute Cord (or whatever you have on hand) -Pair of scissors -Lighter -Pliers (not necessary but can make a tighter bracelet) The lanyard knot is a nice way to spruce up your bracelet, but can easily be replaced with an over hand knot. First make a small twist in the cord. Then make a "U" shape beneath the loop. Take the piece that points left and place it over the bottom loop, and under the right piece. Then over, under, and then over again. Hold the bottom loop down. This braid is very simple once you get it down. Make a small twist or loop in the cord. Then make a "U" shape and put it through the other loop. Pull tight. When the loop is facing left, then place the left piece through the loop. Continue until the bracelet is long enough. First, put both pieces all the way through the last loop. Then, as before you can make a lanyard knot again or an over hand knot. Trim the end and then melt it down. There you have it, a true survival bracelet.

```markdown
# Survival Bracelet Using Chain Sinnet Braid

## System Overview:
The system takes parachute cord as an input and produces a survival bracelet as an output through a series of steps that involve measuring, cutting, knotting, and finishing the cord. The system's goal is to create a bracelet that can be unraveled to provide a length of rope for survival purposes.

## Process Steps:

### START:
- Begin the process of creating a survival bracelet.

### INPUT:
- Acquire about 8 feet of 550 Parachute Cord.
- Gather a pair of scissors, lighter, and optionally pliers.

### PROCESS: [Preparing the Cord]
- Make a small twist in the cord to start the lanyard knot.

### PROCESS: [Forming the First Knot]
- Create a "U" shape beneath the loop with the cord.
- Take the piece of cord that points left and place it over the bottom loop and under the right piece of the cord.
- Continue the pattern: over, under, and then over again with the left piece.
- Secure the bottom loop by holding it down.

### DECISION [IF]: [Is the lanyard knot desired?]
  - Yes: Continue to use the lanyard knot.
  - No: Replace with an overhand knot.

### PROCESS: [Starting the Chain Sinnet Braid]
- Make a small twist or loop in the cord.
- Create a "U" shape with the cord and put it through the existing loop.
- Pull tight to secure the braid.

### PROCESS: [Continuing the Braid]
- When the loop is facing left, place the left piece of cord through the loop.
- Continue this pattern until the bracelet is of the desired length.

### PROCESS: [Finishing the Braid]
- Put both ends of the cord all the way through the last loop to secure the braid.

### DECISION [IF]: [Is a final lanyard knot desired?]
  - Yes: Make a lanyard knot with the remaining cord.
  - No: Make an overhand knot instead.

### PROCESS: [Trimming and Sealing the Ends]
- Trim the excess cord with scissors.
- Use the lighter to melt the ends of the cord.
- If available, use pliers to press the melted cord to ensure a tight seal and finish.

### OUTPUT:
- The final product is a true survival bracelet made from parachute cord.

### END:
- The process of creating a survival bracelet using the chain sinnet braid is complete.
```

instruct00111.title: How to (almost) Waterproof Air Dry Clay
instruct00111.text: The method I use to waterproof paper mache has been working pretty good, so I thought I would use it for outdoor air-dry clay sculptures.IngredientsAir dry clay Waterproof Wood Glue FlexBond Thin-set Mortar Exterior House Paint Acrylic paint Polyurethane Spray Simple star fish using Activa Air-Dry Clay. Let Dry 24 Hours. Paint Top and bottom with h a mixture of waterproof wood glue and acrylic paint. Roughly equal amounts of each.The paint thins down the glue a little and makes it easier to apply. The color doesn't matter at this point. Let Dry 24 hours. Mix up a bowl of roughly 4 parts mortar to 1 part water. Mix as you slowly ad water until you get a consistency you can paint with. It should slowly flow off your mixing spoon in a thick stream, something like pancake batter. If it runs off quickly , add more mortar. If it drops off in clumps, add more water.Paint your piece with the mortar mix. It will destroy your paint brush after your done, so use an old one. The mortar doesn't get absorbed into the red glue layer. It just kind of sits on top. Make sure you get full coverage.There are two major disadvantages when using this-set mortar.You lose detail You will have a rough surfaceThis method is only good for certain kinds of sculptures. It's great for anything made to look like concrete like garden statues or gargoyles. Also creatures with rough skin like dinosaurs, dragons, Godzilla and starfish! Paint a layer of exterior house-paint to seal the mortar layer.I use black Exterior Semi-Gloss Acrylic-Latex house paint. Here I've started painting with orange acrylic paint on top of the black house paint. Finish your paint job with acrylic paint, Then spray with polyurethane spay.Just sealing the clay with polyurethane or varnish without the waterproof glue will make the clay water resistant but not waterproof. Eventually it will disintegrate. I don't expect any of my outdoor sculptures to last forever, but this method seems to be working pretty good so far.Dan at Gourmet Paper Mache has had success with his Waterproof Dragon outside in a tree using waterproof glue and exterior paint. Dan is in Seattle. I'm in Vancouver, Canada so we get similar weather.After watching the waterproofing method recommended by DIY Easycraft, I started using Thin -Set Mortar for all my outdoor paper mache projectsLet me know in the comments your method of waterproofing air-dray clay. The keys to a waterproof outdoor sculptures are Waterproof Wood Glue, Thin-set mortar, and exterior house paint.UPDATE: The starfish started to fall apart after 1 month of being fully submerged in water. This method is great for the rain and the summer heat, but it's not 100% waterproof.Here are some outdoor paper-mache sculptures that have held up very well in the rain.See more at Paper Mache Props
instruct00111.summary:
```markdown
# Structured Summary of Waterproofing Air-Dry Clay Sculptures

## START:
- Begin the process of waterproofing an air-dry clay sculpture.

## INPUT:
- Air-dry clay sculpted into desired shape (e.g., a simple starfish).
- Waterproof wood glue.
- FlexBond Thin-set mortar.
- Exterior house paint.
- Acrylic paint.
- Polyurethane spray.

## PROCESS: Prepare the sculpture
- Create a sculpture using air-dry clay.
- STORE the sculpture and let it dry for 24 hours.

## PROCESS: Apply the first waterproof layer
- INPUT a mixture of waterproof wood glue and acrylic paint in roughly equal amounts.
- PROCESS: Paint the top and bottom of the sculpture with the glue-paint mixture.
- STORE the sculpture and let it dry for another 24 hours.

## PROCESS: Prepare the mortar mixture
- INPUT roughly 4 parts mortar to 1 part water.
- PROCESS: Mix mortar and water slowly until it reaches a pancake batter-like consistency.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the mixture too runny?
    - Yes: Add more mortar.
    - No: Continue to the next step.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the mixture too clumpy?
    - Yes: Add more water.
    - No: Continue to the next step.

## PROCESS: Apply the mortar mixture
- USE an old paintbrush to apply the mortar mix to the sculpture.
- ENSURE full coverage.
- NOTE: The mortar layer will result in a loss of detail and a rough surface.

## OUTPUT:
- The sculpture is now covered with a mortar layer that sits on top of the red glue layer.

## PROCESS: Seal the mortar layer
- PAINT a layer of exterior house paint to seal the mortar.
- STORE the sculpture and let the paint dry.

## PROCESS: Finish the paint job
- APPLY acrylic paint over the sealed mortar layer.
- SPRAY the sculpture with polyurethane spray to finish the waterproofing.

## OUTPUT:
- The completed and waterproofed air-dry clay sculpture.

## DECISION [IF]: Will the sculpture be submerged in water?
  - Yes: Note that this method is not 100% waterproof for full submersion.
  - No: Expect the sculpture to be durable against rain and summer heat.

## END:
- The process of waterproofing an air-dry clay sculpture is completed.
```

instruct00102.text: These cupcakes are Perfect for Weddings, Sweet 16's, Birthdays, Showers and can be gifted to someone special! :)Things you will need: Fondant Gumpaste/Gum-tex/Tylose Cornflour Rolling pin Flower cutters Leaf cutters Shashlik Stick Toothpicks Modelling tools Cupcakes (Of course :) ) Buttercream Spatula Brush Piping Bag Large round piping tip Red Color (I used Wilton No-taste Red) Flower Former Foam Pizza Cutter Water for gluing the fondant pieces Smooth Working Surface Shortening for greasing your hands Trays, Flower Former for drying flowers etc Important Notes: The fondant that is used EXCLUDING in covering of cupcakes, has been mixed with gumpaste 3:1 (3 part fondant and 1 part gumpaste), you can use Gum-tex or Tylose instead of gumpaste. After mixing colors in fondant, leave it to rest overnight or for 24 hours. Use cornflour for dusting your work area and also for dipping your cutters before using them. Freeze cupcakes for about an hour after icing. When drying the fondant pieces, keep them on cornflour dusted plates or trays. When making roses, let the bud dry completely before covering with petals. And then let each ring of petals dry after pasting to bud. Otherwise the rose will fall apart. Roll fondant 1/16 inch thick for covering the cupcakes and 1/8 inch thick for everything else. I have done my best to include each and every step. instruct00500.title: Instant Hammock
instruct00500.text: Here's how to make a hammock in a minute from a sheet or any big piece of cloth. It's the simplest method from my "Instant Hammock" article in Make Magazine Issue #9.I used the program "Avd Video Processor" to make these animated gifs from video.Now on Know How! Click on the steps above for more details.Do you like this Instructable? Digg it!. Then check out episodes one, two, four, five, six, and seven!First bunch up the ends and tie knots in them as shown. If you don't have much cloth, are skilled with rope, or don't care if you fall you can skip this step. just like this, or tie whatever knot you like best. If you don't fall it means you did it right. In utter comfort. Rachael Norman Demonstrates. For extra coziness pull the hammock around you like a coccoon. Saul Griffith uses an instant hammock at MITERS to work on large drawings for a kite he's making. Danielle rigged up this swell triangular hammock in her yard in Austin TX. It's a bedspread tied at the corners to three trees. Her offspring Rhett Applestone gets his relax on. In case you'd like to make an elaborate Maya style hammock, here are some notes from 2001. You should probably buy a hammock to look at (and rest in) before attempting to make your own. Lauro lives at the entrance to Bahias de Punta Soliman in the Yucatan, Mexico. He weaves hammocks to pass the time. Here he is at work. He's using a netting needle just the same as the fishermen use to mend their nets. The string is thin hammock string which is sold in fabric and hardware stores there. The wooden frame is held together with wedges so he can change what size of hammock he makes. Also so he can remove the hammock from it when it's done. To start out he winds about half the string needed to make the hammock at the top of the loom at 'a'. Let's call that the "warp" string, although technically he's "twining" rather than "weaving" and it probably has a different official name. Then he loads up his netting needle with string and starts to wind it around the first two strands of warp string as shown. Wrap another turn of warp thread around the frame and go around and around it with your netting needle. The drawing is a little ambiguous (and rough). It's supposed to look like going around and around, not any other sort of more complicated pattern. There are many styles of hammock. This style gets you the most hammock for the least string. There are some where you wind your string around three or more warp strings at a time rather than the two shown here. There are lots of ways to finish a hammock, this is how Lauro did it. The strings at the very edge are important. If they break it's easy to fall out of the hammock. And hard to get comfortable.

```markdown
# Hammock Making System

## START:
- Begin with a piece of cloth or sheet to create a hammock.

## PROCESS: Prepare the Cloth
- INPUT: A large piece of cloth or sheet.
- PROCESS: Bunch up the ends of the cloth.
- DECISION [IF]: Is there enough cloth?
    - Yes: Proceed to tie knots.
    - No: Skip the knot-tying step. [END]

## PROCESS: Tie Knots
- PROCESS: Tie knots at the bunched ends of the cloth.
- DECISION [IF]: Did you fall when using the hammock?
    - Yes: The knots were not tied correctly. [END]
    - No: OUTPUT: Hammock is correctly made.

## OUTPUT: Basic Hammock
- OUTPUT: A functional hammock is created.

## PROCESS: Enhance Comfort
- DECISION [IF]: Do you want extra coziness?
    - Yes: Pull the hammock around like a cocoon.
    - No: Use the hammock as is.

## PROCESS: Use Cases
- PROCESS: Observe different uses such as working on large drawings or relaxing in a yard.

## PROCESS: Advanced Hammock Making
- INPUT: Purchase a hammock for reference.
- PROCESS: Learn from an experienced hammock weaver like Lauro.
- STORE: Study the technique and tools used by Lauro for future reference.

## PROCESS: Start Weaving (Advanced Technique)
- INPUT: Thin hammock string, netting needle, wooden frame.
- PROCESS: Wind half the string on the top of the loom (warp string).
- PROCESS: Load netting needle with string.
- PROCESS: Begin winding string around the warp strings using the netting needle.

## PROCESS: Continue Weaving (Advanced Technique)
- PROCESS: Wrap another turn of warp thread around the frame.
- PROCESS: Continue winding with the netting needle around and around.

## OUTPUT: Advanced Hammock
- OUTPUT: A more elaborate, woven hammock.

## PROCESS: Finishing Touches (Advanced Technique)
- PROCESS: Secure the strings at the very edge of the hammock.
- DECISION [IF]: Are the edge strings secure?
    - Yes: OUTPUT: Finished, comfortable hammock. [END]
    - No: Risk of falling or discomfort. [END]
```

instruct00374.title: Nutella Stuffed Vanilla Bean Cupcakes
instruct00374.text: I have an obsession with Nutella. It has invaded my cookies, my ice cream and my cakes. If you do not share my love of Nutella then turn back now as this recipe was not meant for you. As for the others who share my endless love of this yummy chocolate hazelnut spread, your mouth will water as you look through these steps. This instructable will show you how to do Nutella stuffed Vanilla Bean Cupcakes with Nutella buttercream frosting (wow! that's a mouthful, litterally).note: this is my first instructable, I hope it works! *crosses fingers* check out my recipe blog for more Nutella recipes:http://www.maries-cuisine.com/p.s: the little black specks are the vanilla seeds. Yield: about 24 cupcakesIngredients: 3 cups all-purpose flour 1 tbsp. baking powder 1 vanilla bean, split lengthwise (or 1 tbsp vanilla paste) 1 cup butter, softened 2 cups sugar 5 large eggs 1 cups milk 1 tbsp. vanilla extract about 24 tbs Nutella Directions: 1. Preheat the oven to 350 F and line cupcake trays. 2. On parchment paper (or in a bowl) sift flour and baking powder. Set aside. 3. In your mixing bowl, cream butter and vanilla bean seeds. 4. Add sugar to the butter mixture. Mix in the eggs one at a time. 6. Add the dry ingredients alternately with the milk, beginning and ending with the dry ingredients and mixing just until incorporated, add the vanilla extract and mix well. 7. Divide the batter (using a 1/4 measuring cup) between the prepared paper liners. 8. Drop teaspoon sized dollops* of Nutella on top of the cupcakes. Do not push down. When the cake rises, it will close up on it's on. 8. Bake 18-22 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. * I might have gone a bit crazy with the size of my dollops.. you only live once right? (death by nutella! bring it on!) At this point your kitchen is starting to smell like pure awesomeness. You're thinking that instead of going all the way you'll just shove the cupcakes in your mouth as soon as the timer goes off. As your Nutella Anonymous mentor I encourage you to have patience because 1) you might burn your mouth & 2) you'll want to finish the job. Allow the cupcakes to cool completely before frosting. Aww, I'm proud of you for making it this far into your cupcake making adventures without giving in to temptation and eating the unfrosted 24 cupcakes to yourself. Unless you did...... you did, didn't you. Yields: Probably a lot more than you actually need.Ingredients: 1 c soft butter 1 c nutella 2 c icing sugar 2 tsp vanilla extract 1-2 tbs milk or cream (optional)Directions: 1. Mix the butter and nutella on medium-high until smooth. 2. Gradually add the sifted icing sugar until just incorporated. Scrape the sides of the bowl and mix in the vanilla extract. Optional: if you feel like the frosting is a bit too hard, add the milk or cream. 3. Mix until light and fluffy. 4. Frost cooled cake or cupcakes. *The piping tip used for this cupcake is an 9PT extra large round tip (aka huge round mama). You could very well use a knife or any other piping tip for this. I like big ones. :) I also topped the cupcakes with a hazelnut because they are both cute and tasty. Yay! you've made it! Chow down and enjoy with a tall glass of cold milk. Seriously though, if you can eat more than one, you're tougher than me and might develop diabetes in the coming seconds. I Hope you've enjoyed my first instructable ever! Here is my recipe blog if you're interested:http://www.maries-cuisine.com/

```markdown
# Nutella Stuffed Vanilla Bean Cupcakes with Nutella Buttercream Frosting Recipe System

## Ingredients Input
- 3 cups all-purpose flour
- 1 tbsp. baking powder
- 1 vanilla bean, split lengthwise (or 1 tbsp vanilla paste)
- 1 cup butter, softened
- 2 cups sugar
- 5 large eggs
- 1 cups milk
- 1 tbsp. vanilla extract
- 24 tbsp Nutella (for cupcakes)
- 1 cup soft butter (for frosting)
- 1 cup Nutella (for frosting)
- 2 cups icing sugar (for frosting)
- 2 tsp vanilla extract (for frosting)
- 1-2 tbsp milk or cream (optional for frosting)

## Cupcakes Preparation

### START: Begin Cupcake Baking Process
- Preheat the oven to 350 F.
- Line cupcake trays with paper liners.

### PROCESS: Sift Dry Ingredients
- Sift 3 cups all-purpose flour and 1 tbsp. baking powder onto parchment paper or in a bowl.
- STORE the sifted mixture for later use.

### PROCESS: Cream Butter and Vanilla
- Extract seeds from 1 split vanilla bean.
- Cream 1 cup softened butter with vanilla bean seeds in a mixing bowl.

### PROCESS: Add Sugar and Eggs
- Add 2 cups sugar to the butter mixture and mix.
- Mix in 5 large eggs one at a time.

### PROCESS: Combine Dry and Wet Ingredients
- Add the sifted dry ingredients to the creamed mixture alternately with 1 cup milk, starting and ending with the dry ingredients.
- Mix just until incorporated.
- Add 1 tbsp. vanilla extract and mix well.

### PROCESS: Fill Cupcake Liners
- Divide the batter between the prepared paper liners using a 1/4 measuring cup.

### PROCESS: Add Nutella
- Drop teaspoon-sized dollops of Nutella on top of the batter in each cupcake liner.

### DECISION [IF]: Is Nutella dollop size excessive?
  - Yes: Acknowledge the indulgence.
  - No: Continue to next step.

### PROCESS: Bake Cupcakes
- Bake for 18-22 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.

### OUTPUT: Baked Cupcakes
- Allow the cupcakes to cool completely before frosting.

## Frosting Preparation

### START: Begin Frosting Making Process

### PROCESS: Mix Butter and Nutella
- Mix 1 cup soft butter and 1 cup Nutella on medium-high until smooth.

### PROCESS: Add Icing Sugar and Vanilla
- Gradually add 2 cups sifted icing sugar until just incorporated.
- Scrape the sides of the bowl and mix in 2 tsp vanilla extract.

### DECISION [IF]: Is frosting too hard?
  - Yes: Add 1-2 tbsp milk or cream to soften.
  - No: Proceed to next step.

### PROCESS: Achieve Desired Consistency
- Mix until the frosting is light and fluffy.

### OUTPUT: Nutella Buttercream Frosting

## Cupcake Assembly

### PROCESS: Frost Cooled Cupcakes
- Frost the cooled cupcakes using a piping tip or knife.

### PROCESS: Add Hazelnut Topping (Optional)
- Top each cupcake with a hazelnut for decoration.

### OUTPUT: Nutella Stuffed Vanilla Bean Cupcakes with Nutella Buttercream Frosting

## End of Process Consumption

### DECISION [IF]: Can you eat more than one cupcake?
  - Yes: Acknowledge the challenge.
  - No: Enjoy in moderation.

### END: Enjoy the Cupcakes
- Serve with a tall glass of cold milk and enjoy the cupcakes.
```

instruct00683.title: Restoring Old Sneakers
instruct00683.text: Like many people, I don't like to throw away perfectly useful shoes, especially not Vans that I found second-hand for seven bucks Canadian. This is how I restored them. The right-foot shoe was my control, and the left-foot shoe was my first test. You will need: Your scruffy shoes Some toothpaste A plastic scrubber (or steel wool) -A friend of mine recommended using a toothbrush, but I found that it couldn't scrub hard enough. Put it onto the scrubber and not the shoe. You want the paste, which contains an abrasive (possibly sand), to stay with the scrubber. Scrub like you've never scrubbed before. This requires real vigour. See if you've missed any spots. Then scrub some more. If there is a little bit of yellow that won't come off, don't fret. That's the glue that's holding the rubber on. It seems to become more obvious when shoes are washed. Get a little bit of the toothpaste out of the scrubber. I didn't do this part when I dealt with the other shoe and it foamed up and soaked in. I had to spend a while getting it all out. There's probably some still in there. These shoes had quite a bit of dirt and dust in them. If yours are old and dirty, this step will benefit them. If they're new and you want to preserve the colour, ignore this. It might make them look faded. Rinse rinse rinse so your shoes don't smell like mint (although that might be nice). Squeeze out the water to dry faster. Just like new. The regular toothpaste works great, but I may try this again later on with a whitening toothpaste or a hardcore industrial-strength hand-cleaner.
