instruct00599.title: Chickpea Sandwich
instruct00599.text: If you love chickpeas as much as I do, this sandwich is a great way to eat them. I originally saw this recipe for smashed chickpea salad a few years ago over at smitten kitchen and immediately fell in love. My recipe varies slightly from hers, but can definitely be eaten as a chickpea salad or a chickpea sandwich. I like to take my chickpea sandwiches to the next level, and I'll show you how to do that at the end. :D This is something I make when nothing else sounds good - and it's a fantastically filling work lunch or a quick dinner when you don't want to put much effort into it! one 14.5 oz can chickpeas, drained and rinsed 2-3 tablespoons finely chopped red onion (the more red onion the better!) one lemon salt and pepper to taste one garlic clove, minced 1-2 tablespoons chopped parsley or cilantro, whatever you have on hand good quality olive oil And for a very fancy sandwich - bread, butter, and a little of your favorite shredded cheese. (I use Earth Balance and Daiya cheese, so it's vegan!) Combine the chickpeas, onion, herbs, and garlic in a medium sized bowl. Now, zest your lemon! Try to get as much zest as possible off it - it makes it extra yummy! I've forgotten to zest the lemon a couple times when making this and it just didn't taste as awesome. Squeeze half a lemon over the bowl, being careful to not include any seeds. They can be very hard to see in this mixture! Then, add a good glug of olive oil (probably a tablespoon to start, you can add more later.) Also add a good pinch of salt and a few grinds of pepper. :) Using a potato masher or a giant fork or whatever you can find that would work, mash everything together until you can't see any whole chickpeas anymore. If it seems crumbly, add a little more olive oil to help it come together. :) At this point, give it a taste! I normally add more pepper and more lemon juice. Just keep adding and tasting until you're happy with it. This basically turns into a chickpea grilled cheese - it's super easy if you have a sandwich maker, but it's much prettier if you cook it on the stove. :) Butter two slices of bread and place a little cheese on the first slice. Then layer on a few big spoons of the chickpea mixture, pressing it into place. Add a little more cheese on top and then cook it like you would a grilled cheese. I cook it over medium heat so the outside won't burn before the cheese melts - the cheese melting is key in getting it to turn over without a catastrophe. It kinda acts like glue. If you're not feeling up to it, it's pretty good on plain old bread too, or in a pita. :D And you can eat the leftover chickpea mixture as a salad if you like. Double duty!

```markdown
# Smashed Chickpea Sandwich System

## Ingredients Input
- START: Begin the system for preparing a smashed chickpea sandwich.
- INPUT: One 14.5 oz can of chickpeas, drained and rinsed.
- INPUT: 2-3 tablespoons finely chopped red onion.
- INPUT: One lemon.
- INPUT: Salt and pepper to taste.
- INPUT: One garlic clove, minced.
- INPUT: 1-2 tablespoons chopped parsley or cilantro.
- INPUT: Good quality olive oil.
- INPUT [OPTIONAL FOR FANCY SANDWICH]: Bread, butter, and shredded cheese (vegan options if desired).

## Chickpea Mixture Preparation
- PROCESS: Combine chickpeas, red onion, herbs, and garlic in a medium-sized bowl.
- PROCESS: Zest the lemon and add the zest to the bowl.
- DECISION: Did you zest the lemon?
  - IF Yes: Proceed to the next step.
  - IF No: Go back and zest the lemon before proceeding.
- PROCESS: Squeeze half a lemon over the bowl, ensuring no seeds are included.
- PROCESS: Add a tablespoon of olive oil to the bowl.
- PROCESS: Add a pinch of salt and a few grinds of pepper to the bowl.
- PROCESS: Mash the mixture with a potato masher or a large fork until no whole chickpeas are visible.
- DECISION: Is the mixture crumbly?
  - IF Yes: Add more olive oil to help it come together.
  - IF No: Proceed to the tasting step.
- PROCESS: Taste the mixture and adjust seasoning with more pepper or lemon juice as needed.

## Sandwich Assembly (Optional Fancy Version)
- DECISION: Are you making a fancy sandwich?
  - IF Yes: Proceed with fancy sandwich assembly.
  - IF No: Skip to the Plain Sandwich Assembly or Salad Option.

- PROCESS: Place a little cheese on one slice of bread.
- PROCESS: Add a few big spoons of the chickpea mixture onto the cheese, pressing it down.
- PROCESS: Add more cheese on top of the chickpea mixture.
- PROCESS: Cook over medium heat like a grilled cheese until the cheese melts and acts as glue.
- OUTPUT: A fancy smashed chickpea grilled cheese sandwich.
- END: The fancy sandwich preparation is complete.

## Plain Sandwich Assembly or Salad Option
- DECISION: Are you making a plain sandwich or eating it as a salad?
```

instruct00616.title: DIY Photo Postcards on the Go
instruct00616.text: We love to travel, and somewhere along the line, during past journeys, we've always made it a point to stop and grab some postcards and stamps and whip out quick greetings to loved ones back home. After recently ordering some photos online, via a local drugstore website, I got to wondering about the feasibility of sending personal photos as postcards.For better or worse, there are drug stores and big box stores almost everywhere these days, and it takes all of 5 minutes to upload and order photos, and often less than an hour for them to be ready. If you don't have Internet access at a hotel or lodging, you can order right at the counter.So we gave the DIY Postcard a shot - and have decided this is how we'll do it from now on! What better greeting to send folks, than one featuring you or the family in the place where you're traveling?! Sure, you can send a standard "Wish you were here" postcard, but isn't a "We are Here!" postcard more special?A standard postcard will run you about 75 cents to a dollar or more at a local store, and it looks like all the other postcards for that area. As a matter of fact, you can buy almost any postcard you see at a gift shop online at any number of postcard websites. But your own travel photo? No one's got that but you! First of all, rest assured that sending a photograph through the mail is perfectly fine with the post office! According to the USPS , to qualify for mailing at the First-Class Mail postcard price (currently 35 cents) , it must be:Rectangular At least 3-1/2 inches high x 5 inches long x 0.007 inch thick No more than 4-1/4 inches high x 6 inches long x 0.016 inches thickBy golly, that's a standard 4x6 inch photo! PhotosPostcard stampsA pen I used Walgreens here in Tampa. You can actually order your photos as postcards at Walgreens , for a dollar more than a single 4x6 print, but there's no real reason to spend the extra money, especially when you're traveling and could put that buck towards an appetizer or a park ticket.I ordered a couple of photos via the online drug store photo service, and got a confirmation that they would be ready within the hour. I picked them up while I was out, along with some postcard stamps for 35 cents each. You don't need to do this, but I customized the back of my photo to look more like a standard postcard, running a vertical off-centered line to set off the address area from the greeting area. Then I wrote a cheery greeting, addressed it, stamped it and tossed it in the mail. Without all the extra printing that's on the back of a store bought postcard, there's plenty of space to write, too No complaints from the postal service when they picked it up, and two days later it was back, showing a little wear and tear but no more than a standard postcard. I know I'd love to receive a personal photo postcard from friends and relatives on travels. I'd keep those!Happy Trails!

```markdown
# Making a Mushroom-Shaped Bison Tube

## System Overview:
The system takes a bison tube and transforms it into a mushroom-shaped container using materials such as Polyform clay, a construction screw, paint, and a few other tools. The process involves molding, baking, and painting the clay to create a mushroom appearance, then assembling the parts to complete the transformation.

## Materials:
- Polyform clay
- Bison tube
- Construction screw
- Paint and brush
- Small piece of saran wrap (optional)

### PROCESS: [Baking the Clay]

- COVER a pan with foil (optional).

- INPUT: Preheated oven

### PROCESS: [Painting the Mushroom]

### PROCESS: [Final Assembly]

- FILL the tube with a log for geocaching.
- SCREW the cap back on.

- PLACE the mushroom bison tube in a chosen location and enjoy the finished product.
```

instruct00419.title: DIY - Making of Lord Ganesha at Home
instruct00419.text: I have made my entry for Instructables contest category - HOMEMADE GIFTS CONTEST. Your votes are very valuable. So if you like this craft, kindly vote and help me get through this. I would really appreciate your support.Ganesh Chaturthi, a very famous festival celebrated in my home country - India. Having moved to Florida, I didn't want to miss the celebration without traditional clay Ganesha. I remember watching making of mini-Ganesh in the streets back at home. So here is what I tried to replicate. I really enjoyed making this and it was one of the best Ganesh Chaturthi i ever celebrated. I hope you will enjoy too! Happy crafting!Construction time - 60 to 90 minsSUPPLIES YOU WILL NEED: Clay Toothpick Acrylic paint Divide the clay in proportion as shown in the image. Flatten the base pedestal clay (like the way you would flatten roti dough). Flatten it in such a way that it has space to hold stomach and legs. Insert a small piece of toothpick into one end of the base and fix the stomach onto that. This way these parts will stay together even after drying. Use water when required to brush at places that are dry. Roll out the leg portions as shown in the picture. Press on top and bottom, and bend to form shape of the leg. Fix the legs to the stomach and base pedestal, reinforce it with toothpicks. Press the joints of leg and stomach at the back, so that they become one and joints are not seen. Roll out the hands in the same way as legs and bend them to form the shape of hands as shown in the image. Fix the hands and gently press them to join it with the stomach. Insert a toothpick into the body and fix the head to it. Similarly fix the ears. Roll out the trunk (similar to legs and hands). Bend it and fix it to the head as shown in the image. Gently press the years and flatten them. Make eyes, tusk and 3 tiers of head crown. To make the back crown, first roll and press the clay like roti dough (about 6cm in diameter). Then use tools like bottle/mason jar lid, pen refill, pen cap to do the ornamentation. Allow this to dry a bit and gently fix it to the body by using more wet clay. Kindly check the below link for making of umbrella.https://www.instructables.com/id/DIY-Paper-umbrella...Fix the umbrella skewer to body of Ganesh using clay. Leave it to dry for couple of days and paint them. To make the elevated pedestal, I have used a square thermocol piece (3"L x 3"B x 1"H) and wrapped it with 1" blue satin ribbon.

```markdown
# Structured Summary and Step-by-Step Representation of the Blog Post

## START:
- The process of creating a traditional clay Ganesha for Ganesh Chaturthi celebration.

## INPUT:
- Supplies needed: Clay, Toothpick, Acrylic paint, Water, Tools for ornamentation (bottle/mason jar lid, pen refill, pen cap), Square thermocol piece (3"L x 3"B x 1"H), 1" blue satin ribbon.
- Time required: 60 to 90 minutes.

## PROCESS: [Divide Clay]
- Divide the clay into proportions as shown in an image (not provided in the blog post).

## PROCESS: [Create Base Pedestal]
- Flatten the base pedestal clay similar to flattening roti dough.
- Ensure it has space to hold the stomach and legs.

- Insert a small piece of toothpick into one end of the base.
- Fix the stomach onto the toothpick to ensure they stay connected after drying.
- Use water to brush any dry areas to make the clay malleable.

## PROCESS: [Form and Attach Legs]
- Roll out the leg portions as depicted in a picture (not provided in the blog post).
- Press the top and bottom of the legs and bend them to form the shape.
- Fix the legs to the stomach and base pedestal using toothpicks for reinforcement.
- Press the joints at the back to unify the leg and stomach connection.

## PROCESS: [Form and Attach Arms]
- Roll out the hands similar to the legs and bend them into shape.
- Fix the hands to the stomach and gently press to join.

## PROCESS: [Attach Head and Ears]
- Insert a toothpick into the body.
- Fix the head to the toothpick.
- Roll out and attach the ears to the head.

## PROCESS: [Form and Attach Trunk]
- Roll out the trunk like the legs and hands.
- Bend it and fix it to the head as shown in an image (not provided in the blog post).

## PROCESS: [Add Facial Features and Crown]
- Create and attach eyes, tusk, and a three-tiered head crown to the head.

## PROCESS: [Create and Attach Back Crown]
- Roll and flatten clay like roti dough to about 6cm in diameter for the back crown.
- Use tools to add ornamentation to the back crown.
- Allow it to dry slightly.
- Fix the back crown to the body with more wet clay.

## PROCESS: [Make and Attach Umbrella]
- Follow instructions from a provided link to make an umbrella.
- Fix the umbrella skewer to the body of Ganesh using clay.

## PROCESS: [Dry the Clay Ganesha]
- Leave the clay Ganesha to dry for a couple of days.

## PROCESS: [Paint the Clay Ganesha]
- Once dry, paint the clay Ganesha with acrylic paint.

## PROCESS: [Create Elevated Pedestal]
- Use a square thermocol piece and wrap it with blue satin ribbon to make an elevated pedestal.

## OUTPUT:
- A completed and painted traditional clay Ganesha with an elevated pedestal.

## END:
- The process concludes with a handcrafted traditional clay Ganesha ready for Ganesh Chaturthi celebration.
```

instruct00163.title: How to Make a USB No-data Charger Cable
instruct00163.text: Your USB charged devices can be attacked through the USB port while charging. This has been demonstrated at Blackhat 2013 (https://www.blackhat.com/us-13/briefings.html#Lau,http://www.extremetech.com/extreme/157207-black-hat-hackers-break-into-any-iphone-in-under-a-minute-using-a-malicious-charger) and documented on the web under the general term "Juice Jacking". See for example: http://www.zdziarski.com/blog/?p=2345.How can we protect ourselves against malicious public charging stations or cheap iphone chargers sold on chinese websites? One of the answers is to make a USB cable which can only feed power to the USB device without any ability to transfer data. This is suprisingly easy to do so let's get starting! We will need:a micro USB cable which has a micro USB plug at one end and a micro USB socket at the other end. Purchase at your favorite chinese vendor.duct tapeTools & skills:paper cutterl33t cable surgery skills :) We need to make a short incision along the length of the USB cable using the paper cutter. It can be a bit tricky as you need to be careful not to cut the USB wires and at the same time cut through the whole insulation which can be thick.One way I found that works is to first make a shallow cut and make it gradually deeper until you can feel the knife moving smoothly when it's tip gets to the empty space between the insulation and the wires. In case you are not sure you can do this properly take some old keyboard or mouse cable and practice.Also, it's good to buy two USB cables so that you won't have to wait for a new one when you make a mistake. They are dirt cheap so it's a good idea to have a backup. Open and inspect the cut to see if the USB wires that we care about are not damaged. We have to leave the red and black wires as they provide the power. The other wires (white and green) are the data lines. Simply cut the data wires leaving the power wires intact. Seal the incision with a bit of duct tape. Connect the device to your PC using the cable you've made. If the device starts to charge but the operating system doesn't see the new device plugged in your cable works! How to check if your operating system detects the device or not?Under Windows go and check out USBview: https://twitter.com/abcminiuser/statuses/502313224...Under Linux use the 'lsusb' terminal commandUnder Mac OS X go for the 'system_profiler SPUSBDataType' terminal command

```markdown
# USB Data Blocker Creation Process

## Summary
This process describes how to create a USB cable that allows charging without data transfer to protect devices from "Juice Jacking" when using public charging stations or unreliable chargers.

## Steps

### START:
- Begin the process of creating a secure USB charging cable.

### INPUT:
- Acquire a micro USB cable with a micro USB plug at one end and a socket at the other end.
- Gather necessary tools: duct tape and a paper cutter.
- Obtain l33t cable surgery skills.

### PROCESS: [Prepare for Cable Modification]
- Make an initial shallow incision along the length of the USB cable with the paper cutter.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the cut deep enough to reach the empty space between the insulation and the wires without damaging the wires?
    - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
    - No: Gradually deepen the cut until the knife moves smoothly in the empty space.

### PROCESS: [Practice on Spare Cable]
- DECISION [IF]: Are you unsure about making the incision correctly?
  - Yes: Practice on an old keyboard or mouse cable.
  - No: Proceed with the actual cable.

### INPUT:
- Consider purchasing two USB cables as a precaution in case of errors.

### PROCESS: [Inspect the Cable]
- Open the cut and inspect the USB wires.
  - DECISION [IF]: Are the red and black power wires intact?
    - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
    - No: Use the backup cable and repeat the process.

### PROCESS: [Cut Data Wires]
- Cut the white and green data wires while leaving the red and black power wires intact.

### OUTPUT:
- The modified USB cable should now only have the power wires connected.

### PROCESS: [Seal the Cable]
- Use duct tape to seal the incision on the USB cable.

### PROCESS: [Test the Cable]
- Connect the modified cable to a PC and attach a USB device to charge.
  - DECISION [IF]: Does the device charge without the operating system detecting a new device?
    - Yes: The cable modification is successful.
    - No: Inspect the cable and connections, and retry if necessary.

### PROCESS: [Check Device Detection]
- Check if the operating system detects the device.
  - For Windows, use USBview (https://twitter.com/abcminiuser/statuses/502313224).
  - For Linux, use the 'lsusb' terminal command.
  - For Mac OS X, use the 'system_profiler SPUSBDataType' terminal command.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the device not detected by the operating system?
  - Yes: The USB data blocker cable is working correctly.
  - No: Review and repeat the modification process.

### END:
- The process of creating a secure USB charging cable is complete.
```

instruct00129.title: 3 Ingredient Slime (No Borax)
instruct00129.text: Hello fellow makers! Today I will be showing you how to make this Slime. Please vote for this in the 3 ingredient contest! It would mean a lot to me! Ingredients:Liquid Detergent (Any Detergent with perfume will not work)White Elmer's GlueFood Dye (I used icing dye because that's what I had)Tools:A 1/4 of a cup measuring cupSomething to stir with (The toothpicks)Something to stir inOptional:An air-tight containerOk lets go! Time to start!First measure 1/4 of a cup of glue and pour it into the bowl. Now add a bit of Detergent. Start stirring the mixture together. After a bit you want to add your food coloring and stir that in as well. While stirring it check the consistency with your finger to see if it is to sticky. If it is too sticky add some more detergent. Continue stirring and adding detergent until you have the consistency you want. Everything was going well as it seems. After stirring it enough and checking the consistency you have to knead it to mix it more. Apparently knead doesn't mean squish in your hands. That caused the slime to stick all over my hands. I didn't feel like starting over so if this happens attempt to put as much as you can back in the container and put in some more detergent in until the right consistency. After the fail I put it back into the bowl, added more detergent and boom. The slime was starting to actually feel like slime. Once you are able to put it in your hands without it sticking everywhere start kneading it. (Not squishing it) Roll it around in your hands. If it is still a little bit sticky you can dip your finger in the detergent and rub it around it. If you want the slime to be a bit darker you can make a little bowl in the middle and add coloring in it. Then after that you can knead it in. Yay! You have successfully completed this magic slime! Now you can knead it and play with it.If this didn't work it was probably the detergent you used because not all of them work. Also if you have a container you could place it in there. See you later!Shoutout to tazmmenr for helping me with this project! Go check her insstructables out!https://www.instructables.com/member/tazmeenr/

```markdown
# Slime Making Process

## START:
- Begin the slime-making process.

## INPUT:
- Gather ingredients:
  - Liquid Detergent (without perfume)
  - White Elmer's Glue
  - Food Dye (or icing dye)

- Gather tools:
  - 1/4 cup measuring cup
  - Stirring instrument (toothpicks)
  - Bowl for mixing
  - Optional: Air-tight container for storage

## PROCESS: Measure Ingredients
- Measure 1/4 cup of White Elmer's Glue.

## OUTPUT:
- Measured glue ready for mixing.

## PROCESS: Initial Mixing
- Pour the measured glue into the bowl.
- Add a small amount of Liquid Detergent to the glue.

## PROCESS: Stir Mixture
- Start stirring the glue and detergent mixture.

## PROCESS: Add Color
- Add Food Dye to the mixture.
- Continue stirring the mixture.

## DECISION [IF]: Check Consistency
- Check if the mixture is too sticky.
  - [YES]: Proceed to add more detergent.
  - [NO]: Continue to next step.

## PROCESS: Adjust Consistency
- While stirring, gradually add more detergent until desired consistency is achieved.

## PROCESS: Knead the Mixture
- After achieving the right consistency, knead the mixture to further mix it.

## DECISION [IF]: Mixture Too Sticky on Hands
- Check if the slime sticks to hands.
  - [YES]: Add more detergent and knead again.
  - [NO]: Continue to next step.

## PROCESS: Knead Until Non-Sticky
- Knead the slime until it can be handled without sticking.

## PROCESS: Final Touches
- Roll the slime in your hands.
- If needed, dip fingers in detergent to handle sticky parts.

## DECISION [IF]: Desire Darker Color
- Decide if a darker color is wanted.
  - [YES]: Add more dye and knead.
  - [NO]: Continue to next step.

## OUTPUT:
- The final product is a non-sticky, pliable slime.

## DECISION [IF]: Slime Not Forming
- Assess if the slime did not form correctly.
  - [YES]: The issue may be with the detergent used. Try a different detergent.
  - [NO]: Slime is successfully made.

## PROCESS: Storage
- If an air-tight container is available, store the slime in it.

## END:
- The slime-making process is complete.

- Special thanks to tazmeenr for assistance with the project.
- Visit tazmeenr's Instructables page: [tazmeenr's Instructables](https://www.instructables.com/member/tazmeenr/)
```

instruct00063.title: Grow Your Own Magic Crystal Tree
instruct00063.text: If you found an ad for this instructable in the back of a comic book, it would read something like:"Amaze your friends by growing a crystal tree out of common table salt and a few other ingredients available from the grocery store" Gathering the ingredients is probably the most difficult step. To grow your Magic Crystal Tree, you'll need:- Mrs Stewart's Bluing- Table salt- Household Ammonia (the kind with no soap added)- Cardboard (not corrugated)- Bowl- Water- Measuring spoon- Food Coloring (optional)The bluing is the hardest item to find but can be found in the cleaning section of many grocery stores. You can find the ammonia close by.The cardboard I used came as packing material from a new shirt, or the backing from a paper notepad. Cereal box cardboard might work, but it's thinner & has printing on one side...Depending on the temperature & humidity of your location, the ammonia is optional, but speeds up the crystal growth -- the tree in this Instructable started "sprouting" in less than an hour. Without ammonia, it may take a couple of days to start. For this Instructable, I made a tree formed out of two cardboard triangles, roughly 2" at the base and about 3.5" high. If you'd prefer some form of unspeakable tentacled beasty, send me a picture! Cut a slot from the top to the middle in one piece, and from the bottom to the middle in the other. The slots allow the two pieces to be assembled into a 3D shape. Make sure that whatever shape you create can stand up by itself. If you like, you can add a little color to your shape by putting drops of food coloring on the edges. The food coloring will soak into the cardboard. The "Magic" Solution -- Mix together:- 1 tablespoon water- 1 tablespoon salt- 1 tablespoon bluing- 1/2 tablespoon household ammoniaI put everything into a small bottle that could be shaken to mix the ingredients.Again, the ammonia is optional, but I'd recommend it.Find a place where you can watch your magic tree grow undisturbed for a few days.Put the tree into the bowl and add the solution Wait... Wait a little longer... More waiting... (First sign of growth showed up at around the one hour mark...) The tree after 12 hours. You can keep your crystal shape growing indefinately, by adding more water/salt solution to the bowel. The salt solution is wicked up into the cardboard tree via capillary action. Water evaporates from the surface of the tree, forcing the salt to crystallize out.Mrs. Stewart's Bluing is a colloid -- tiny particles suspended in water (think of glitter in a snow globe, but much, much smaller). The tiny particles make it easier for the salt crystals to form.The ammonia helps speed up the evaporation process, which makes the crystals grow faster.There's a more detail explanation available from Mrs. Stewart's Bluing at http://www.mrsstewart.com/pages/explanation.htm I set up a Canon PowerShot A40 with remote capture software to take one picture every minute. The halogen desk lamp overhead is an attempt to provide a consistent light source, as well as warming things up a little (to speed up evaporation).

```markdown
# Magic Crystal Tree System

## Ingredients and Materials Collection
START:
- INPUT: Gather the following items
  - Mrs. Stewart's Bluing
  - Table salt
  - Household Ammonia (without soap)
  - Cardboard (not corrugated)
  - Bowl
  - Water
  - Measuring spoon
  - Food Coloring (optional)

## Cardboard Tree Construction
PROCESS: Cut two cardboard triangles, approximately 2" at the base and 3.5" high.
- PROCESS: Cut a slot from the top to the middle on one triangle.
- PROCESS: Cut a slot from the bottom to the middle on the other triangle.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the shape able to stand on its own?
  - Yes: Proceed to next step.
  - No: Adjust the shape until it stands.
- PROCESS: Optionally apply food coloring to the edges of the cardboard for color.

## Preparing the Magic Solution
- INPUT: Mix the following ingredients into a small bottle
  - 1 tablespoon water
  - 1 tablespoon salt
  - 1 tablespoon bluing
  - DECISION [IF]: Will you use ammonia to speed up the process?
    - Yes: Add 1/2 tablespoon household ammonia.
    - No: Do not add ammonia.
- PROCESS: Shake the bottle to mix the ingredients.

## Crystal Growth
- PROCESS: Find a stable location where the tree can grow undisturbed.
- PROCESS: Place the cardboard tree in the bowl.
- PROCESS: Pour the mixed solution over the cardboard tree.
- OUTPUT: Begin the waiting period for crystal growth.
  - PROCESS: Observe first signs of growth (approximately 1 hour with ammonia, longer without).
- OUTPUT: Tree after 12 hours, showing significant crystal growth.

## Maintenance of Crystal Growth
- DECISION [IF]: Do you want to continue growing the crystal shape?
  - Yes: Add more water/salt solution to the bowl.
  - No: END.

## System Explanation
- STORE/DATABASE SUBROUTINE: For detailed explanation, refer to Mrs. Stewart's Bluing website (http://www.mrsstewart.com/pages/explanation.htm).
- OUTPUT: The bluing acts as a colloid assisting in crystal formation.
- OUTPUT: Ammonia accelerates evaporation, speeding up crystal growth.

## Documentation (Optional)
- PROCESS: Set up a camera with remote capture software to take pictures at intervals.
- PROCESS: Use consistent lighting, possibly warming the area to speed up evaporation.

END: The Magic Crystal Tree growth process is complete.
```

instruct00287.title: PVC Instrument
instruct00287.text: This is a great and fun to play instrument. I will give you simple instructions to follow so that you too can build your own unique instrument. On mine, there are 3 octaves, plus an extra C. If you plan everything right, it can be easy to build. Special thanks to Snubby J who first inspired me to build one. I used ABS pipe even though I called it a PVC instrument. Here is a demonstration of how it sounds. Shown in photo: -2" ABS/PVC Piping -2" ABS/PVC Elbows -2" ABS/PVC Couplings -Tuner -Measuring Tape -Pipe cutter (a hacksaw will work too, but it makes the edges rough) Not Shown in Photo: -2x4 and 2x10's -2 1/2" Bore -ABS/PVC Cement -Power tools and screws -Castor Wheels (Optional) I used 2 2x4's cut to about 6 feet to make my keyboard. One section was used for the sharps and flats while the other was used for the natural notes. Use the 2 1/2" bore to cut the holes for the pipes. On small gaps, the centers of the holes should be 3 1/2" apart. On the larger gaps, 6 1/2" apart. If starting on a C, space the holes correctly as shown in the picture. The size of your base will depend on how many notes you choose to use. Mine ended up being a little more than six feet wide. With the two keyboard sections, I created two tiers, placing the one with the sharps and flats on top. For comfortable playing, your bottom tier should be as high as your hand when you have your arm bent at a 90 degree angle. I installed castor wheels on mine to make it more portable, to do this, I had to put 2 2x4's side by side on each side of the base so that there was a wide enough space for the wheels. Where the wheels were placed, it is extended out so the instrument does not easily topple. My paddles were purchased online but you can make your own. You need to get closed cell, dense foam similar to the foam used in flip flops, but flip flops are a little more dense than what I have. You can cut up and use the foam from flip flops. Whatever you decide to use, attach it to some sort of wooden dowel or anything you can find that would work. Experiment with the paddles until you find what you like. This is one of the trickiest parts of the whole process. The pipes will hang by the couplings, the pipe is small enough to pass through the hole, but the coupling is too large to pass through. As you add more notes, you will have to add turns to the pipes so you have enough room. Once a note is installed, use the tuner to fine tune it, making minor adjustments to do so. I recommend starting from the bottom because the notes get shorter as you move up. My lowest note was about 8 feet long, which required it to go down, travel across the instrument, then go forward. My highest note was around 1 foot long. I got an equation from nate true that will give you the length of the pipe you need when you plug in the frequency: Tube Length (in) = (13300/(2*Frequency))+(Tube Diameter/2) For the frequencies of the notes in the range of the piano go here: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piano_key_frequencies My low note was number 16 (C2) in the list on the wikipedia page. Remember, if a note is too sharp, it is too short. If it is too flat, it is too long. You do not need to glue every single joint. The best places to glue would be at the couplings or anywhere a joint is bearing weight. When not glued, notes can fall off while playing. This becomes very annoying! You might also want to consider installing something to hold your paddles when you are not playing. Please let me know if you have any comments or questions.

```markdown
# Structured Summary of Building a PVC Instrument

## START:
- Begin the process of constructing a unique PVC instrument.

## INPUT: Required Materials
- 2" ABS/PVC Piping
- 2" ABS/PVC Elbows
- 2" ABS/PVC Couplings
- Tuner
- Measuring Tape
- Pipe Cutter or Hacksaw
- 2x4 and 2x10 wood planks
- 2 1/2" Bore
- ABS/PVC Cement
- Power Tools and Screws
- Castor Wheels (Optional)
- Dense Foam for Paddles
- Wooden Dowels for Paddles

## PROCESS: Building the Keyboard Base
1. Cut two 2x4 planks to approximately 6 feet for the keyboard base.
2. Use one section for sharps and flats and the other for natural notes.
3. Use the 2 1/2" bore to cut holes for the pipes, spacing them 3 1/2" apart for small gaps and 6 1/2" apart for larger gaps.
4. Arrange the holes starting on a C note, following the correct spacing as demonstrated in the accompanying picture.
5. Determine the size of the base depending on the number of notes; the example base is slightly over six feet wide.
6. Create two tiers for the keyboard, with sharps and flats on the upper tier.
7. Ensure the bottom tier is at the height of your hand when your arm is bent at a 90-degree angle for comfortable playing.

## PROCESS: Adding Mobility (Optional)
1. Install castor wheels for portability.
2. Position two 2x4 planks side by side on each side of the base to accommodate the wheels.
3. Extend the area where the wheels are placed to prevent the instrument from toppling.

## PROCESS: Making the Paddles
1. Purchase or create paddles using closed cell, dense foam.
2. Attach the foam to wooden dowels or a suitable alternative.
3. Experiment with paddle materials and design to find the preferred playing feel.

## PROCESS: Installing the Pipes
1. Hang the pipes by the couplings, ensuring the pipe fits through the hole but the coupling does not.
2. Incorporate turns in the pipes to save space as more notes are added.
3. Start from the bottom, with longer pipes for lower notes and shorter pipes for higher notes.
4. Use the tuner to fine-tune each note after installation, adjusting the pipe length as needed.

## PROCESS: Calculating Pipe Lengths
1. Use the provided equation: Tube Length (in) = (13300/(2*Frequency))+(Tube Diameter/2).
2. Refer to the piano key frequencies link for note frequencies: [Piano Key Frequencies](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piano_key_frequencies).
3. Remember, if a note is too sharp, shorten the pipe; if too flat, lengthen it.

## PROCESS: Gluing Joints
1. Decide which joints to glue, focusing on couplings or weight-bearing joints.
2. Avoid gluing all joints to allow for adjustments and maintenance.
3. Ensure notes are securely attached to prevent them from falling off during play.

## PROCESS: Storing Paddles
- Consider installing a holder for the paddles when not in use.

## OUTPUT:
- The final product is a fully functional PVC instrument with a range of 3 octaves plus an extra C.

## END:
- The construction process is complete. Test the instrument and make any necessary adjustments for tuning and playability.
```

instruct00196.title: Easy to Build, Easy to Use, Water Bottle Launcher!
instruct00196.text: Here it is... a simple water bottle rocket launcher that you can build in an evening and play with the very next day. I first saw this design at the Tunnel Mill scout camp in southern Indiana. Kids will have a blast (no pun intended) launching water filled 20oz plastic bottles 50 ft or more into the air, all the while getting their weekly shower! Shopping (enough for 2 launchers)**** PRINT THIS LIST AND TAKE IT WITH YOU ****Go to the hardware store and buy...1 - 10 foot piece of 1/2 inch outer diameter PVC pipe. 8 - 1/2 inch PVC T???s2 - 1/2 inch PVC elbows6 - 1/2 inch PVC caps (you may want to buy a couple of extra T's, Elbows and Caps in case you mess up drilling or gluing)1 PVC pipe cutting tool. Your really don't absolutely need this but it sure make cutting this pipe easier. You can use a hacksaw instead.PVC Glue and cleaner (primer, often purple in color), comes in a two pack. Your neighbor probably has some you can borrow.Go to the auto parts store and buy...2 auto tire valves, also called Schrader valves. The end of them should be able to fit inside a 1/2 inch PVC pipe cap.You will also need...several 20 oz soda bottles. The ones that have previously held carbonated beverages. Wash them out or you may get ants!An abundant supply of water. I like to take a 5 gallon bucket of water out to the launch site.A standup bicycle tire pump.A supply of neighborhood kids with dreams of becoming Astronauts! They will get wet!A nice sunny day! Using the handy PVC pipe cutting tool, cut the pipe into eight (8) one foot sections and four (4) six inch sections. Use a permanent marker and a ruler to measure before you cut. Measure twice, cut once! Put one of the pipe caps into a vice and drill a hole on the top of it that is big enough to fit the tire valve. You will only need two caps with holes in them (one per launcher). Go ahead and insert the valve into the cap from the inside, with the connector facing out. It is now time to take your project outside because PVC pipe glue fumes can knock you out. Lay the pipes out on a drop cloth or newspaper. Read the instruction on the PVC primer and glue! Use the purple primer to clean the ends of the pipes and the insides of the caps, elbows and T's. Carefully apply glue to the pieces and fit them together. You do not have to glue the valve to the cap, air pressure will do that job. This is not rocket surgery (or maybe it is), there really is not much you can mess up. If you do, cut the pipe off and try again. A few inches here and there are not going to hurt your launcher. Let the glue set overnight. Have a break; drink a 20oz soda or two. Gather your launcher, kids, 20oz soda bottles, bicycle air pump, a big bucket of water and excitement and take them to the launch area. Your launch area should be an open field, back yard, cul-de-sac but probably not your mother-in-law's living room. Hook the pump to the tire valve. Fill your 20oz soda bottle 1/4 to 1/3 full of water. Carefully and quickly shove the soda bottle down on the launch pipe. Some bottles will fit on easily; some are going to be much tighter. Hold the soda bottle with your hands and have another person pump air into the launcher. When the air pressure is too great to hold, let go! KEEP YOUR FACE AWAY FROM THE PATH OF THE ROCKET! I told you that you would get wet.

```markdown
# Water Bottle Rocket Launcher System

## Summary
This system provides the steps to construct a water bottle rocket launcher, which is capable of launching 20oz water-filled plastic bottles into the air. The system involves shopping for materials, preparing components, assembling the launcher, and using it for launching bottles.

## System Steps

### START:
- Begin the construction process of the water bottle rocket launcher.

### INPUT:
- Obtain the following materials:
  - 1 x 10 foot piece of 1/2 inch outer diameter PVC pipe
  - 8 x 1/2 inch PVC T's
  - 2 x 1/2 inch PVC elbows
  - 6 x 1/2 inch PVC caps (plus extra in case of mistakes)
  - 1 x PVC pipe cutting tool (or a hacksaw)
  - PVC Glue and cleaner (primer, often purple)
  - 2 x auto tire valves (Schrader valves)
  - Several 20 oz soda bottles, washed
  - An abundant supply of water
  - 1 x standup bicycle tire pump
  - Neighborhood kids with dreams of becoming astronauts

### PROCESS: [Cutting PVC Pipes]
- Use the PVC pipe cutting tool to cut the PVC pipe into the following sections:
  - 8 x one foot sections
  - 4 x six inch sections
- Use a permanent marker and a ruler to measure before cutting.
- Remember the mantra: Measure twice, cut once.

### PROCESS: [Preparing Caps]
- Secure one PVC cap in a vice.
- Drill a hole in the top of the cap large enough for the tire valve.
- Repeat for the second cap.

### PROCESS: [Installing Tire Valves]
- Insert the tire valve into the drilled cap from the inside, with the connector facing out.
- Ensure that the fit is snug, relying on air pressure to secure it later.

### PROCESS: [Gluing PVC Components]
- Take the project outside to avoid fume inhalation.
- Lay out the pipes and fittings on a drop cloth or newspaper.
- Read and follow the instructions on the PVC primer and glue.
- Apply the primer to clean the ends of the pipes and the insides of the fittings.
- Apply glue to the pieces and fit them together (excluding the valve-cap assembly).
- Allow the glue to set overnight.

### PROCESS: [Launcher Assembly]
- After the glue has set, assemble the launcher using the glued PVC components.

### DECISION [IF: Is it a sunny day?]
  - Yes: Continue to the launching process.
  - No: Postpone the launch until weather conditions improve.

### PROCESS: [Preparing for Launch]
- Gather the launcher, soda bottles, air pump, water bucket, and participants.
- Move to an open launch area, ensuring safety and space.

### PROCESS: [Launching]
- Attach the pump to the tire valve on the launcher.
- Fill a 20oz soda bottle 1/4 to 1/3 full of water.
- Quickly place the bottle onto the launch pipe.
- Hold the bottle in place while another person pumps air into the launcher.
- Release the bottle when air pressure becomes too great to hold.

### OUTPUT:
- The water bottle is launched into the air.

### DECISION [IF: Do you have more bottles and want to continue launching?]
  - Yes: Repeat the launching process.
  - No: Proceed to end the activity.

### END:
- The construction and launch process is complete.
```

instruct00711.text: You can easily make a bearings cleaning kit yourself with materials you might have already at home for a fraction of the cost of store bought bearings cleaning kits and you can make under 10 minutes.Cleaning your longboard bearings is a necessity to keep them smooth. You will ride much better with clean longboard skateboard bearings.There are bearing cleaning kits out there you can buy such as Bones Bearings Cleaning kit or Oust Bearings Cleaning Kit for around $15, but with cheap or free (recycled) materials you already have - you can make one yourself. Best of all, you can use it over and over again. The kit is also great for skateboard bearings. Small plastic bottle with a wide enough lid (sample: small Gatorade bottle) = recycleCheap ballpoint casing = one you have lying aroundScissors = you have already " washer = $0,112 x " nut with coarse tread = $0,28" x 6" Bolt with coarse tread = $ 0,46O- ring that fits around the bolt (like 1/16" OD x " I.D x 3/32 O-ring) =$0,22 Take off the lid from the bottle. Cut a small hole in the lid that will fit your bolt. You can use a scissor and punch it in. Slide the O-ring on the bolt all the way to the top. This prevents leaking. You can find an O-ring in the plumbing department at home improvement stores. Slip the bolt through the hole. Take your washer and slide this all the way in the lid. # DIY Longboard Bearing Cleaning Kit System

```markdown
## Summary
This system provides a step-by-step process to create a homemade longboard bearing cleaning kit using common household items and inexpensive hardware store materials. The final product can be used to clean longboard and skateboard bearings.

## Steps

### START:
- Begin the process of creating a DIY bearing cleaning kit.

### INPUT: Gather Materials
- Small plastic bottle with a wide enough lid (e.g., small Gatorade bottle)
- Cheap ballpoint pen casing
- Scissors
- Washer
- 1/2" nut with coarse thread
- 1/2" x 6" Bolt with coarse thread
- O-ring that fits around the bolt (1/16" OD x 1/2" I.D x 3/32 O-ring)

### PROCESS: Prepare the Bottle Lid
- Remove the lid from the bottle.
- Cut a small hole in the lid that will fit your bolt using scissors.

### STORE: Bolt and O-ring Assembly
- Slide the O-ring onto the bolt up to the top to prevent leaking.

### PROCESS: Insert Bolt into Lid
- Slip the bolt through the hole in the lid.

### STORE: Secure Bolt with Washer and Nut
- Slide the washer onto the bolt inside the lid.
- Screw the 1/2" nut onto the bolt until it reaches the lid, securing the assembly.

### PROCESS: Create Spacers from Pen
- Disassemble the pen.
- Cut or saw the pen's casing to create 9 spacers, sanding rough edges if necessary.

### DECISION: Are the spacers the correct length?
- [IF YES] Proceed to assemble the cleaning kit.
- [ELSE] Adjust the length of the spacers accordingly.

### PROCESS: Assemble the Cleaning Kit
- Alternate placing spacers and bearings onto the bolt. There should be 8 bearings in total.

### STORE: Finalize Assembly
- Place the final nut at the end of the bolt to secure the bearings and spacers.

### OUTPUT: DIY Bearing Cleaning Kit Ready
- The DIY Longboard Bearing Cleaning Kit is now ready for use.

### END:
- The process of creating the DIY cleaning kit is complete.
```

instruct00360.title: Coffee Flan
instruct00360.text: Flan is a charming little Spanish dessert! It's easy and fast to make and it tastes sooo good. And if you also like coffee, well then, this recipe is for you! I'll show you how to make traditional coffee flan as well as a few alternatives. Serves 6:for the caramel- 300 g of sugar- 100 ml of water- 4 tbsp of lemon juicefor the flans- 500 ml of milk- 100 ml of espresso- 30 g of sugar- 4 eggs- 1 tbsp of vanilla extract- 6 flaneras or any bowls that you can use in the oven- baking tray If you prefer your flan more creamy, juse cream instead of the milk, same amount. If you can't or don't want to have milk, use any kind of substitute like almond or soy milk in the same amount.If you don't like espresso, just use coffee made another way or use 600 ml of milk and add 2 tsp of soluble coffee to the mixture.Don't have a sweet tooth? Skip the sugar in the flan recipe, the caramel will make it sweet enough! Place the sugar and water in a saucepan and melt it over very small heat. When you sugar has completely melted, take it off the stove and mix in the lemon juice. The lemon juice prefents the caramel from becoming too hard.Pour a little caramel on the bottom of each bowl, then take each bowl and turn it so that the caramel covers the sides. Be very careful, the caramel is very hot, so use gloves or at least a cloth. Set the bowls aside, not in the fridge. Mix the eggs, sugar and vanilla extract in a bowl and whish well.Place the milk anc coffee in a saucepan and heat it slowly. Take it off the stove just before it starts boiling and pour the egg mixture into the milk while whisking constantly.Then pour the finished mixture into the bowls (on the caramel).Preheat the oven on 150 C.Place the bowls on a baking tray and fill the tray with water. Bake for 40 minutes, then take the bowls out of the water, let them cool down completely and put them in the fridge for at least half an hour.To serve just flip the bowl with flan upside down on a plate, the caramel will cover the flan.

```markdown
# Coffee Flan Recipe System Summary

## Ingredients Database:
- Caramel:
  - 300g sugar
  - 100ml water
  - 4 tbsp lemon juice
- Flan:
  - 500ml milk (or cream, or milk substitute like almond/soy milk)
  - 100ml espresso (or coffee made another way, or 600ml milk + 2 tsp soluble coffee)
  - 30g sugar (optional)
  - 4 eggs
  - 1 tbsp vanilla extract
- Equipment:
  - 6 flaneras or oven-safe bowls
  - Baking tray

## Process:

START:
- Begin with the preparation of caramel.

PROCESS: Making the Caramel
- INPUT: 300g sugar, 100ml water
- Combine sugar and water in a saucepan.
- Heat the saucepan over very low heat until the sugar has completely melted.
- DECISION [IF]: Has the sugar completely melted?
  - Yes: Proceed to add lemon juice.
  - No: Continue heating until melted.
- INPUT: 4 tbsp lemon juice

- Carefully turn each bowl to coat the sides with caramel.
- STORE: Set the caramel-coated bowls aside at room temperature (not in the fridge).

PROCESS: Making the Flan Mixture
- INPUT: 4 eggs, 30g sugar (optional), 1 tbsp vanilla extract
- In a separate bowl, whisk together eggs, sugar (if using), and vanilla extract until well combined.
- INPUT: 500ml milk (or alternative), 100ml espresso (or alternative)

  - No: Continue heating until just before boiling.

PROCESS: Preparing the Oven and Baking Tray
- Preheat the oven to 150°C.
- INPUT: Baking tray, water
- Place the caramel-coated bowls on the baking tray.
- Fill the tray with water to create a water bath.

PROCESS: Baking the Flan
- Pour the prepared flan mixture into the bowls, over the caramel.
- Bake in the preheated oven for 40 minutes.

PROCESS: Cooling the Flan
- After baking, remove bowls from the water bath.
- Let the flans cool down completely at room temperature.
- STORE: Place the cooled flans in the fridge for at least half an hour to set.

END: Serving the Flan
- To serve, flip each bowl with flan upside down onto a plate.
- OUTPUT: The caramel will cover the flan, and it is ready to be served.
```

instruct00315.title: Floppy Disk Bag
instruct00315.text: This is a bag I made from floppy disks. I found scads of floppy disks in a dumpster and wanted to make plate mail armor out of it (that is my next floppy project) I found out that a bag would be a great proof of concept project. Here goes...Check out the update (2008) and my new bag: Floppy Disk Bag: Install Disk 2 Drill, hand, regular or trephine 1/8" drill bit Pliers, I used bulldog pliers Floppy disks (CRUCIAL) Links, bits of chain from your local bead store Nails and a plank o' wood A pen Elementary math skills Eg: the ability to count NOT PICTURED The hardware for adding a strap the strap This is the matrix for my bag, feel free to make your own. Also, try to get other colors and incoperate a pattern (I just love the classic beige, black, and blue.) The horizontal is the most easy to drill because it has premarked holes. for one all you have to do is unlock the disk. Then drill a hole in the divots already in place. Insert the links and squeeze shut use your judgment as to where to place the upper and lower holes, just remember that there will be a weak link because there is a weak part of the disk, This will help you drill accurate holes in every disk (you shant need to drill all the holes for the disks that wont be attached on all sides keep this in mind How to attatch the edges. Notice that the top holes for the disk on the left are not the same as the top holes for the disk on the right (the same is true for the bottom holes) this is because I measured and eyeballed and found out where those holes will need to be so I can fasten the peices together when I fold it up depending on how you set up the bag these could be side holes or whatever... use your best judgement. Begin folding and linking at the corners when every last link in the matrix is complete Here is the bag fully formed Keys make good feet for the bag, trim out the inside and glue them on these are what will hold the straps to your bag, these are held on with nuts and bolts. you can find all the strapcessories at your local camping, military surplus or other man-store This side wil be held on by looping it through the metal dealie and securing it to itself with a metal ladder to enable adjustment of the strap Upon initial usage of this bag I got three offers to buy one and also realized that it needed some kind of interior reinforcement to make it able to bear weight easily. I suggest sealing the inside with duct or packing tape to keep problems from arising.Enjoy this newfound skill.

```markdown
# Floppy Disk Bag Creation Process

## START:
- Begin the process of creating a floppy disk bag.

## INPUT:
- Gather the following materials:
  - Floppy disks
  - Drill (hand, regular, or trephine)
  - 1/8" drill bit
  - Pliers (bulldog pliers recommended)
  - Links or bits of chain from a bead store
  - Nails
  - Plank of wood
  - Pen
  - Elementary math skills (counting ability)
  - Strap hardware and strap
  - Keys (for bag feet)
  - Nuts and bolts
  - Duct or packing tape (for interior reinforcement)

## PROCESS: [Design Matrix]
- Create a design matrix for the bag layout.
- Consider incorporating a color pattern with the floppy disks.
- Identify premarked holes on the disks for horizontal drilling.
- Use elementary math skills to count and plan the layout.

## PROCESS: [Drilling Holes]
- Unlock the floppy disk if necessary.
- Drill holes in the divots already present on the disks.
- Use judgment to place additional upper and lower holes, avoiding weak parts of the disk.
- Ensure not all holes need to be drilled if the disk won't be attached on all sides.

## DECISION [IF]: Is the disk being attached on all sides?
- Yes: Drill all necessary holes.
- No: Drill only the holes needed for attachment.

## PROCESS: [Attaching Edges]
- Measure and eyeball to determine where holes need to be for folding and linking the disks.
- Adjust hole placement based on the bag's configuration (sides, top, bottom).

## PROCESS: [Linking Disks]
- Begin folding and linking disks at the corners.
- Continue until all links in the matrix are complete.

## OUTPUT:
- The bag is fully formed.

## PROCESS: [Adding Bag Feet]
- Use keys as feet for the bag.
- Trim the inside of the bag and glue the keys on.

## PROCESS: [Attaching Strap]
- Secure the strap to the bag using nuts and bolts.
- Use metal ladders for strap adjustment.

## DECISION [IF]: Is the bag initially functional and strong enough?
- Yes: Proceed to final steps.
- No: Reinforce the interior with duct or packing tape.

## PROCESS: [Interior Reinforcement]
- Seal the inside of the bag with duct or packing tape to prevent issues and add strength.

## OUTPUT:
- The completed floppy disk bag is ready for use.

## END:
- Enjoy the newly created floppy disk bag and its newfound skill.
```

instruct00152.text: I've been wanting to make one of these for a long time. I finally made my own pattern, and I'm quite happy with how it turned out!! Supplies: Pencil My petal template (see attached file) Thin cardboard or card stock (a small piece for petal pattern pieces) Deck of playing cards (makes 4 flowers) Scissors Low temp hot glue gun and glue sticks Hair clip blank or pin back blank Pom pom, button, or other round embellishment piece for the flower's center. Cut out all your petal pieces. Fold a small tab on the bottom of each petal, and snip a small notch in the center of the tab (up to the fold line). Curl the tops of the petals around your finger. # Playing Card Flower Craft System

```markdown
## Inputs:
- Pencil
- Petal template (attached file)
- Thin cardboard or card stock
- Deck of playing cards
- Scissors
- Low temp hot glue gun and glue sticks
- Hair clip blank or pin back blank
- Pom pom, button, or other round embellishment (about 15mm diameter)

## Outputs:
- Completed playing card flower with an attached hair clip or pin back

## Process:

### START:
- Begin the playing card flower crafting process.

### PROCESS: Transfer the Pattern
- INPUT: Print the attached petal pattern.
- PROCESS: Trace over the lines of the petal pieces with a pencil darkly.
- PROCESS: Flip the pattern page onto card stock with the image facing down.
- PROCESS: Hold the pages down tightly.
- PROCESS: Scribble over all lines of the pattern pieces with a pencil.
- OUTPUT: The pattern is now transferred onto the card stock.
- PROCESS: Cut the three pattern pieces out of card stock.

### PROCESS: Trace and Cut Petals
- INPUT: Trace the petal pieces onto playing cards as shown in the image.
  - Small petal: Trace over the faces of the King, Queen, and Jack (3 petals).
  - Medium petal: Trace near a corner over the number and suit of the 9,8,7,6, and 5 cards (5 petals).
  - Large petal: Trace as close as possible to a corner of King, Queen, Jack, Ace, and 10 Cards (5 petals).
- NOTE: Small petals will be cut from the same cards as 3 of the large petals.
- PROCESS: Cut out all the petal pieces from the playing cards.

### PROCESS: Prepare Petals
- PROCESS: Fold a small tab on the bottom of each petal.
- PROCESS: Snip a small notch in the center of the tab (up to the fold line).
- PROCESS: Curl the tops of the petals around your finger so they hold their shape.

### PROCESS: Assemble Large Petals
- PROCESS: Apply a small amount of hot glue on the top right side of the 10 card tab.
- PROCESS: Overlap with the Jack card tab and press together to glue.
- PROCESS: Continue overlapping and gluing all 5 large petals as shown in the first image.
- DECISION [IF]: Is glue on the last 2 petals dry?
  - Yes: Continue to next step.
  - No: Wait until the glue dries.
- PROCESS: Pull the end cards together to form a circle as shown in the second image.
- PROCESS: Glue the tabs of the last 2 cards in place.
- OUTPUT: Base circle of large petals is formed.

### PROCESS: Attach Medium Petals
- PROCESS: Apply a small amount of glue on the bottom of medium petal tabs.
- PROCESS: Glue them to the tabs of the large petals in a staggered position.

### PROCESS: Attach Small Petals
- PROCESS: Apply a small amount of hot glue on the bottom of the small petal tabs.
- PROCESS: Glue them down onto the medium petal tabs.

### PROCESS: Add Center Embellishment
- PROCESS: Apply a small amount of hot glue on the tops of the small petal tabs.
- PROCESS: Press the center embellishment down into the flower's center.

### PROCESS: Attach Backing
- PROCESS: Apply hot glue to the chosen backing (hair clip or pin back).
- PROCESS: Press it against the bottom of the flower to secure it.
- OUTPUT: Completed playing card flower with an attached hair clip or pin back.

### END:
- The crafting process for the playing card flower is completed.
```

instruct00693.title: ASCII-Art
instruct00693.text: I'll show you how to do great ASCII-Art the very simple way. Sorry for my bad English - I'm German ;) Choose any image from the internet or from your desktop. It should have no background and not too much little parts. Comic-figures work best. For this instructable, I'll choose Homer Simpson. Open a new Word-document and paste the picture into it. You can set the size if you want. Now do a right-click on the image and choose the last option (In German it's Grafik formatieren, I don't know what it is in English). In 'Position', normally move object with text or something like that is hooked. If it is so, click it, that it doesn't move with the text. Right beside 'Position' is another option, Textfluss in German. Click on Transparent. Then click OK. If the picture has moved down, move it up again. Open the menu again and click on the the option right beside Transparent. It should be named Without or something like that. On 'Graphic', set the colors to grey and the brightness to 70. Set the font to Courir New, size 10 or 12. Now type over the image, line for line. For the background simply use spaces. For lightly colored areas use letters like ! or l. For normally colored areas use letters like C, E or F, for dark colored use Ms and Ws. For the edges you can use (, ), V, A, Y, d, b and so on. Try to catch the picture with the letters. When you're done, remove the picture and you've made a brillant ASCII-Art-Document. Take a screenshot, if you want.

instruct00873.text: Hello and welcome to my instructable . In this i will show you How to make an Instructable ( Full Guide).It is very easy and i hope you like It .What Wikipedia Says About instructablesAfter graduating from the Media Lab at MIT, Wilhelm and Griffith founded Squid Labs, an engineering and technology company specializing in design and consulting. Instructables started as an internal Squid Labs project, which later spun out as an independent company with Wilhelm as its CEO. Wilhelm still regularly contributes to the site.A prototype version of the site, complete with the initial content of electronics, cooking, kiting, and bicycle projects, was released in August 2005 at the O'Reilly Foo Camp conference.The original content focused mostly on such projects as building electronic or mechanical devices to solve common problems around the home. The scope of the project has expanded to include a larger array of categories, including Food, Living, Outside, Tech, Play and Workshop. Sponsored categories are sometimes added for companies to advertise a specific topic on the site.The site allows uploading of photos, diagrams, video and animation to help explain complex terminology and mechanisms in clear and understandable terms.Instructables employs a full-time staff, and also has a volunteer group, who feature well-documented articles, welcome new users, and help out around the site.On August 1, 2011, Autodesk announced the acquisition of Instructables.Autodesk released the official instructables app for iOS devices on January 11, 2013. The app allows users to create and publish instructables from their mobile devices as well as view other instructables. Later on, a similar app was released for Android devices and Windows devices. # How to Make an Instructable - Full Guide

```markdown
## Systematic Representation of the Blog Post

### START:
- Open the Instructables website.

### INPUT:
- URL for the Instructables website.

### PROCESS: [Navigating the Website]
- Click on "Share what you make".

### PROCESS: [Creating a New Instructable]
- Click on "new instructable".

### INPUT:
- Enter your Project name.

### PROCESS: [Selecting Channel and Category]
- Choose the channel and category of your instructable.

### INPUT:
- Add the intro picture of your instructable.

### PROCESS: [Adding Step-by-Step Pictures]
- Add more pics of your project step by step.

### PROCESS: [Publishing the Instructable]
- Click on "publish".

### OUTPUT:
- A new page will open.

### PROCESS: [Entering Keywords]
- Enter keywords of your instructable, for example: "Car", "Arduino".

### PROCESS: [Keyword Confirmation]
- Press enter after each keyword.

### PROCESS: [Selecting a Contest]
- Scroll down the page.
- DECISION [IF]: Is there a contest you want to participate in?

    - No: Skip contest selection.

### PROCESS: [Finalizing Publication]
- Click on "Publish my instructable".

### OUTPUT:
- Your instructable is ready.

### END:
- Enjoy your published instructable.
- Request for votes in the contest if applicable.

- Instructables was founded by Wilhelm and Griffith after graduating from MIT's Media Lab.
- It started as a Squid Labs project and later became an independent company.
- The site originally focused on electronics, cooking, kiting, and bicycle projects but has expanded into various categories.
- Instructables allows for multimedia uploads to aid in explanations.
- It employs a full-time staff and has a volunteer group to maintain the community.
- Autodesk acquired Instructables on August 1, 2011.
- Official Instructables apps were released for iOS, Android, and Windows devices to allow mobile creation and viewing of instructables.
```

instruct00054.title: Weight Bench (5 Position,Flat/Incline) Doubles As Patio Bench
instruct00054.text: If you'd like to have a brand-new weight bench, but you don't want to spend a lot of money, then you might consider making one yourself. I decided to make a multi-position flat/incline bench using a 4x4 post as a base. This bench doubles as a patio seat so i don't have to hide/put it away after each workout. Bear in mind that the dimensions of this bench will not be suitable for everybody; it will depend on the height of the person using the weight bench. The bench is about 3.75 feet long which is an average size. The Bench plan can be viewed/downloaded here>>> Weight Bench Plan/Drawing To download a copy, right click then "Save Target As" then hit "Save".NOTE: This built is not designed for serious heavy weightlifting.Materials you need: 4 ft. of 3/4 x 12 piece of plywood or solid wood 3 ft. of 1 x 2 wood 8 ft. of 2 x 2 wood 8 ft. of 4 x 4 wood post 1 (#10) 8" bolt and nut 2 (#8) 3" bolt and nuts 1 (#10) 12" bolt/screw and 4 bolt nuts 8 (#10) nylon washers 14 (#10) flat washers 4-3 inch long lag screws 4 rubber or rubberized feet Some nails and wood glue Wood stain and Polyurethane protective sealant (Optional)Tools you need: Circular saw Miter saw (optional) Power drill with drill bits, Forstner bit and the like (used to counter sink lag screws) Wood chisel Socket wrench/ pliers Hammer Sander or Sand paper Pictured below is the finished weight bench. 1. Cut all wood pieces to the proper lengths (please refer to Detailed Weight Bench Plan/ Illustration). 2. If you've noticed from thebench plan/illustration, a simple dado joint was used to join the bench wooden base and legs. Use your circular saw and make multiple passes to remove the unneeded portion, finish it up using a wood chisel (shown below). 3. Use a generous amount of wood glue to all joints; then secure it with a lag screw.Countersink the head of lag screw to make it flush. See image below. 4. Next, drill a hole through on one end of the (2) 2 x 2 wood (hole should be big enough to accommodate the #10 bolt), this will be used for the adjustable backrest support. Then, drill a hole straight through the side of the bench top support (pls. refer to the bench plan/illustration). Use (#10) 8" bolt and nut to fasten the adjustable backrest support to the bench top. Place a nylon washer in between the metal flat washers to minimize friction during operation. 5. Do the same thing with the swing arm. 6. The (#10) 12" bolt is secured at the end of the swing arm using 4 bolt nuts. Again, refer to the bench plan/illustration where to cut the notches on the bench top support; this is where the swing arm support will rest during use. If you prefer, you can eliminate some notches thus limiting the angle it can be adjusted. 7. Due to proximity of the second notch to the first notch, i use a small metal L-bracket to give it more strength. The second picture shows how it should look like after the adjustable backrest support and swing arm are bolted in place. Note that everything should be flush with the bench top support when in neutral/flat position. 8. Next, fasten the bench seat and backrest using nails and wood glue. Give it a good sanding to remove rough edges. 9. Use rubber or rubberized feet to prevent the bench from sliding during use. After some finishing touches (wood stain and 2 coats of polyurethane finish) this is how it looks like.

```markdown
# DIY Weight Bench System

## Summary Representation of the DIY Weight Bench Blog Post

START:
  - Begin the process of creating a DIY multi-position flat/incline weight bench.

PROCESS: [Gather Materials]
  INPUT:
    - 4 ft. of 3/4 x 12 piece of plywood or solid wood
    - 3 ft. of 1 x 2 wood
    - 8 ft. of 2 x 2 wood
    - 8 ft. of 4 x 4 wood post
    - 1 (#10) 8" bolt and nut
    - 2 (#8) 3" bolt and nuts
    - 1 (#10) 12" bolt/screw and 4 bolt nuts
    - 8 (#10) nylon washers
    - 14 (#10) flat washers
    - 4-3 inch long lag screws
    - 4 rubber or rubberized feet
    - Some nails and wood glue
    - Wood stain and Polyurethane protective sealant (Optional)

PROCESS: [Gather Tools]
  INPUT:
    - Circular saw
    - Miter saw (optional)
    - Power drill with various bits
    - Wood chisel
    - Socket wrench/ pliers
    - Hammer
    - Sander or sandpaper

PROCESS: [Preparation]
  - Download and print the Weight Bench Plan/Drawing.
  - Review the plan to understand the bench design.

PROCESS: [Cut Wood]
  - Cut all wood pieces to the proper lengths according to the Weight Bench Plan.

PROCESS: [Create Joints]
  - Use a circular saw to make multiple passes to cut out dado joints.
  - Finish the joints using a wood chisel.

PROCESS: [Assemble Base and Legs]
  - Apply a generous amount of wood glue to all joints.
  - Secure the base and legs with lag screws, countersinking the heads.

PROCESS: [Drill Holes for Adjustable Backrest]
  - Drill a hole through one end of the two 2 x 2 wood pieces for the #10 bolt.
  - Drill a corresponding hole through the bench top support.

PROCESS: [Assemble Adjustable Backrest]
  - Fasten the adjustable backrest support to the bench top with the #10 8" bolt and nut.
  - Include a nylon washer between metal flat washers to reduce friction.

PROCESS: [Prepare and Attach Swing Arm]
  - Secure the #10 12" bolt at the end of the swing arm with 4 bolt nuts.
  - Cut notches on the bench top support for the swing arm to rest during use.
  DECISION [IF]: Is the second notch close to the first notch?
    - YES: Use a small metal L-bracket for additional strength.
    - NO: Continue without additional bracket.
  - Attach the swing arm to the bench top support.

PROCESS: [Attach Seat and Backrest]
  - Fasten the bench seat and backrest to the structure using nails and wood glue.
  - Sand the bench to remove rough edges.

PROCESS: [Add Feet and Finish]
  - Attach rubber or rubberized feet to the bottom of the bench.
  - Optionally, apply wood stain and polyurethane finish for protection.

OUTPUT:
  - A finished DIY multi-position flat/incline weight bench that doubles as a patio seat.

END.
```

instruct00358.title: Automated Pop-up Kitchen Spice Rack
instruct00358.text: This is a simple Kitchen Automation project. A Firgelli Automation FA-400-12-18" stroke linear actuator was used to pop up this spice rack. Of course the top would typically be the granite square that was cut out originally, and the spice rack could be a coffee machine, microwave, TV, wine rack or anything else you wish to hide in your kitchen. The actuator sits pointing upwards and as you can see the middle of the spice rack has a sort of hollow column, this is where the other end of the actuator fits inside. It's not required if you use the Firgelli Automations column lift which is a ready to go remote control lift mechanism. This customer wanted to have the spice rack lift up from the Kitchen island. 1st thing they did was cut a square hole in the granite top, the granite maker can do that for you. Typically you would use another square piece to fill the hole so that when the rack drops the granite becomes flush with the top lid to look like a single piece of granite The spice rack needs to have a hollow center so that the actuator shaft goes through the center and lifts the top, the bottom of the actuator is attached as shown below. the height is adjusted by propping up the base so that the limits of the actuator are such that when the actuator retracts and shuts off, the spice rack is fully closed. To make it go up and down you need a 12vdc power source and a DPDT switch all available from Firgelli Auto. the actuators are all 2 wire and the power source is too, here is the wiring diagram for the switch.

instruct00826.title: Turn a Photo Into a Stencil!
instruct00826.text: Using just Photoshop, we're going to turn an ordinary photograph into a stencil worthy image in just a few minutes! I was bored today and decided I wanted to make a stencil. Looking through my old profile pictures on facebook, I found a particular one that I thought might make a good stencil. After playing around for a bit, I discovered this process for turning it into a two-color image on photoshop.Keep in mind, you can also use this for silk screening, or any other process that requires a smooth edged image. First we make it into a rough two-tone shape:Load the imageImage>Adjustments>Posterize - You don't want it to look too different. I posterized it to 10 levels.Image>Adjustments>Threshold - Slide the bar around until you see something that looks like a stencil. You have to keep it as simple as possible, for ease of cutting it out, and also watch out for islands that wouldn't be connected to the main stencil i.e. floating blobs. I set my threshold level to 100. Right now we have a very rough, jagged stencil. It won't work well for cutting out with a knife at all. This step is what took me some time to figure out.Filter>Blur>Gaussian Blur - Set the radius to a level that still leaves a distict image, but with evenly blurred edges. 4 pixels was perfect for me.Posterize it again, this time at 2 levels, and you should be all set! I printed my stencil out, and then used a cardboard cutter to cut the stencil out from a shoe box. So far i've only spray painted it onto newspaper, but it definitely turned out well!A few tips:When you print it out, change the color from black to a light gray. It'll save you some ink.This instructable gives some help on making stencils with islands.A light layer of spray on adhesive can help give you cleaner edges when you're spray painting. Make sure to remove the stencil immediately after painting, or it may get stuck!Have fun with your new stencil!UPDATE: I ended up putting it onto a T-Shirt. Acetate sheets (over head transparencies) work well for reusable stencils, so I printed it onto one of them and cut the images out with scissors, and voila! It's drying as I speak.

```markdown
# Stencil Creation from a Photograph Using Photoshop

## Step-by-Step Process

### START:
- Begin the process to convert a photograph into a two-tone stencil using Photoshop.

### PROCESS: Load the Image
- INPUT: Select and open the desired photograph in Photoshop.

### PROCESS: Posterize the Image
- Navigate to `Image > Adjustments > Posterize`.
- INPUT: Set levels to 10 to maintain recognizability while simplifying colors.

### PROCESS: Apply Threshold Adjustment
- Navigate to `Image > Adjustments > Threshold`.
- PROCESS: Adjust the threshold level.
- DECISION [IF]: Does the image look like a simple stencil?
    - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
    - No: Adjust the threshold level again.

### STORE: Save Threshold Level
- OUTPUT: Save the set threshold level (e.g., 100).

### PROCESS: Apply Gaussian Blur
- Navigate to `Filter > Blur > Gaussian Blur`.
- INPUT: Set the blur radius.
- DECISION [IF]: Do the edges appear evenly blurred while maintaining a distinct image?
    - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
    - No: Adjust the blur radius.

### STORE: Save Blur Radius
- OUTPUT: Save the set blur radius (e.g., 4 pixels).

### PROCESS: Posterize Again
- Navigate to `Image > Adjustments > Posterize`.
- INPUT: Set levels to 2 for a two-tone image.

### OUTPUT: Final Stencil Image
- OUTPUT: The image is now ready to be used as a stencil.

### PROCESS: Print the Stencil
- DECISION [IF]: Is the stencil for a one-time use?
    - Yes: Print onto paper.
    - No: Proceed to print on acetate sheets for reusability.

### INPUT: Change Print Color
- Modify the color settings to light gray to conserve ink before printing.

### OUTPUT: Printed Stencil
- OUTPUT: Obtain a physical copy of the stencil.

### PROCESS: Cut Out the Stencil
- Use a cardboard cutter for paper or scissors for an acetate sheet to cut out the stencil.

### PROCESS: Prepare for Painting
- Apply a light layer of spray-on adhesive to the stencil if necessary for cleaner edges.

### PROCESS: Apply Paint
- Use spray paint to transfer the stencil onto the desired surface (e.g., newspaper, T-shirt).

### DECISION [IF]: Is the paint applied?
    - Yes: Proceed to remove the stencil.
    - No: Reapply paint as necessary.

### PROCESS: Remove Stencil
- Remove the stencil immediately after painting to avoid it getting stuck.

### OUTPUT: Final Artwork
- OUTPUT: The final artwork with the stencil design is complete.

### END:
- The stencil creation process using Photoshop is concluded.
```

instruct00674.title: How to Grow Cat Grass
instruct00674.text: Cat grass is something my cats LOVE. It's a special treat for them - we try to keep it around most of the time. It keeps them entertained and happy. :D Plus, it's super cheap and easy to grow! It'll take about a week to get it to a good height, but after that, it's a grass eating free-for-all. More cat pictures on the last step - Big Dee and Luna spent forever grazing when I set it out, and I took waaaaaay too many photos :D a small pot to grow in organic potting soil cat grass seeds plastic wrap water I say organic potting soil because your kitties are going to be eating this and probably digging around in it when you're not looking. Avoid potting soils with lots of fertilizer in them - the cat grass doesn't need it anyway since it won't last long. :) Cat grass can be many different types of seed, but it's typically oats or wheat. You should be able to find it in your local pet store pretty easily! And the good news is the seed lasts forever. The seed I'm using for this is some that was given to me 5-6 years ago by a friend for babysitting her cat. :D Fill your pot with soil, stopping 1-2 inches from the top. Scatter a handful of cat grass seed over the top of this - I like to do one thin, even layer. Then add a couple of handfuls of soil over the top so the seeds are covered with about 1/4 inch of soil. Water the seeds with 1/2 cup of water or so - you want the soil to be nice and moist. Once that's done, cover the pot with plastic wrap (not too tightly - you still want a little airflow!) and set in a warm and dark location - I keep mine on top of the fridge! The second or third day you should see little sprouts coming up from the soil. Check that the soil is still moist every other day or so. As soon as the grass gets to the size in the second photo, take off the plastic wrap and keep in a nice sunny place. I set mine on the back porch so the kitties would not be temped to eat it yet! When your grass is 4-6 inches, feel free to let them have a go at it! It normally takes about a week to get to this size. If you don't wait until the grass is high enough, chances are your cat with destroy is really quickly. :D As the resident cat lady I feel it is my duty. Big Dee likes to put her whole face in the grass. Luna always looks like a crazed murderer when she eats it.
instruct00674.summary:
```markdown
# Cat Grass Growing System

## Summary Representation

### START:
- Begin the process of growing cat grass.

### INPUT:
- Small pot
- Organic potting soil
- Cat grass seeds (typically oats or wheat)
- Plastic wrap
- Water

### PROCESS: Prepare the Pot
- Fill the pot with organic potting soil, leaving 1-2 inches of space at the top.

### PROCESS: Plant the Seeds
- Scatter a thin, even layer of cat grass seeds over the soil.

### PROCESS: Cover the Seeds
- Cover the seeds with additional soil, about 1/4 inch deep.

### PROCESS: Water the Seeds
- Water the seeds with approximately 1/2 cup of water to ensure the soil is moist.

### PROCESS: Cover the Pot
- Cover the pot with plastic wrap to create a greenhouse effect. Ensure there is still some airflow.

### PROCESS: Store the Pot
- Place the pot in a warm and dark location, like on top of a refrigerator.

### DECISION [IF]: Check for Sprouts (Day 2 or 3)
- IF sprouts are visible THEN proceed to remove the plastic wrap ELSE continue to store the pot.

### PROCESS: Remove Plastic Wrap
- Take off the plastic wrap once grass sprouts reach the size shown in the second photo.

### PROCESS: Provide Sunlight
- Move the pot to a sunny location to continue growing.

### DECISION [IF]: Check Grass Height
- IF grass is 4-6 inches tall THEN proceed to OUTPUT ELSE continue to provide sunlight and wait.

### OUTPUT:
- Cat grass ready for feline consumption.

### END:
- Cats enjoy their grass-eating free-for-all.

## Additional Notes:
- Check soil moisture every other day and water if necessary.
- Avoid using potting soil with lots of fertilizer.
- The process from planting to ready-to-eat grass takes about a week.
- Waiting until the grass is high enough before offering it to cats prevents quick destruction.
- Store unused seeds properly as they can last for years.
- Enjoy taking many photos of your cats, like Big Dee and Luna, enjoying the grass.

```
