instruct00299.title: Rocket Powered Glider
instruct00299.text: Glue a micro rocket engine to a balsa glider. This is NOT a launch it entry, I didn't feel like doing the safety stuff, this was done to blow off steam between bouts of statics and statistics homework. A balsa glider super glue micro maxx rocket engines aluminum tape a spring from a pen bamboo skewer Let's skip that part. Then apply a strip of aluminum tape down half the length of the body on the underside. his keeps the rocket from igniting the balsa. These motors come with a proprietary igniter, we start by disassembling the igniter, the two halves are held together with sticky tape. Separate them with an xacto knife and remove the igniter . Now use a spot of superglue to secure the igniter in the rocket motor. Glue the rocket motor onto the aluminum tape just under the nose of the glider, and then, as a launch guide, glue the spring halfway back on the side body of the glider. THe launch rod is a bamboo skewer propped in a roll of solder, should have secured it, oh well. Wires are hooked to the igniter, a 9.6 volt drill battery as attached to the other end and fire happens. Reloads are accomplished by snapping off the old, and gluing on a new engine.

# Structured Summary of Gluing a Micro Rocket Engine to a Balsa Glider

## START:

## PROCESS: Preparing the Glider
- Apply a strip of aluminum tape down half the length of the body on the underside of the glider.
  - OUTPUT: Aluminum tape protects the balsa from ignition.

## PROCESS: Igniter Assembly Disassembly
- Use an xacto knife to separate the two halves of the proprietary igniter.
  - OUTPUT: Igniter halves separated.

## DECISION [IF]: Is the igniter removed successfully?
  - Yes: Proceed to glue the igniter.
  - No: Repeat the process of separating the igniter halves with the xacto knife.

## PROCESS: Securing the Igniter
- Apply a spot of super glue to secure the igniter in the rocket motor.
  - OUTPUT: Igniter secured in the rocket motor.

## PROCESS: Attaching the Rocket Motor
- Glue the rocket motor onto the aluminum tape just under the nose of the glider.
  - OUTPUT: Rocket motor attached to the glider.

## PROCESS: Attaching the Launch Guide
- Glue the spring halfway back on the side body of the glider as a launch guide.
  - OUTPUT: Launch guide (spring) attached to the glider.

## PROCESS: Setting Up the Launch Rod
- Use a bamboo skewer as a launch rod, propped in a roll of solder.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the launch rod secured?
    - Yes: Proceed to ignition.
    - No: Secure the launch rod appropriately (Skipped in the blog).

## PROCESS: Ignition
- Hook wires to the igniter and attach a 9.6-volt drill battery to the other end.
- Activate the battery to ignite the rocket engine.
  - OUTPUT: Rocket engine is ignited, and fire happens.

## PROCESS: Reloading the Rocket Engine
- Snap off the old engine from the glider.
- Glue a new engine onto the glider.
  - OUTPUT: Glider is reloaded with a new rocket engine.

## END:
- The process of attaching and igniting a micro rocket engine to a balsa glider is complete.

instruct00298.title: How to Achieve Miniature Effect Via Photoshop
instruct00298.text: Tilt-shift photography refers to the use of camera movements on small and medium format cameras, and sometimes specifically refers to the use of tilt for selective focus, often for simulating a miniature scene. Sometimes the term is used when the shallow depth of field is simulated with digital post-processing; the name may derive from the tilt-shift lens normally required when the effect is produced optically. (Wiki) Since I don't have the expensive tilt-shift lens and I don't have enough time to make my own lens for the miniature effect, I experimented on some stock photos I have via Photoshop CS4 instead. It's quite easy and it brings you the exact effect you want. Miniature effect has been a popular medium used in commercials lately. But anyway, to get an idea, some cool tilt-shift photography can be seen here. Not all photos can give the right miniature effect. When choosing photos one must remember the following: 1) Choose a picture that was taken from a afar. 2) It is also advisable to choose an image not only that it was taken from afar but rather on an elevated level like you're on 4th or 5th floor of a building taking city streets down below. A good perspective is always a key point. 3) Most of the time, cars, buildings and trees are the best subjects although if you want to take pictures of people, just make sure that there's an element in the picture that would make them look like plastic toy models, for example a building or at least a few cars, trees any structure. For this tutorial I chose one of my favorite miniature effect subject, trains. Take note that I chose a photo that was taken a floor higher than the subject. Open up your chosen image via Photoshop. In my case, I used CS4. After opening the image to your Photoshop press on "Q" to enable Quick Mask Mode. After pressing "Q" you may then press "G" to enable Gradient. Choose the Reflected Gradient for the miniature effect. After enabling "Gradient," draw a vertical line on the picture. After drawing a vertical line, a reddish color gradient should appear which will mark that those part of the image will be the focus or the subject of your picture and not to be blurred out. After determining the focus and subject of your picture, press on "Q" again to exit Quick Mask Mode and go back to Standard Mode. Clicking on this will make the marching ants selection lines appear where our "Lens Blur" should be applied later on. After exiting the Quick Mode, go to Filter > Blur > Lens Blur. Adjust the radius until you reached the desired output and press on "OK." In my case, I adjusted the radius until 40. Press CTRL-D on the keyboard to remove the marching ants selection boundary. Once done with the focus, you need to enhance the saturation of your image. To achieve miniature effect, most of the time, saturation of the images are adjusted to 40 above the normal saturation since miniature models usually are brightly painted. So in order to achieve the desired output, you need to adjust either the vibrance or the saturation of the image. Just go to Image > Adjustments > Hue/Saturation. You also may want to adjust the contrast. To do this just go to Image > Adjustments > Curves. Experiment on the curves until you reached the desired output. Once done with the following just save your image and find your next target image. I wanted to try something with bridges but I don't have photos of bridges taken from above so I borrowed this to try and see how it would look like. Original images of these can be seen here. Anyway, some cool tilt-shift photography here.

```markdown
# Tilt-Shift Photography Miniature Effect in Photoshop CS4

## System Overview
The system takes a photograph as input and applies a series of Photoshop CS4 manipulations to simulate a tilt-shift miniature effect. The process involves selecting the focus area, applying a lens blur to the background, and adjusting color properties to mimic the look of miniature models. The final output is the manipulated image with a tilt-shift miniature effect.

## Process Steps

### START
- Begin the tilt-shift miniature effect process in Photoshop CS4.

### INPUT
- Input a stock photo that was taken from an elevated perspective.

### PROCESS [Selecting the Right Photo]
- [IF] Was the photo taken from afar and an elevated level (like the 4th or 5th floor of a building)?
    - [Yes] Continue with the chosen photo.
    - [No] END the process; a new photo is needed.

### PROCESS [Enabling Quick Mask Mode]
- Open the chosen image in Photoshop CS4.
- Press "Q" to enable Quick Mask Mode.

### PROCESS [Enabling Gradient Tool]
- Press "G" to select the Gradient Tool.
- Choose the Reflected Gradient option.

### PROCESS [Drawing the Gradient Line]
- Draw a vertical line on the picture where you want the focus to be.
- A reddish gradient will appear indicating the focused area.

### PROCESS [Exiting Quick Mask Mode]
- Press "Q" again to exit Quick Mask Mode.
- "Marching ants" selection lines will appear around the focus area.

### PROCESS [Applying Lens Blur]
- Navigate to Filter > Blur > Lens Blur in the menu.
- Adjust the radius to achieve the desired blur effect.
- [INPUT] Set the desired blur radius (e.g., radius of 40).
- Press "OK" to apply the Lens Blur.

### PROCESS [Removing Selection]
- Press CTRL-D to deselect and remove the "marching ants" boundary.

### PROCESS [Adjusting Saturation]
- Navigate to Image > Adjustments > Hue/Saturation.
- Adjust the saturation to be 40 units above normal, or to the desired level.

### PROCESS [Adjusting Contrast]
- Navigate to Image > Adjustments > Curves.
- Experiment with the curves until the desired contrast is achieved.

### OUTPUT
- The image with the applied tilt-shift miniature effect.

### PROCESS [Saving the Image]
- Save the manipulated image.

### END
- The process is complete. Find the next image to apply the tilt-shift miniature effect if desired.
```

instruct00189.title: EASY YUMMY CHOCOLATE CREAM CHEESE PIE
instruct00189.text: I have made this quick pie for last minute guests but it does take at least four hours in the refrigerator to set. It is simply delicious but more so - very quick to make and I usually have these ingredients quick on hand. Most people love chocolate like me and believe me will ask for this recipe after taking the first bite! 2 packages chocolate Jell-O puddings 3.9 oz 1 8 oz package cream cheese 1 tub Cool Whip 1 graham cracker crust 1 cups milk cup sugar Optional: pecans and chocolate chips for garnish Add 1 1/2 cups milk and the Jello pudding mix and stir for one minute and 1/4 cup granulated sugar. Beat until mixed thoroughly. and 1/4 cup of granulated sugar into the chocolate pudding cream cheese mixture. Spread the chocolate mixture in the graham cracker crust. I drop tablespoons of cool whip over the mixture. I melt 1/4 cup chocolate chips and drip over the pie and top off with chopped up pecans. Cool in refrigerator until set at least four hours-enjoy!

# Chocolate Jell-O Pudding Pie Recipe Process

## Ingredients:
- 2 packages chocolate Jell-O puddings (3.9 oz each)
- 1 (8 oz) package cream cheese
- 1 tub Cool Whip
- 1 graham cracker crust
- 1 1/2 cups milk
- 1/4 cup granulated sugar
- Optional: pecans and chocolate chips for garnish

## Steps:

START: Begin the pie-making process.

INPUT: Gather all ingredients.

PROCESS: Add 1 1/2 cups of milk to a mixing bowl.

INPUT: Add 2 packages of chocolate Jell-O pudding mix to the bowl.

PROCESS: Stir the milk and pudding mix for one minute.

INPUT: Add 1/4 cup granulated sugar to the mixture.

PROCESS: Beat the mixture until it is thoroughly mixed.

DECISION [IF]: Is the mixture well-combined?
- Yes: Proceed to the next step.
- No: Continue mixing until well-combined.

PROCESS: In a separate bowl, soften the cream cheese.

DECISION [IF]: Is the cream cheese softened?
- Yes: Proceed to the next step.
- No: Continue softening until it reaches the desired consistency.

PROCESS: Combine the chocolate pudding mixture with the softened cream cheese.

PROCESS: Mix the cream cheese and chocolate pudding until well combined.

DECISION [IF]: Is the chocolate and cream cheese mixture smooth?
- Yes: Proceed to the next step.
- No: Continue mixing until smooth.

PROCESS: Spread the chocolate and cream cheese mixture into the graham cracker crust.

PROCESS: Drop tablespoons of Cool Whip over the chocolate mixture.

DECISION [IF]: Are optional garnishes being used?
- Yes: Proceed to garnish the pie.
- No: Skip to the refrigeration step.

INPUT: Melt 1/4 cup chocolate chips (if using).

PROCESS: Drizzle the melted chocolate chips over the pie.

INPUT: Chop pecans (if using).

PROCESS: Sprinkle the chopped pecans over the pie.

PROCESS: Place the pie in the refrigerator.

PROCESS: Chill the pie for at least four hours to set.

DECISION [IF]: Has the pie set for at least four hours?
- Yes: The pie is ready to be served.
- No: Continue chilling until set.

OUTPUT: The chocolate Jell-O pudding pie is ready to enjoy.

END: The pie-making process is complete.
```

# Char Cloth Creation System

## START:
- Begin the process of making char cloth.

## INPUT:
- Acquire a closeable tin that is somewhat airtight, such as a mint tin or an Altoids can.

## PROCESS: [Prepare the Tin]
- Punch a small hole in the top of the tin using a small nail or similar tool.

## DECISION [IF]: [Is the hole no bigger than 1cm?]
  - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
  - No: Resize the hole to ensure it is no bigger than 1cm to avoid explosion risk.

## INPUT:
- Cut 100% cotton cloth into squares.

## PROCESS: [Place Cloth in Tin]
- Gently place the cotton cloth squares into the tin without packing them tightly.

## PROCESS: [Seal the Tin]
- Put the cap on the tin securely.

## PROCESS: [Start a Controlled Fire]
- Start a calm fire or use a bed of embers which usually works better.

## PROCESS: [Place Tin in Fire]
- Set the tin somewhere in the fire where it will not fall over.

## OUTPUT: [Observation of Smoke]
- Observe smoke billowing out of the tin's hole.

## DECISION [IF]: [Has the smoke stopped coming out?]
  - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
  - No: Continue to observe until the smoke stops.

## PROCESS: [Remove Tin from Fire]
- Once the smoke has stopped, remove the tin from the fire.

## DECISION [IF]: [Is the tin cool enough to handle?]
  - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
  - No: Wait until the tin cools down.

## PROCESS: [Open the Tin]
- Carefully remove the lid from the tin after ensuring it's cool.

## DECISION [IF]: [Is the char cloth brown?]
  - Yes: Cover the tin and return it to the fire.
  - No: Proceed to the next step.

## DECISION [IF]: [Is the char cloth very fragile or crumbly?]
  - Yes: Start over, as the cloth is overcooked.
  - No: Proceed to the next step.

## DECISION [IF]: [Is the char cloth soft, black, and not fragile?]
  - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
  - No: Adjust the process as needed depending on the condition of the cloth.

## PROCESS: [Remove and Separate Char Cloth]
- Take the char cloth out of the can and gently separate each piece.

## OUTPUT: [Final Char Cloth]
- Ensure the char cloth is ready to catch a spark and glow red with a hot ember without flame.

## END:
- The char cloth is now prepared for use in fire starting.
```

instruct00598.title: Basketball Hoop
instruct00598.text: Like basketball & want a hoop? I did but I didn't want to buy one. I looked on instructables only to find there wasn't any. So I made this. It is a fairly cheap way of making a ring especially if you have some stuff lying around. let's start building. Please tell me of any spelling ormeasurement mistakes I have made and I will try to fix them. Don't forget to comment & rate. The first thing you'll need is a ring, I made this out of 12mm (1/2inch )rod but it doesn't have to be that size. A standard basketball ring diameter is 450mm (18inches). to make the ring you'll need something to wrap it around, this should be about 400mm (16inches) as the ring will expand. I found an old rim the right size but you may need to cut a disc out of wood. once you have your formerclampit to thebench. As shown in pic 2 put another clamp just away from the former with the rod in between. as shown in pic 3 slowly pull the rod around, once you have the rod pulled right around and overlapped cut the straight ends off. use a bar clamp tosqueezethe ends together, then weld it together to finish it off put the ring on the ground and bash it flat. bend a piece of flat metal, mine is 4mm (0.16inches) thick. weld it to the flat spot in the ring. cut two rods 320mm (12.8inches) long. weld them as shown in the picture. drill four hole to the size of the bolts you have avaliable. If you want a netball ring you can just bolt this to a post and ignore the rest of the steps. ONLY DO THIS STEP IF YOU WANT A NET ifyou want a net you'll have to buy it, I got mine off Ebay. This step is not as complicated as it looks. 1. cut 12 pieces of wire 90mm (3.6inches) long (I wouldrecommendmaking a few spares as they are easy to mess up.) 2. bend them in the middle(it doesn't really matter how much as long as they're all the same) 3. clamp it along side a small piece off rod 4. bend over the wire. 5. repeat this with all pieces 6. re clamp the wire around the rod 7. bend it over 8. repeat with all pieces 9. re clamp the wire around the rod 10. bend it over (you won't be able to remove these without sliding them of the end of the rod) 11. repeat with all pieces. 12. divide you ring into 12 parts and weld the clips on. cut a bit of board to size. mine isnt full size. (in the second pic there is the dimensions for a standard backboard.)my dimensions are 1100mm (44inches) wide by 700mm (28inches) tall by 25mm (1inch) thick. (it does not have to be this size)mark the centre and mark your holes. once you have all your lines marked on the backboard . put masking tape along them. if you do this well it will make it neat.if your using MDF you will need to waterproof the edges as shown in pic 2paint in the masking tape carefully.pull off the masking tape after you have done enough coats that it looks nice. to start with you'll need to sand the metal clean. I used a sanding disk on an angle grinder. the ring shouldn't be black or white so stands out from the backboard. Normally the ring is orange or red. a spray can will make this a lot easier to paint. joining it all together. bolt the ring to the backboard. clip the net on. this would be great for the side of a shed or house but if you want a pole you can make that your self. I am mounting mine to our patio. I just used real heavy duty woodscrews. A standard Basketball ring should be 3meters(10feet) of theground. I am not responsible for any damage you do to yourself, your gear or your house/sheds. Don't forget to comment, rate and vote. Happy shooting.

# DIY Basketball Hoop System

## START:
- Begin the process of creating a DIY basketball hoop.

## PROCESS: Acquire Materials
- INPUT: 12mm rod for the ring, something to wrap the rod around (former), clamps, bar clamp, welder, flat metal piece, two additional rods, drill, bolts, wire for net hooks, board for backboard, masking tape, paint for backboard and ring, heavy duty wood screws (if mounting).

## PROCESS: Create the Ring
- Wrap the 12mm rod around the former of approximately 400mm diameter to create a ring.
- STORE: Secure the former to a bench.
- PROCESS: Use clamps to hold the rod in place as it is bent around the former.
- OUTPUT: A circular basketball ring.

## DECISION: Is the ring fully wrapped and overlapped?
- IF YES: Cut the straight ends off.
- IF NO: Continue to pull and wrap the rod.

## PROCESS: Secure the Ring
- Use a bar clamp to squeeze the ends of the ring together.
- Weld the ends to secure the ring's shape.
- Flatten the ring by placing it on the ground and bashing it.

## PROCESS: Attach the Flat Metal Piece
- Bend the flat metal piece.
- Weld it to the flat spot on the ring.

## PROCESS: Prepare Supports
- Cut two rods to 320mm in length.
- Weld them onto the ring as shown in the instructions.
- Drill four holes for the bolts.

## DECISION: Is a netball ring desired?
- IF YES: Bolt the ring to a post and END.
- IF NO: Proceed to create net hooks.

## PROCESS: Create Net Hooks
- Cut 12 pieces of wire to 90mm in length.
- Bend each piece in the middle and form hooks as detailed in the instructions.
- Weld the hooks onto the ring, equally spaced.

## PROCESS: Prepare the Backboard
- Cut the board to the desired size.
- Mark the center and holes for mounting.
- Apply masking tape along marked lines.
- Waterproof edges if using MDF.
- Paint within the masking tape.
- Remove the masking tape after painting.

## PROCESS: Paint the Ring
- Sand the ring to clean the metal.
- Paint the ring a color that stands out from the backboard (typically orange or red).

## PROCESS: Assemble the Hoop
- Bolt the ring to the backboard.
- Clip the net onto the ring.

## DECISION: Is the hoop being mounted to a pole or a structure?
- IF POLE: Construct or acquire a pole and mount the hoop at 3 meters off the ground.
- IF STRUCTURE: Use heavy duty wood screws to mount to a patio, shed, or house.

## END:
- The DIY basketball hoop is complete.
- OUTPUT: A functional basketball hoop ready for use.
- Reminder: The creator is not responsible for any damage incurred during the making or installation of the hoop.
```

instruct00454.title: Wicked Easy Bean Salad
instruct00454.text: This salad is really quick, really easy and really really yummy. You will need: 1 can Red Kidney Beans 1 can Chick Peas (akaGarbanzobeans) Tomatoes Italian Dressing ( I like Ken's Light Italian. You want a dressing with a bit of spice, no Hidden Valley crap) Optional: Cucumbers (my favorite, but I haven't successfully grown any this year) Feta cheese or mozzarella cheese. Green Peppers (because I didsuccessfullygrow them this year) also good: Celery, baked tofu, Tuna Fish, green beans....... whatever you want. Drain the beans. (I don't rinse them) Chop up the tomatoes and peppers. Toss it all together in the big bowl. Add Italian dressing, ( about 1/4 C) and toss it together. Eat and enjoy. You can put it in the fridge, and the beans absorb some of the dressing. This is a quick and easy meal, or bring it to a pot luck/ BBQ. It's also really good to take on a picnic. With a little Italian Bread........yum............. Mangia!

# Structured Summary of Salad Recipe System

## Inputs
- 1 can Red Kidney Beans
- 1 can Chick Peas (Garbanzo beans)
- Tomatoes
- Italian Dressing (spicy preferred, e.g., Ken's Light Italian)
- Optional:
  - Cucumbers
  - Feta or mozzarella cheese
  - Green Peppers
- Other optional ingredients:
  - Celery
  - Baked tofu
  - Tuna Fish
  - Green beans

## Outputs
- A mixed bean salad ready to eat or store for later consumption.

## Process Steps

START:
- Begin the salad preparation process.

PROCESS [Drain Beans]:
- Open cans of Red Kidney Beans and Chick Peas.
- Drain the liquid from both cans of beans.

DECISION [Are Optional Ingredients Being Used?]:
  - IF Yes: Proceed to next PROCESS step to prepare optional ingredients.
  - IF No: Skip to PROCESS [Chop Tomatoes].

PROCESS [Prepare Optional Ingredients]:
  - IF Cucumbers are chosen:
    - Wash and chop cucumbers.
  - IF Green Peppers are chosen:
    - Wash, remove seeds, and chop green peppers.
  - IF Feta or mozzarella cheese is chosen:
    - Cut cheese into small cubes or crumbles.
  - IF Celery, baked tofu, Tuna Fish, or green beans are chosen:
    - Prepare these ingredients accordingly (e.g., chop celery, cube tofu, drain tuna, trim green beans).

PROCESS [Chop Tomatoes]:
- Wash and chop tomatoes into bite-sized pieces.

PROCESS [Combine Ingredients]:
- In a large bowl, combine the drained Red Kidney Beans and Chick Peas.
- Add chopped tomatoes and any prepared optional ingredients.

PROCESS [Add Dressing]:
- Pour approximately 1/4 cup of Italian dressing over the salad ingredients in the bowl.

PROCESS [Toss Salad]:
- Toss all ingredients together until well mixed and the dressing is evenly distributed.

OUTPUT [Salad Ready]:
- The bean salad is now ready to be served.

DECISION [Will the Salad Be Served Immediately?]:
  - IF Yes: Proceed to END.
  - IF No: Proceed to PROCESS [Refrigerate Salad].

PROCESS [Refrigerate Salad]:
- Cover the bowl with a lid or plastic wrap.
- Place the salad in the refrigerator to allow the beans to absorb some of the dressing.

END:
- The salad preparation process is complete. Enjoy the salad immediately or after refrigeration with Italian Bread if desired.
```

# TARDIS Card Creation Process

## Inputs
- 1 piece of paper (21cm x 28cm)
- 2 pieces of paper (21cm x 6.9cm each)
- Scissors
- Ruler
- Pencil
- Crayon
- Black pen

## Process Steps

START:

PROCESS: Take the first piece of paper (28cm x 21cm).

PROCESS: Fold the paper down the middle lengthwise.

PROCESS: Unfold the paper.

PROCESS: Fold the paper again with the sides folding in towards the center crease.

PROCESS: Unfold the paper again, resulting in four 7cm divisions.

PROCESS: Fold the paper once more down the center crease.

PROCESS: With a pencil, make three marks along the middle fold at 5.25cm, 10.5cm, and 10.75cm.

PROCESS: Cut on the marked lines, as indicated in the reference picture.

PROCESS: Open the paper to reveal the cuts made, resembling the image shown.

PROCESS: Take the two strips of paper (21cm x 6.9cm each).

PROCESS: Weave the strips through the cuts in the first piece of paper, alternating in and out.

DECISION [IF]: Is the card decorated?
    If No: 
        PROCESS: Decorate or paint the card as desired using crayons and a black pen.
    If Yes: 
        OUTPUT: Proceed to the next step.

PROCESS: Write a personal message on the card.

END: The TARDIS card is now complete and ready to be sent to someone special.
```

instruct00628.title: How to Calibrate the Extruder on Your 3d Printer
instruct00628.text: If you're one of the many who have bought into the 3d printing craze you've probably realized they require a great deal of tinkering to get optimum results. I'll show you how to calibrate the extruder in order to get better quality prints. As you can see by the printed table above, a poorly calibrated extruder can have adverse effects on your prints. These easy to follow instructions are great for beginners because all you need is about 20 minutes and some basic tools. These instructions will be shown for a Solidoodle 2 but will work for any RepRap using Repetier Host. The best part is, they require no permanent modifications. Lets get started! Gather the following Materials: - A No. 1 Philips Screwdriver - Metric Caliper ( Metric ruler will also work) - Sharpie or other marker - Pen and Paper - 3d Printer - Computer Optional - Drinking Straw - Scissors Remove the screws holding the cover on. This step may not be applicable for everyone. If you have a Solidoodle there are 4 screws. There will be two on each side, towards the front-bottom. There will also be two screws at each bottom corner at the rear. Carefully remove these four screws and lift the cover straight up with a slight tilt to the rear. At this point you should also have your printer powered and connected to Repetier Host. Under the Manual Control tab click "Heat Extruder". This will save you from having to wait for it to heat up later. Mark a 100mm segment on the filament. This can easilybe achievedwith a 100mm length of drinking straw or a steady hand. Take note whether the top or bottom of the mark signifies the correct length. Set Extrude length to "1" and click the down arrow until your bottom mark is lined up with the top of the extruder [this can mean top of mark or bottom depending on your measurement/mark technique]. In my picture you'll notice the top of the mark is level with the extruder. Set extrude length to 100 and click the down arrow. If everything is working properly the top mark which is 100 mm above the bottom mark should be lined up with the top of the extruder. Mark the filament at the top of the extruder and measure the difference between the two marks[This may require pushing the up arrow to reverse your extruder]. If the original mark you made is lined up with the top of the extruder, skip to step 9. Click on Config, then EEPROM Settings[this will be at the top of the window]. On the first line you will see "Steps per mm". All the way to the right you will see "E:" then a number. This number is the number of steps your extruder stepper takes to extrude 1mm of filament. Create a ratio from the expected extrusion length [100mm] and the actual extrusion length [105.03mm]. (expected length) x steps = (actual length) x new steps We know three of these numbers so we can easily solve for the new steps. This will tell us the amount of steps the extruder must actually take in order to extrude 1mm. We extrude 100mm for the test because the greater length amplifies the minute error. A simpler form of the ratio is New steps= (100*113.68)/105.03New Steps=107.958 Type the new number in Steps per mm: and click save to EEPROM Clean up the mess from the extruder. And re-assemble your printer. If you followed these steps correctly you should be producing much better prints. As you can see below the extra 5mm measured makes a tremendous difference. If you were to repeat these instructions from step one you should get no leftover extrusion when you extrude 100mm.

# Extruder Calibration Guide for 3D Printers

## Summary Representation

### START:
- Begin the extruder calibration process.

### INPUT: Gather Materials
- No. 1 Philips Screwdriver
- Metric Caliper or Metric Ruler
- Sharpie or other Marker
- Pen and Paper
- 3D Printer
- Computer with Repetier Host installed
- Optional: Drinking Straw, Scissors

### PROCESS: Access the Extruder
- DECISION [IF]: Is the printer model a Solidoodle?
  - Yes: Remove four screws from the printer cover.
  - No: Skip to the next step.

### PROCESS: Prepare Printer Software
- Power on the 3D Printer and connect it to Repetier Host.
- Under the Manual Control tab, click "Heat Extruder".

### INPUT: Mark the Filament
- Use a drinking straw or a steady hand to mark a 100mm segment on the filament.

### PROCESS: Align Filament Mark with Extruder
- Set Extrude length to "1" in Repetier Host.
- Click the down arrow until the bottom mark aligns with the top of the extruder.

### PROCESS: Extrude Filament
- Set extrude length to "100" in Repetier Host.
- Click the down arrow to extrude.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the top mark aligned with the top of the extruder after extruding?
  - Yes: Move to the cleanup step.
  - No: Mark the filament at the top of the extruder and measure the difference.

### PROCESS: Calculate New Steps per mm
- Click on Config, then EEPROM Settings in Repetier Host.
- Note the "Steps per mm" value next to "E:".
- Create a ratio from the expected extrusion length (100mm) to the actual extrusion length.
- OUTPUT: Calculate the new steps per mm value.

### PROCESS: Update Firmware Settings
- Type the new steps per mm value into the EEPROM Settings.
- Click save to EEPROM.

### PROCESS: Cleanup and Reassemble
- Clean up any extrusion mess.
- Reassemble the printer if necessary.

### DECISION [IF]: Were the steps followed correctly?
  - Yes: OUTPUT: The printer should now produce better quality prints.
  - No: Repeat the instructions from the beginning.

### END:
- The extruder calibration process is complete.
```

instruct00779.title: DIY Carbon Tape Heated Vest
instruct00779.text: diy heated clothing kit The pattern made from some factory vest. 6 meters of carbon heating flex tape from www.carbonheater.us and now on Amazon placed on back and both sides. By touch carbon is a little bit like a loose weave silk. It's very soft but strong enough. Because of big length it provides uniform heating of body. Back. Front. Tape connected in parallel 6x1m. It takes about 3A under 12V (36W). You can sew wire to carbon tape to make a good and flexible connection. The contact place shouldn't be hotter than the tape itself. If not you must increase the contact area. The best idea to place wire between two layers of carbon tape. Contacts may be sewed by sewing machine or just wraped with a wire. But as you can see sewed contact is colder than the tape itself (left contact). Wraped contact (on the right) is more hotter than tape. Carbon tape can be extended. Place two pieces of carbon tape together on each other with little overlap and sew it on. As you can see the connection place is not hotter than the tape itself. Sewed contact very flexible. It's powered by 6x18650 connected in parallel (2x3). I use it with an adjustable controller. With a half power. I use it with my heated gloves and insoles.

# DIY Heated Clothing Kit

## System Overview
The system is designed to create a DIY heated clothing kit using carbon heating flex tape to provide uniform heating to a vest. The system is powered by a 12V source and is regulated by an adjustable controller, which can also be used with heated gloves and insoles.

### System Inputs:
- Factory vest pattern
- 6 meters of carbon heating flex tape
- 12V power source (6x18650 batteries connected in parallel 2x3 configuration)
- Adjustable controller
- Sewing materials (sewing machine, wire, etc.)

### System Outputs:
- Heated clothing with uniform body heating
- Sewed or wrapped connections for the carbon tape

## Step-by-Step Process Representation

### START:
- Begin with a factory vest pattern.

### PROCESS: Prepare the Heating Element
- INPUT: Take 6 meters of carbon heating flex tape.

### PROCESS: Arrange the Tape
- Place the carbon tape on the back and both sides of the vest.

### PROCESS: Connect the Tape
- Connect the tape in parallel configuration (6x1m strips).

### OUTPUT: Confirm Power Consumption
- Ensure the tape takes about 3A under 12V (36W).

### DECISION [IF]: Check Connection Heat
- IF the contact place is hotter than the tape itself, THEN proceed to PROCESS: Increase Contact Area.
- ELSE, proceed to PROCESS: Place Wire.

### PROCESS: Increase Contact Area
- Increase the contact area to reduce heat at the connection point.

### PROCESS: Place Wire
- Place the wire between two layers of carbon tape for optimal connection.

### DECISION [IF]: Choose Connection Method
- IF the sewed contact is preferred, THEN proceed to PROCESS: Sew Contact.
- ELSE, proceed to PROCESS: Wrap Contact.

### PROCESS: Sew Contact
- Sew contacts by sewing machine.

### OUTPUT: Verify Contact Temperature
- Ensure that the sewed contact is colder than the tape itself.

### PROCESS: Wrap Contact
- Wrap contacts with a wire.

### OUTPUT: Verify Contact Temperature
- Ensure that the wrapped contact is not hotter than the tape.

### PROCESS: Extend Carbon Tape
- Overlap two pieces of carbon tape and sew them together.

### OUTPUT: Check Connection Flexibility and Temperature
- Confirm that the connection place is not hotter than the tape and that the sewed contact is very flexible.

### PROCESS: Assemble Power Source
- INPUT: Assemble 6x18650 batteries in parallel (2x3).

### PROCESS: Attach Controller
- Use the vest with an adjustable controller.

### DECISION [IF]: Set Power Level
- IF half power is desired, THEN set the controller to half power.

### PROCESS: Integrate Additional Heated Accessories
- Use the system with heated gloves and insoles if desired.

### END:
- The DIY heated clothing kit is now ready for use.
```

instruct00589.title: JOE ON THE GO BRACELETS
instruct00589.text: These personalized accessories contain a serving size dose of your favorite instant coffee or drink mix. They are perfect for a busy office setting, or after a workout in the gym. When you use your "joe on the go bracelet" having a hot cup of joe, or an ice cold flavored water, is just an arms length away! NOTE: You may be thinking, "why not just use your pockets?" Well simply because in a lot of business attire and exercise wear there are NO pockets. :) Plus it's just fun! You'll need very few things for this project: ~ Your favorite coffee/drink mix ~ 1 condiment bottle ~ 1 dowel rod 3/16" ~ Airline Tubing Optional: Decorations to disguise your tubing. (ribbon & embellishments) TOOLS hot glue for decorations bolt cutters (to cut dowel) 1. Cut a length of tubing long enough to go around your wrist. (This will hold about 1 serving) If you want to really "load up" you can cut a length long enough to wrap around the wrist a few times, or make a necklace version. 2. Cut about a 1 inch piece of the dowel rod to be the "cork" on the bracelet. 3. OPTIONAL: Decorate it by hot glue a strip of ribbon down the length of the tubing, rolling it up, and gluing it closed. Then you can add your embellishments as you wish. NOTE: The following steps are down without decorations so you can see things clearly. 4. Push your "cork" piece into one end of the tubing about half way. 5. Fill your condiment bottle up with your mix. It should be fairly fine.(The coffee crystals may need to be ground a little more) 6. Holding your tube in one hand and the bottle in the other slowly fill your bracelet. Try to leave about 1/2" clearance from the top. 7. Once your bracelet is full, put it around your wrist and slide the open end of the tubing over the other half of the "cork" NOW YOUR OFF AND RUNNING! ~ To use your "joe on the go bracelet" simply pop one of the ends of the "cork" and dump your coffee into a mug of hot water, or your drink mix into an ice cold bottle of water. (which ever you've prepared for) When dumping the mix it is bestto keep the tube straight & to pour at some distance above the cup to prevent any condensation at the end of the tube. You can roll the tube a little between your fingers if you feel it is sticking a bit. ~ Snap your now empty bracelet back onto your wrist and drink up! NOTE: To clean it at home just remove the plug and rinse water through it until the water runs clear. Set it out to dry before next use.

instruct00854.title: Simple Fruit Fly Trap
instruct00854.text: In this Instructable learn how to make a simple fruit fly trap. Summer time is wonderful but pesky fruit flies can be super annoying. This trap is super effective and you probably already have all the materials needed. You will need:Piece of paper Balsamic vinegar or cider vinegar (actually any type will work but these are the most common) Tall glass Tape Scissors Here is a video of the trap in action and how to construct it. Take the piece of paper and roll it into a cone. The cone needs to be wide enough at the top so it does not fall into the rim of the glass but not so long that the tip of the cone touches the bottom of the glass. The bottom of the cone should be a sharp point but with a tiny opening, if there is no opening you can cut one. The opening only needs to be 1 mm in diameter.Pour a tiny amount of the balsamic vinegar into the glass, you only need a tiny bit, this will be the bait for the fruit flies. Place the cone in the glass making sure the tip does not touch the vinegar, it make take a few tries until you get the sizing correct. Push down on the cone to ensure a tight fit around the rim of the glass and paper or else the flies could have an escape route. Put the finished trap where you have a problem with fruit flies. It will passively start catching them, once they fly down into the cone and out through the tiny opening they will not be able to find their way out.See the pics of the trap after being left out over night. Make a bunch and place them around your house to keep the flies in control.

instruct00703.title: How to Make Playdough (Play-doh)
instruct00703.text: Playdough (aka Play-doh) is easy to make at home, and fun for kids of all ages. Here's how to make your own non-toxic toy with custom colors and fragrances. This is the classic method that involves a bit of cooking on the stovetop - I prefer it because cooked playdough has a better texture than uncooked varieties. If you want the kids to be able to do it all themselves, try this uncooked playdough recipe.Warning: Keep away from dogs and other pets. Playdough smells like people food but contains lots of salt, and a hungry dog can eat enough to cause a dangerous salt imbalance. Playdough is a classic childhood toy everyone can have fun with, and it's so easy to make at home you'll never buy that stinky store variety again.Basic ingredient ratios: 2 cups flour 2 cups warm water 1 cup salt 2 Tablespoons vegetable oil 1 Tablespoon cream of tartar (optional for improved elasticity)food coloring (liquid, powder, or unsweetened Kool-Aid or similar drink mix) scented oils Mix all of the ingredients together, and stir over low heat. The dough will begin to thicken until it resembles mashed potatoes. When the dough pulls away from the sides and clumps in the center, as shown below, remove the pan from heat and allow the dough to cool enough to handle.IMPORTANT NOTE: if your playdough is still sticky, you simply need to cook it longer! Keep stirring and cooking until the dough is dry and feels like playdough. I've gotten many comments asking about sticky dough, so please just keep cooking a bit longer and it will work! Turn the dough out onto a clean counter or silicone mat, and knead vigorously until it becomes silky-smooth. Divide the dough into balls for coloring.Make a divot in the center of the ball, and drop some food coloring1 in. Fold the dough over, working the food color through the body of the playdough, trying to keep the raw dye away from your hands and the counter. You could use gloves, a big ziplock bag, or plastic wrap at this stage to keep your hands clean- only the concentrated dye will color your skin, so as soon as it's worked in bare hands are fine.Work the dye through, adding more as necessary to achieve your chosen color.1 If you use Kool-Aid or similar unsweetened drink mix for color, test on a small ball first- it won't go as far as the "real" food coloring. Play with your playdough- I really don't need to help you there. It's entirely edible, if a bit salty, so it's kid-safe. When you're done, store your playdough in an air-tight container. - If it begins to dry out, you can knead a bit of water in again to soften the dough back to useability. Once it's dried past a certain point, however, you'll just have to start over; thankfully it's not terribly difficult. - If it gets soggy, you can re-heat it to drive off the extra water the dough absorbed overnight. This is usually the result of high humidity, but is fixable! You can also bake it in the oven to make hard dough figures and ornaments, then paint or otherwise decorate the surface. One of the comments below even suggests using baked play-dough as a salt lick for your pet rabbit! (thanks, redcore4!)

# Homemade Playdough System

## Ingredients and Materials
- 2 cups flour
- 2 cups warm water
- 1 cup salt
- 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
- 1 tablespoon cream of tartar (optional)
- Food coloring (liquid, powder, or unsweetened drink mix)
- Scented oils (optional)
- Stovetop
- Cooking pan
- Stirring spoon
- Clean counter or silicone mat for kneading
- Airtight container for storage

## Process Steps

### START:
- Begin the process of making homemade playdough.

### PROCESS: Mix Basic Ingredients
- INPUT: Measure and pour 2 cups of flour, 2 cups of warm water, 1 cup of salt, 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil, and 1 tablespoon of cream of tartar (if using) into a cooking pan.

### PROCESS: Heat and Stir
- Stir the mixture over low heat.

### DECISION: Is Dough Thickening?
- IF YES: Proceed to next step.
- IF NO: Continue stirring over low heat.

### DECISION: Has Dough Clumped in Center?
- IF YES: Remove pan from heat.
- IF NO: Continue heating and stirring.

### DECISION: Is Dough Still Sticky?
- IF YES: Keep stirring and cooking.
- IF NO: Move to cooling step.

### PROCESS: Cool the Dough
- OUTPUT: Allow the dough to cool until it is safe to handle.

### PROCESS: Knead the Dough
- Turn the dough onto a clean counter or silicone mat.
- Knead vigorously until the dough becomes silky-smooth.

### PROCESS: Divide for Coloring
- Divide the dough into balls for coloring.

### INPUT: Add Color
- Make a divot in the center of the ball and add food coloring or drink mix.

### PROCESS: Work in the Color
- Fold the dough over the color, working it through to achieve the desired hue.
- Use gloves, a bag, or plastic wrap to avoid staining hands if necessary.

### DECISION: Is Desired Color Achieved?
- IF YES: Proceed to play with playdough.
- IF NO: Add more color and continue working it in.

### OUTPUT: Playdough Ready
- Play with the freshly made playdough.

### PROCESS: Store Playdough
- Store the playdough in an airtight container when not in use.

### DECISION: Is Playdough Drying Out?
- IF YES: Knead in a bit of water to soften.
- IF NO: Continue to store as is.

### DECISION: Has Playdough Become Soggy?
- IF YES: Re-heat to remove excess moisture or bake if desired.
- IF NO: Continue to store as is.

### END:
- The process of making and maintaining homemade playdough is complete.
```

instruct00448.title: DIY Swirly Paper Flowers
instruct00448.text: I found instructables more than a year ago while I was searching for paper flower tutorials and I was amazed to find out all these amazing flower tutorials in this site. After a long time I've finally decided to post a paper flower ible as soon as I saw these paper flowers on a facebook page. I wasn't sure what to name this flower, though it looked quite similar to Saccharumspontaneum (kans grass), but as this flower has a lot of swirls I named it 'swirly paper flower'. They're really easy and fun to make, hope you like'em! To make this flower you'll need: Colored paper, Customized colored paper, Scissor, Glue. You can use single colored (usual craft paper) papers for making these flowers but I liked using the customized colored papers for making them. You can paint the papers with the colors of your choice and create beautiful shades to make the flowers look prettier. First, you have to cut the colored paper into strips of at least 2 inches width and length of your choice, I kept the paper strips 2 X 8 inches. Make a thin fold along any one of the vertical edges (of the strips). You can fold the paper strip into half to save your time cutting fringes on it, Cut the paper strip horizontally, but not all the way through. Leave 1 cm of the strip along the vertical edges, or more clearly leave the thin folded area (the vertical fold made in step 1) intact. Try to cut all the fringes equally, no pressure, I'm sure you can do it, Also try to keep the fringes as thin as possible, the thinner the fringes the prettier the flower :) Now that you're done cutting fringes along the vertical edges it's time to roll the thin strips (fringes) into swirly patterns. Start rolling each strip from its end and all the way through the other end, which means use the whole strip (fringe) to make a swirly pattern. This is the only step which takes time but it's the most important step. Roll each strip one by one and make sure the swirls turn out fine. Take your time and make the swirls carefully, I'm telling you it's worth it :) Before making the flower you'll have to make a stem for the flower. Use green paper for making the stem. Cut a long strip (2 X 10 inches) of green craft paper, start rolling the paper diagonally from any one end (corner) and keep rolling the paper till you reach the other end. Apply a small amount of glue on both ends of the rolled paper to make sure the roll is secure. Take the swirly-fringed paper and apply glue along the intact part of the swirly-fringed paper- see the first picture of this step to be more clear about on which part to apply the glue.Wrap the glued area of the swirly-fringed paper on the green rolled paper (stem), Start gluing it from the top of the stem carefully rolling it towards the bottom of the stem. Keep rolling (and gluing) until the swirly paper ends. You'll be happy to see how pretty the flower turns out! Use green craft papers for making the leaves. Cut a small piece ( 2 X 3 inches) green paper, Fold the paper in 1 cm accordion fold, Cut any one side into a pointy shape, Unfold the paper and glue it around the stem, below the paper flower. Done! Make as many as you want (or can!), use different beautiful colors. Paper crafts are always amazing and this was a fun one! You can also find a video tutorial of making this flower by deba, click here to find out. Enjoy!
instruct00448.summary:
```markdown
# Swirly Paper Flower Creation Process

## START:
- Begin the process of creating a swirly paper flower.

## INPUT:
- Gather materials: colored paper, customized colored paper, scissors, and glue.

## PROCESS: [Prepare the Paper]
- Cut colored paper into strips of at least 2 inches in width and a length of your choice, recommended 2 X 8 inches.
- Make a thin fold along one of the vertical edges of the strips.
- Fold the paper strip in half to facilitate the next step of cutting fringes.

## PROCESS: [Cutting Fringes]
- Cut the paper strip horizontally to create fringes, stopping 1 cm before the vertical edge to leave the thin folded area intact.
- Ensure fringes are cut equally and as thin as possible for a prettier flower.

## PROCESS: [Creating Swirls]
- Roll each fringe from one end to the other to create a swirly pattern.
- Take time to carefully make the swirls, as this is a crucial step for the flower's appearance.

## PROCESS: [Making the Stem]
- Cut a long strip (2 X 10 inches) of green craft paper for the stem.
- Roll the paper diagonally from one corner to the other.
- Apply glue to both ends to secure the roll.

## PROCESS: [Assembling the Flower]
- Apply glue along the intact part of the swirly-fringed paper.
- Wrap the glued area of the swirly-fringed paper around the green rolled paper (stem) from the top to the bottom.

## OUTPUT:
- A completed swirly paper flower with a stem.

## PROCESS: [Making the Leaves]
- Cut a small piece (2 X 3 inches) of green paper for the leaves.
- Fold the paper in a 1 cm accordion fold.
- Cut one side of the folded paper into a pointy shape to form leaves.

## PROCESS: [Attaching the Leaves]
- Unfold the paper leaves.
- Apply glue and attach them around the stem, below the paper flower.

## OUTPUT:
- A finished swirly paper flower with leaves.

## DECISION: [Make More Flowers?]
  - IF Yes: Repeat the process for each additional flower.
  - ELSE No: Proceed to the end of the process.

## END:
- The creation of swirly paper flowers is complete.
- Enjoy the paper crafts and make as many flowers as desired, experimenting with different colors.
```

instruct00576.title: Computer-controlled Music-synchronized Flashing Christmas Tree Lights
instruct00576.text: Use solid-state relays to blink the lights on your Christmas tree in time with music. Also good for Halloween haunted houses. Get a nice large, healthy tree set up in front of your biggest windows. See How to Pick and Decorate a Christmas Tree for more details. String lots of lights onto the tree. Use as many sets as you like, but arrange them such that there are three light regions, each with a separate plug. Run these three plugs down the trunk so they can easily be attached to the light controller. Up to three strings of lights can usually be linked in series, so you can almost certainly cover even big trees. Plug light strings into the controller you built for Halloween: https://www.instructables.com/id/Solid-state-Halloween-controller-and-how-to-build-/ Attach computer and sound system. Select high-quality Christmas music and sync the lights with a winamp plugin: http://www.8-legs.org/ewilhelm/projects/2.165/index.html Fire up the music, and treat your friends, family, and entire neighborhood to a great light now. If you really want to share, hook the music up to your outside speaker system and make the house shake in time to the music.

instruct00269.title: Milky Way Salted Caramel Cookies
instruct00269.text: Salted Caramel is all the rage lately! Here is a chocolate chip cookie that is updated with the sweet Milky Way Simply Caramel fun size candy bars and Sea Salt, of course! Just one bite into this cookie will begin the revolution of flavor in your mouth. There is Sea Salt on the interior candy itself, as well as sprinkled on top, so you are GUARANTEED to pull that salt into the caramel and enjoy the lacing of the flavors as you chew your favorite (soft) chocolate chip cookie. This cookie totally works. It's my lab experiment - gone totally yummy. Now, because I can't give out samples, you need to bake these right now, come back, post your review!! <3 And if you want doorstep service... Milky Way Salted Caramel Chocolate Chip Cookies Yields 30+ cookies Milky Way Simply Caramel Fun Size (3 of the Six Pack) 4c Flour 1t Baking Soda 1t Salt, Sea Salt Preferred 1.5c Unsalted Butter, Melted 2c Brown Sugar, Packed 1c Granulated Sugar 1T Vanilla Extract 2 Eggs 2 Egg Yolks 3c Semi-Sweet Chocolate Chips Sift the flour with your salt and baking soda, set aside. In a mixer - Cream together the melted butter, brown and granulated sugar. Once incorporated, beat in the eggs, then vanilla. After the wet ingredients are combined, add in your dry ingredients. Mix until just combined and then add the chocolate chips, gently stir them in. Cut the milky way candies in half (fun size bars), dip them into sea salt to seal the open caramel end. Take a ball of dough, just big enough to cover the half-mini-bar, add more dough if needed. Roll into a ball and sprinkle the top with more sea salt. Bake at 325 degrees for 17 minutes with 12 cookies per sheet/pan. Let cool before transferring to a cooling rack. For any further questions, just send me an email - <EMAIL> :) These are the images of me making the dough! You will see less chocolate chips in your batch because I prefer less chocolate chips for the final recipe. I had 4 cups in these photos. When you mold the cookie ball around the candy bar, they jab and get awkward, so I feel that the ratio would be better if there were less chocolate chips. (Which I've amended in my recipe.) It's very simple! Just follow the instructions in the recipe step and you will have a great cookie dough! Take a handful of dough, press it into your hand to flatten it a little, press your candy in it and build it up. Once you have it covered, you can roll it in your hand like play doh to make sure that it's completely covered. Then sprinkle sea salt, bake, and eat! Enjoy!!

# Salted Caramel Chocolate Chip Cookies Recipe

## Ingredients:
- Milky Way Simply Caramel Fun Size (3 of the Six Pack)
- 4 cups Flour
- 1 teaspoon Baking Soda
- 1 teaspoon Salt (Sea Salt Preferred)
- 1.5 cups Unsalted Butter, Melted
- 2 cups Brown Sugar, Packed
- 1 cup Granulated Sugar
- 1 tablespoon Vanilla Extract
- 2 Eggs
- 2 Egg Yolks
- 3 cups Semi-Sweet Chocolate Chips
- Additional Sea Salt for sprinkling

## Equipment:
- Mixer
- Oven
- Baking Sheets
- Cooling Rack

## Instructions:

### START:
1. Preheat the oven to 325 degrees Fahrenheit.

### PROCESS [Sift Dry Ingredients]:
2. SIFT together the flour, baking soda, and 1 teaspoon of sea salt.
3. STORE the sifted mixture for later use.

### PROCESS [Creaming Wet Ingredients]:
4. CREAM together the melted butter, brown sugar, and granulated sugar in a mixer until well incorporated.
5. BEAT in the eggs one at a time, followed by the egg yolks.
6. ADD the vanilla extract and mix until all wet ingredients are well combined.

### PROCESS [Combine Wet and Dry Ingredients]:
7. GRADUALLY add the dry ingredient mixture to the creamed wet ingredients.
8. MIX until just combined, taking care not to overmix.

### INPUT [Add Chocolate Chips]:
9. GENTLY STIR in the chocolate chips into the dough.

### PROCESS [Prepare Candy Bars]:
10. CUT the Milky Way Simply Caramel Fun Size bars in half.
11. DIP the cut side of the candy bars into sea salt to coat the open caramel end.

### PROCESS [Forming Cookies]:
12. TAKE a ball of dough large enough to cover the half candy bar.
    DECISION [IF] [Is the dough ball too small to cover the candy bar?]:
        [Yes] -> ADD more dough to sufficiently cover the candy bar.
        [No] -> CONTINUE to the next step.
13. ROLL the dough ball with the candy bar inside into a neat ball.
14. SPRINKLE the top of the dough ball with additional sea salt.

### PROCESS [Baking]:
15. PLACE 12 prepared dough balls onto a baking sheet.
16. BAKE in the preheated oven for 17 minutes.

### OUTPUT [Cooling]:
17. REMOVE cookies from the oven and allow them to cool on the baking sheet for a few minutes.
18. TRANSFER cookies to a cooling rack to cool completely.

### END:
19. ENJOY your Salted Caramel Chocolate Chip Cookies!

### STORE/DATABASE SUBROUTINE:
- For any questions, contact the provided email address.

instruct00632.title: Paintball Guitar Case
instruct00632.text: Mod an old guitar case into a custom paintball gear case. Hey everyone! This won't be a typical instructable; I had too much fun doing the project and completely forgot to document what I was doing along the way. Fortunately, there's really no special skills or knowledge needed to make your own custom paintball gear case. Let's get started! You'll need the following supplies: - Guitar case - One half yard of 4" high density foam - All purpose spray adhesive - 1 or 2 yards of fleece - An electric knife - An old newspaper - A marker - Scissors The guitar case should be a hard shell case with a soft lining in it. The high density foam is custom fit and relies on friction to stay in place. If you don't already have a guitar case, check with a local Guitar Center and ask if they have an old case you can buy for cheap (or free if you or your buddy works there). The high density foam can be purchased at a craft store like Michaels or Joanns. A half yard of 4" foam will run about $22.00 so make sure you grab the store flyer that comes out every Sunday (they almost always come with a 40% off coupon). This will put the price around $12.00. Grab your case, newspaper, marker, scissors, and electric knife for this step. Take one sheet of newspaper and lay it inside the body of the guitar case. Trace the edges of the case on the newspaper and cut it out. Lay your template on the high density foam and trace the shape to the foam. Use your electric knife to cut the guitar shape out of the foam. Make sure that the shape you cut out will fit snugly in the case or you'll just be wasting foam. Once you have the foam in the case, take some time and experiment with the layout of your gear. When you've decided where everything will go, trace out the shapes of your equipment and start cutting. After everything is cut and all your gear is in place, it's time to apply the fleece. Start by removing everything from the foam and removing the foam from the case. Lay the fleece across the foam and cut the fleece to the same shape as the foam making sure to leave about 2" of excess all the way around. Take the spray adhesive and apply a liberal amount to the foam. Quickly put the fleece in place and adjust as necessary (pull taut and remove wrinkles). Cut the fleece to allow access to the holes in the foam. Install the foam in the case and push the excess fleece in down around the edges of the case. Once everything is dry, put your gear in place and admire your handiwork. Here are a few side notes that you may helpful: -To keep my gun from shifting, I cut out a long rectangle piece from the leftover foam. The piece statically clings to the furry lining of the case. - Use leftover foam to make the pieces that will hold your tank in place. - The built-in compartment is a great place to put your small paintball tools and equipment. - This is not the sturdiest of materials. After some hard use, you will start to notice some edges of fleece separating from the foam. That's it! If anybody out there gives this a try, I would really like to see your results.

# Custom Paintball Gear Case System

## Summary:
This system details the process of converting an old guitar case into a custom paintball gear case using high density foam, fleece, and adhesive. It involves creating a foam insert shaped to the guitar case and cut to fit the specific gear, covering the foam with fleece, and securing it in the case.

## Process Steps:

### START:
- Begin the conversion of an old guitar case into a custom paintball gear case.

### INPUT:
- Gather the following materials:
  - Hard shell guitar case with soft lining
  - One half yard of 4" high density foam
  - All-purpose spray adhesive
  - 1 or 2 yards of fleece
  - Electric knife
  - Old newspaper
  - Marker
  - Scissors

### PROCESS: [Acquire Guitar Case]
- IF no guitar case is available THEN
  - Check with local music stores for an old case to purchase at a low cost or for free.

### PROCESS: [Purchase High Density Foam]
- Obtain high density foam from a craft store.
- Use a coupon to reduce the price if available.

### PROCESS: [Create Foam Template]
- Lay a sheet of newspaper inside the guitar case.
- Trace the interior edges of the case onto the newspaper.
- Cut out the traced shape to create a template.

### PROCESS: [Cut Foam to Shape]
- Place the newspaper template on the high density foam.
- Trace the template onto the foam.
- Use an electric knife to cut the foam following the traced shape.
- Ensure the foam fits snugly into the case.

### DECISION: [Does Foam Fit Snugly?]
  - IF Yes THEN proceed to layout gear.
  - IF No THEN re-cut foam to fit.

### PROCESS: [Layout Gear on Foam]
- Arrange paintball gear on the foam.
- Trace out the shapes of the equipment onto the foam.

### PROCESS: [Cut Foam for Gear]
- Cut out the traced shapes of the equipment from the foam.

### PROCESS: [Prepare Fleece]
- Remove the foam from the case.
- Lay fleece over the foam and cut to the same shape, leaving 2 inches of excess.

### PROCESS: [Apply Fleece to Foam]
- Apply spray adhesive to the foam.
- Place the fleece on the foam, ensuring it is taut and wrinkle-free.
- Cut fleece for access to the holes in the foam.

### PROCESS: [Install Foam in Case]
- Insert the foam into the case.
- Push excess fleece down around the edges.

### OUTPUT:
- The customized foam insert is now installed in the case.

### PROCESS: [Finalize Gear Arrangement]
- Place gear into the cutouts in the foam.

### DECISION: [Is Gear Securely Fitted?]
  - IF Yes THEN proceed to admire handiwork.
  - IF No THEN adjust foam and fleece as needed.

### OUTPUT:
- The custom paintball gear case is complete.

### END:
- The process of converting a guitar case into a custom paintball gear case is finished.

## Additional Tips:
- Use leftover foam to create additional support for the gun and tank.
- Utilize the built-in compartment for small tools and equipment.
- Note that the materials may wear out over time with hard use.
- Encourage feedback from others who try this project.

# Pallet Planter Project Summary

## System Overview
This system represents the process of creating a planter from pallet wood, which involves sourcing materials, preparing the wood, cutting, assembling, and finishing. The output is a completed wooden planter designed to house two large pots.

## Process Steps

### START:
- Begin the pallet planter project.

### INPUT: Materials and Tools
- Obtain free pallets from Craigslist or purchase locally if necessary.
- Ensure you have a jig or circular saw, a pry bar, hammer, nails, glue, sandpaper, stain, and outdoor urethane.

### PROCESS: Dismantling Pallets
- Use a jig or circular saw to cut the ends of the pallets.
- Pry the wood from the center support to retrieve 8 to 14 boards per pallet.

### PROCESS: Preparing the Slats
- Remove nails from the slats.
- Determine the best pieces to use based on the desired width, cutting off any damaged parts.

### INPUT: Cutting Dimensions
- Refer to the provided drawing files for the length of each board.

### PROCESS: Cutting Wood

### PROCESS: Sanding

### PROCESS: Assembling Top Frame

### PROCESS: Assembling Bottom Platform
- Assemble the bottom platform using nails and glue.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the top frame and bottom platform ready?

  - No: Resolve any issues before proceeding.

### PROCESS: Attaching Sides
- Attach the sides to the top frame and bottom platform using nails and glue.

### PROCESS: Attaching Side Trim
- Attach the side trim to the upper sides using nails and glue.

### PROCESS: Attaching Top Trim
- Attach the top trim using nails and glue.

### PROCESS: Final Sanding
- Sand the assembled planter to ensure a smooth finish.

### INPUT: Finishing Options
- Decide on the desired finish for the planter.

### DECISION [IF]: Is staining desired?
  - Yes: Apply red oak stain or chosen color.
  - No: Skip to applying urethane.

### PROCESS: Applying Urethane
- Coat the planter with outdoor urethane to protect it from the elements.

### OUTPUT: Finished Planter
- The completed wooden planter is now ready to house two large pots.

### END:
- The pallet planter project is complete.

### STORE/DATABASE SUBROUTINE:
- For reference or improvement, upgrade to the design can be found at the provided Instructables link.

instruct00630.title: Easy Faux Pearl Necklace Made of Cornstarch Clay
instruct00630.text: Here is a super easy Faux Pearl Necklace you can make for a great Mothers Day present. This is so much fun to make and so easy - just 3 ingredients that you have in your pantry. Measure out your ingredents1 cup of water1.5 cup of salt - table salt1 cup of corn starch To put the entire necklace together you will need 1 long needle and thread ( color choice is up to you). Add your water and salt and bring to a boil. I like when the salt has almost dissolved completely. Once you have a good boil turn down the heat and quickly add the cornstarch. Start to stir - then almost like magic the cornstarch will takeover the water and from a sticky paste. Keep stirring. Spoon a good size of dough out of the cooking pot and add to a mixing bowl ** remember this dough is going to be really hot so do not touch it yet. Add some more corn stach and stir away. Once the dough has cooled start to mold and shape the dough in your hands. You might have to add more cornstarch to get the right consistency you like. Now you can start to roll out the little pearls to make your necklace. You can even add some food coloring to make diffrent color pearls - so much fun. Once you have all your pearls all made out - using a good size needle poke a hole through each pearl. Let them dry for about 48 hours so they get hard. Once dried, you will be able to use needle and thread and sew you pearls together to make your necklace and or bracelet. Have fun with making all kinds of jewelry - this clay can be molded to make almost anything - and it is so easy to make. Here I string them both and added some silver chain and claps to the end to give a more fancy look.Thanks and have fun!http://www.tissupapers.blogspot.com

# Faux Pearl Necklace Creation Process

## Ingredients and Materials
- 1 cup of water (INPUT)
- 1.5 cups of table salt (INPUT)
- 1 cup of corn starch (INPUT)
- Long needle (INPUT)
- Thread (color of choice) (INPUT)
- Additional corn starch for dough consistency (INPUT)
- Food coloring (optional for colored pearls) (INPUT)
- Silver chain and clasps (optional for a fancy look) (INPUT)

## Steps

### START:
- Begin the faux pearl necklace creation process.

### PROCESS: Prepare Dough
1. Add water and salt to a pot. (PROCESS)
2. Bring the mixture to a boil. (PROCESS)
   - DECISION [IF]: Has the salt almost dissolved completely?
     - Yes: Proceed to step 3.
     - No: Continue boiling until it does.

3. Once boiling with salt dissolved, turn down the heat. (PROCESS)
4. Quickly add the cornstarch to the pot. (INPUT)
5. Stir the mixture until it forms a sticky paste. (PROCESS)
6. Spoon out a good size of dough into a mixing bowl. (PROCESS)
   - OUTPUT: Sticky dough for pearls.

### PROCESS: Cool and Shape Dough
7. Add more cornstarch to the dough in the mixing bowl. (INPUT)
8. Stir until well incorporated. (PROCESS)
9. Allow dough to cool before touching. (PROCESS)
10. Once cooled, mold and shape the dough into desired consistency by adding more cornstarch if needed. (PROCESS)
    - OUTPUT: Consistent dough ready for shaping pearls.

### PROCESS: Create Pearls
11. Roll out little pearls from the dough. (PROCESS)
    - DECISION [IF]: Would you like to add food coloring for different colored pearls?
      - Yes: Add food coloring to the dough. (INPUT)
      - No: Continue with the natural color of the dough.

12. Use a needle to poke a hole through each pearl. (PROCESS)
13. Allow pearls to dry for about 48 hours until they harden. (PROCESS)
    - OUTPUT: Hardened pearls ready for stringing.

### PROCESS: Assemble Necklace
14. Thread the needle with your chosen thread. (PROCESS)
15. Sew the pearls together by passing the thread through the holes in each pearl. (PROCESS)
    - DECISION [IF]: Would you like to add a silver chain and clasps for a fancy look?
      - Yes: Attach silver chain and clasps to the ends of the necklace. (PROCESS)
      - No: Continue to the next step.
    - OUTPUT: Finished Faux Pearl Necklace.

### END:
- The Faux Pearl Necklace is now complete and ready for gifting or wearing.
```

instruct00688.title: Phone Scanner Stand
instruct00688.text: As a teacher, I am always scanning documents (answer keys, student work, etc.) and saving the scans as PDF's. For many years, I have user the scanner function on the office photocopier. Now, with the use of a scanning app on my phone, and this stand, I can scan the documents myself. Then after scanning, I can email the scans, upload them to Google Drive or to Dropbox. So let's get started! You will need:- 1/2" PVC pipe cut to the following lengths:For the base = 4 sections @ 4"For the upright = 2 sections @ 3-3/4"For the arm = 1 section @ 7"- 3 x 1/2" PVC 90 degree elbows - 3 x 1/2" PVC couplings- 1 x 1/2" PVC tee- large 2" binder clip- rubber band- paracord The Body:Following the cut list and the photos, simply press the PVC pieces together. Optionally, you could use PVC primer and cement to permanently connect the pieces, but I prefer the flexibility of being able to take it apart for storage/portability.The Clamp:I am borrowing this idea from another 'ible. I am finding that this works as a very versatile phone clamp. Follow the directions at this 'ible to assemble the clamp. When the clamp is assembled, simply attach it to the end of the arm. You're done! Simply slide your phone into the clamp and position the camera over your document. Download your favorite document scanning app to your phone. Optionally, you could remove one of the upright sections to take "close-up-scans".I'm pleased with this project because it's cheap, simple to assemble, and it works!Happy scanning and thank you!

instruct00340.title: Nail Polish Marbled Flower Pots
instruct00340.text: These nail polish marbled flower pots would make a unique and colorful addition to your backyard, garden, or home!Since nail polish dries quickly, you'll get satisfyingly fast one-of-a-kind results.You can also use this technique to marble pretty much anything, and you'll definitely want to!Looking for more flower pot design ideas? Check out my Instructable for instructions on how to make a Drip Paint Flower Pot. You will need:a flower pot nail polish disposable container that will fit your pot toothpicks gloves paper towels nail polish remover (acetone) lukewarm/room-temperature water I painted my pots with a white enamel spray paint so that the nail polish colors would pop. If you are using pastel-colored nail polish, you could probably leave your pot terracotta colored.You can invert your pot over a tin can to keep it off of the ground while painting. Test your container to make sure your pot fits. The container doesn't have to be too deep because the nail polish should stay at the surface of the water, but it should be able to fit the length and width of your pot. The bigger the surface area, the better. A bigger surface area means more area for your marble design.Nail polish marbling can be a bit tricky, so I would suggest that you practice a bit before trying it out on your pot. (To be honest, it took me more than a few tries to get the technique down.) Once you are comfortable with the technique, you will want to marble EVERYTHING!Start by filling your container with lukewarm water. I tried hotter water, but I found water that was slightly warmer than room-temperature worked the best for me.Put some gloves on when you start to work with the nail polish because removing nail polish from your hands can be a chore.Pour your nail polish from the bottle to the water. Try to pour slowly and close to the surface of the water so that your nail polish doesn't sink to the bottom of the container in globs. The first color that you start with should be your lightest because it will spread out. If you are finding that the polish dries to quickly, or doesn't spread out, try adding a little bit of nail polish remover or acetone to the water.Next, pour in your second color. Use a toothpick to swirl the colors and get a marble happening. Limit the number of colors you use to 1-3.*Since nail polish dries fairly quickly, you will need to work fast* Start at one end of your container and touch the side of your pot to the surface of the water. Rotate your pot so that the nail polish wraps around it. Place your pot on some paper towel to dry.If your container wasn't big enough to have your marble design go all the away around your pot, you can repeat the process and marble some more. You can also marble over your dried marble design if you want to add more color. Change the water every time you make a new design. Add a few coats of clear enamel paint to protect your design. Also seal the inside of your pot if you are using terracotta pots because terracotta likes to absorb water and the water might push off the paint.

# Nail Polish Marbled Flower Pot System

## System Overview
This system describes the process of creating nail polish marbled flower pots. It involves preparing the pot, setting up the marbling container, applying nail polish in water, and marbling the pot. The final output is a uniquely designed flower pot with a marble effect.

## Process Steps

### START:
- Begin the process of creating a nail polish marbled flower pot.

### INPUT:
- Gather materials:
  - Flower pot
  - Nail polish
  - Disposable container
  - Toothpicks
  - Gloves
  - Paper towels
  - Nail polish remover (acetone)
  - Lukewarm/room-temperature water
  - Optional: white enamel spray paint for base coat

### PROCESS: [Prepare the Pot]
- DECISION [IF]: Is the flower pot pre-painted with white enamel spray paint?
  - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
  - No: Paint the pot with white enamel spray paint for better color contrast and let it dry.

### PROCESS: [Prepare the Marbling Container]
- Ensure the container is large enough to fit the pot and has a sufficient surface area for marbling.
- DECISION [IF]: Does the pot fit comfortably in the container without touching the sides?
  - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
  - No: Find a larger container.
  
### PROCESS: [Practice Technique]
- Practice the nail polish marbling technique in water before applying it to the pot to become comfortable with the process.

### PROCESS: [Set Up for Marbling]
- Fill the container with lukewarm water.
- Wear gloves to protect hands from nail polish.

### PROCESS: [Apply Nail Polish to Water]
- Pour the first, lightest color of nail polish slowly and close to the water surface to prevent sinking.
- DECISION [IF]: Is the nail polish spreading too quickly or not at all?
  - Yes: Add a little bit of nail polish remover or acetone to the water and retry.
  - No: Proceed to the next color.

### PROCESS: [Add Additional Colors]
- Pour the second color into the water.
- Use a toothpick to swirl the colors together to create a marbled effect.
- Limit the number of colors to 1-3 for best results.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the nail polish drying too quickly?
  - Yes: Work faster and proceed to marble the pot immediately.
  - No: Continue with the marbling process.

### PROCESS: [Marble the Pot]
- Start at one end of the container and touch the side of the pot to the surface of the water.
- Rotate the pot to wrap the nail polish around it.
- Set the pot on paper towels to dry.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the entire pot covered with the marble design?
  - Yes: Proceed to sealing the pot.
  - No: Repeat the marbling process to cover any missed areas.

### PROCESS: [Seal the Design]
- Apply a few coats of clear enamel paint to protect the exterior marble design.
- Seal the inside of the pot, especially if using terracotta, to prevent water absorption.

### OUTPUT:
- A uniquely designed, nail polish marbled flower pot.

### END:
- The process of creating a nail polish marbled flower pot is complete.
```

instruct00307.title: Italian Roma Tomato and Mozzarella Grilled Pizza!
instruct00307.text: One of my favorite Grilled Pizza Combos! (and we do grilled pizza at least once a week!) You'll need pizza crust, sauce, Roma tomatoes (these would be awesome from your garden) and Mozzarella Cheese...you could make your own like I did here! Thinly slice your tomatoes and slice up your cheese. Mine was presliced, but they were really thick...I tried to cut them in half. Heat up the grill on low. Put your entire crust right on the grill. Wait for it to lightly brown and flip the entire thing over. Add your tomato sauce...I always go with the garlic kind. Add you tomato slices like pepperoni! Add your chunks of mozzarella on top. Sprinkle with some basil...or Italian seasoning. Let the cheese soften and the underside of the crust cook... then get it off the grill and cut it up! Looks like ice cream! So yummy! Perfect Garden Pizza! Try it out and vote for me in the Italian food contest! Thanks! :) Check out my blog doodlecraft for more fun too!

# Grilled Pizza Preparation System

## Summary
This system guides you through the process of making a Grilled Pizza with a specific combination of ingredients including pizza crust, sauce, Roma tomatoes, Mozzarella Cheese, and basil or Italian seasoning. The process involves grilling the pizza crust, adding toppings, and cooking until the cheese is soft and the crust is done.

## Steps

### START:
- Begin the Grilled Pizza preparation process.

### INPUT:
- Gather the following ingredients:
  - Pizza crust
  - Tomato sauce (preferably garlic kind)
  - Roma tomatoes
  - Mozzarella Cheese
  - Basil or Italian seasoning

### PROCESS: Prepare Ingredients
1. Thinly slice the Roma tomatoes.
2. Slice the Mozzarella Cheese into chunks. If pre-sliced, cut slices in half if they are too thick.

### PROCESS: Preheat Grill
1. Heat up the grill on a low setting.

### PROCESS: Grill Pizza Crust
1. Place the entire pizza crust directly on the grill.
2. Wait for the crust to lightly brown.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the crust lightly browned?
- Yes: Proceed to flip the crust.
- No: Continue grilling the crust until lightly browned.

### PROCESS: Flip Crust and Add Toppings
1. Flip the entire pizza crust over.
2. Spread tomato sauce evenly over the crust.
3. Arrange the tomato slices on the sauce.
4. Add chunks of Mozzarella Cheese on top.
5. Sprinkle basil or Italian seasoning over the cheese.

### PROCESS: Cook Pizza
1. Let the cheese soften and the underside of the crust cook.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the cheese soft and crust cooked?
- Yes: Proceed to remove the pizza from the grill.
- No: Continue cooking until cheese is soft and crust is cooked.

### OUTPUT:
- Once the cheese is soft and the crust is cooked, remove the pizza from the grill.

### PROCESS: Finalize and Serve
1. Cut the grilled pizza into slices.

### OUTPUT:
- Serve the perfect Garden Pizza.

### END:
- The Grilled Pizza preparation process is complete.

## Notes
- Vote for this recipe in the Italian food contest if you enjoyed it.
- Visit the blog "doodlecraft" for more fun recipes and crafts.
