```markdown
PROCESS: Plug the Cord Ends Together [PRO TIP]
- INPUT: The plug ends of the extension cord.
- PROCESS: Connect the front plug of the cord to the end plug.
- OUTPUT: A secured Shepherd's Knot with connected plugs.

END:
- The extension cord is now neatly stored in a Shepherd's Knot and ready for easy unraveling when needed.
```

instruct00130.title: How to Make Strike Anywhere Matches
instruct00130.text: You will need: Safety matches (with matchbox), sanding paper, a small container, something to stir with, a pair of pliers, a tube or a D-cell battery, and water. You will also need something to lay the matches on, like a the edge of a table or this CD case that I used. Sand off the phosphorus on the sides of the matchbox (striking surfaces) and put the powder in the container. Put a few drops if water in the container and stir well. Take the matches, one by one, and dip them in the mixture. Then lay them on the edge of the table/CD case. When they're dry, take some new matches and squeeze off the heads with the pliers, then pulverize the powder with the pipe or battery by pressing it down and rolling it over the powder and then put it in the container (if you're using the same container, be sure to wash out the leftover phosphorus). Add a few drops of water and stir well. Then dip the matches in the new mix so that you cover the phosphorus already on them and let them to dry again for a while. Please be sure to wash your hands after making these matches, phosphorus is toxic.

```markdown
# Structured Summary of Blog Post: How to Make Safety Matches

- Use sanding paper to sand off the phosphorus from the sides of the matchbox.

- TAKE a match using pliers.

- IF Yes: Proceed to the next step.

- ADD a few drops of water to the container with the match head powder.

- The process of making safety matches is complete.

- WASH hands thoroughly to remove any phosphorus residue.
- CLEAN all used tools and surfaces to ensure no toxic materials are left.
```

instruct00891.title: How to Ride a Horse in Minecraft
instruct00891.text: I love to ride horses in video games, so when I found out you could ride a horse in Minecraft, I had to give it a try. I talk about this some in my instructable about Minecraft Animals/Mobs, but I wanted to devote an Instructable to how to (tame and) ride a horse in Minecraft. In order to ride a Horse, all you need is a Saddle. Unfortunately, you cannot make a saddle, you have to find one. You can find them occasionally in chests around the world.Optionally, you can put Horse Armor on Horses (not Donkey's or Mules). This also can only be found, not crafted.You can equip a Donkey or Mule with a Chest to have it hold supplies for you (you cannot add a chest to a Horse). Before you can ride a Horse, you need to tame it.The way to tame it is, while not holding an item, click on the Horse like you would to use an item. The Horse will most likely buck you off. You need to repeat this until hearts appear, but you can also feed the Horse Apples, Wheat, Golden Apples, Golden Carrots, Wheat, or a Hay Bale to help tame it. Now your Horse is tamed. instruct00255.title: 40$ USB Super Telescope, Easy to Make, Sees Craters on the Moon
instruct00255.text: Turn an old telelens and a webcam into a powerfull telescope that is capable of seeing craters on the moon. Next to the webcam and tele lens all you need are some standard pvc plumbing materials (pipes, diameter adapters and endcaps) Here's what you need: 1. A webcam (I used a quickcam 4000 from logitech I still had) 2. A telelens, the more focal length the more magnification you'll get, the lens I'm using here is 80-210mm, you can get them at ebay starting from 12dollars. Many people have old tele lenses left from the analog camera era so there are plenty of them on the web. 3. Some standard pvc plumbing materials: pvc pipes, a diameter adapter to fit different diameters and some end caps. What you need precisely depends on your lens. More details on this can be seen on the next steps. 4. It's not part of the telescope itself, but it is important to have a tripod since the magnification is very large so any movement will ge greatly magnified. So without a tripod as a stable base, you won't be able to use your telescope. First you need to take the webcam apart until you're left with the pcb and the microphone and button. Unscrew the original lens of the webcam and remove it completely. Next you have to go to the local hardware store and find the pvc part that fits your lens or gets very very close to fitting so you can easily fill up the gap with some tightly wound tape. I made 2 of these telescopes and didn't have problems finding a perfect match, but that could just be luck. You'll also need an endcap for this phase. Make a hole just as large as the optical tube of the webcam exactly in the middle of the endcap. It must be exactly, or performance will reduce. Now you can put everything together. Fit the adapter to the lens, put on the endcap (I needed an extra piece of pipe to reach the endcap diameter) and put the webcam in. The hole in my encap was to tight I could just lock the webcam in. If yours is a little looser, use some tape. The webcam must be about 3cm behind the rear end of the tele lens. Now you can try it. Hook it up to a pc and put it on a tripod. Aim at something more than 50 meters away and see if you can focus by turning the focus ring of the tele lens. If you can't, then you must play with the distance between the tele lens and the webcam. You may need to change the length of the adapter a bit. Once this is done, you can glue (or tape) everything together. Make sure that all the parts are perfectly aligned in a straight line, this is also vital for the best results. It's very easy to make a housing, just use 2 encaps and a piece of pipe with a slot for the USB wire. It can all be glued or taped together. On the pictures, you can see the various stages of assembly. One endcap needs quite a big hole, otherwise the parts on the pcb will touch the endcap tilting the webcam pcb which is bad for optical quality. These pictures show the weatherstation on my neighbors house. The first picture is made with my normal photo camera without zooming. The circle shows what the telescope is aimed at. The second and third picture are made with the telescope at 100mm and 210mm zoom setting. The first picture is made with my normal camera again. The antenna mast is in the circle. It's 450m away, I checked this with my gps. The second picture is with the telescope at maximum zoom. Here are 2 pictures of the moon. You can easily see craters and mountains. I hope you enjoyed this project! Hanzablast

```markdown
# Structured Summary of Converting a Telelens and Webcam into a Telescope

## System Overview
The system is designed to convert an old telelens and a webcam into a powerful telescope capable of observing lunar details. The process involves disassembling a webcam, adapting PVC plumbing materials to construct a housing and mounting system, and aligning the telelens with the webcam's sensor. The final product is mounted on a tripod and connected to a PC for observation and imaging.

## System Inputs
- An old telelens (e.g., 80-210mm focal length)
- A webcam (e.g., Logitech Quickcam 4000)
- PVC plumbing materials (pipes, diameter adapters, end caps)
- Tripod (not part of the telescope, but necessary for stability)
- Tools for disassembly and construction
- Tape or glue for securing components
- PC for connecting the webcam

## System Outputs
- A homemade telescope capable of viewing craters on the moon
- Images captured by the telescope when connected to a PC

## Process Steps

### START
- Begin the conversion process.

### PROCESS: Disassemble Webcam
- INPUT: Webcam
- OUTPUT: Webcam PCB with microphone and button, lens removed

### DECISION [IF]: Is the PVC part a perfect fit for the lens?
- Yes: Proceed to fitting the adapter.
- No: Use tape to fill the gap and secure fit.

### PROCESS: Prepare PVC Parts
- INPUT: PVC pipes, diameter adapter, end caps
- OUTPUT: Customized PVC housing for the telescope

### PROCESS: Make Hole in Endcap
- INPUT: Endcap, measurements of the optical tube of the webcam
- OUTPUT: Endcap with a precise, centered hole

### PROCESS: Assemble Telescope
- INPUT: Adapter, lens, endcap, modified webcam, PVC parts
- OUTPUT: Assembled telescope without final adjustments

### DECISION [IF]: Can the telescope focus at 50 meters?
- Yes: Proceed to final assembly.
- No: Adjust distance between lens and webcam.

### PROCESS: Final Assembly and Alignment
- INPUT: Adjusted telescope components
- OUTPUT: Fully assembled and aligned telescope

### PROCESS: Create Housing
- INPUT: Endcaps, PVC pipe, slot for USB wire
- OUTPUT: Housing for the telescope

### PROCESS: Test and Adjust Focus
- INPUT: Telescope, tripod, PC
- OUTPUT: Focused images from the telescope

### END
- The telescope is complete and capable of lunar observations.
```

instruct00127.title: The Helicopter Carp Rig
instruct00127.text: Chas Cook is the owner of Vaux French carp lake. This is the 5th article in an excellent series which gives you instruction on how to construct a series of carp rigs he's used to great effect for his carp fishing in France. You can read all the articles here. Both of the following rigs have, once again, been used to great effect when fishing to open water marks using the bag and double foamed hook length, so that neither rig sinks into the silt. They are particularly effective when fishing to far banks, islands and lily pads over lake bottoms of sand and gravel. Takes result in drop backs on swingers and single beeps on buzzers as the carp leave the bank and islands on the reverse. The weight of the lead rapidly transfers to the point of the hook; in these situations 12lb fluorocarbon mainline is used, 30lb low profile leaders and semi tight clutches not bait runners. Bottom baits are used when carp are feeding along the far banks, but in the summer when temperatures are higher, they spend more time in the pads or on the surface under the trees along the far bank and so 40-60mm pop-ups are used on a chod set-up. Zig rigs can also be used off both helicopter set-ups, fishing to variable depths of water wherever the carp are lying in the lake and using 30-50mm pop-ups apple core shaped. The zigs are designed to put the rigs as close as possible to the basking carp; even if they are not feeding, carp at rest will naturally try to take a pop-up if a zig drops close to them. In-line Lead Helicopter Rig (set up retaining the lead)Component Parts * 3oz 5oz inline lead * Standard tail rubber cut @ 450 * Swivel with wide bore one end * Standard reverse inline lead helicopter set-up * Swivel placed onto extended sleeve * 3oz inline lead * Tail rubber placed on lead sleeve but NOT pushed tight * 30lb low profile fluorocarbon leader with swivel already attached passes through the centre of the lead * Q ring attached * Longer hook length (shown) is a bottom bait set-up * A shorter hook length (not shown) would be a helicopter or a chod set-up * Hook length attached to Q ring * Funnel web bag attached to Q ring * Bottom bait of hook length set up Distance Lead Helicopter Rig (set up dropping the lead) Component Parts * Lead core leader * Rubber bead * Wide bore swivel * Extended tail rubber * Inline 3oz-5oz distance lead * Standard size 8 swivel * Wide bore swivel goes over the end of the tail rubber * Rubber bead is pulled/pushed on to the end of the extended tail rubber * Greased tail rubber pushed onto the sleeve of the distance lead * Lead core leader is drawn over the outside of the distance lead and passes through the tail rubber * Swivel goes into the bottom of the distance lead * Leader is then drawn tight over the profile of the lead * Q ring attached to the eye of the swivel at the same point as the lead core is attached * Rig set to show a bottom bait * PVA bag containing carp and trout pellets attached to the Q ring * On the take from the fish the lead is dropped, the helicopter component parts slide down over the leader onto the leader swivelFishing Holiday in France at Vaux

```markdown
# Carp Fishing Rig Construction System

## In-Line Lead Helicopter Rig (Retaining the Lead)

### START:
- START the construction of the In-Line Lead Helicopter Rig.

### PROCESS: [Gathering Component Parts]
- INPUT: 3oz-5oz inline lead, Standard tail rubber, Swivel with wide bore, Fluorocarbon leader (30lb), Q ring, Hook length, Funnel web bag, Bottom bait.

### PROCESS: [Assembling the Rig]
- PROCESS: Cut the standard tail rubber at 45 degrees.
- PROCESS: Place the swivel onto the extended sleeve.
- PROCESS: Attach the 3oz inline lead.
- PROCESS: Fit the tail rubber onto the lead sleeve loosely.
- PROCESS: Pass the fluorocarbon leader through the center of the lead.
- PROCESS: Attach the Q ring.
- DECISION: Is the hook length for a bottom bait setup?
  - IF Yes:
    - PROCESS: Attach the longer hook length to the Q ring.
  - ELSE No:
    - PROCESS: Attach the shorter hook length for helicopter or chod set-up.
- PROCESS: Attach the funnel web bag to the Q ring.
- PROCESS: Attach the bottom bait to the hook length setup.
- OUTPUT: Completed In-Line Lead Helicopter Rig (Retaining the Lead).

### END:
- END of the In-Line Lead Helicopter Rig construction process.

## Distance Lead Helicopter Rig (Dropping the Lead)

### START:
- START the construction of the Distance Lead Helicopter Rig.

### PROCESS: [Gathering Component Parts]
- INPUT: Lead core leader, Rubber bead, Wide bore swivel, Extended tail rubber, Inline 3oz-5oz distance lead, Standard size 8 swivel, PVA bag with carp and trout pellets.

### PROCESS: [Assembling the Rig]
- PROCESS: Attach the wide bore swivel over the end of the tail rubber.
- PROCESS: Fit the rubber bead onto the end of the extended tail rubber.
- PROCESS: Grease and push the tail rubber onto the sleeve of the distance lead.
- PROCESS: Draw the lead core leader over the distance lead and through the tail rubber.
- PROCESS: Insert the standard size 8 swivel into the bottom of the distance lead.
- PROCESS: Tighten the leader over the profile of the lead.
- PROCESS: Attach the Q ring to the eye of the swivel where the lead core is attached.
- PROCESS: Set up the rig to show a bottom bait.
- PROCESS: Attach the PVA bag to the Q ring.
- OUTPUT: Completed Distance Lead Helicopter Rig (Dropping the Lead).

### END:
- END of the Distance Lead Helicopter Rig construction process.

## Additional Information

- Note that both rigs are effective when fishing to open water marks and should not sink into the silt.
- These rigs are particularly effective when fishing to far banks, islands, and lily pads over lake bottoms of sand and gravel.
- For the In-Line Lead Helicopter Rig, takes result in drop backs on swingers and single beeps on buzzers.
- The Distance Lead Helicopter Rig is designed to drop the lead on the take from the fish, allowing the helicopter component parts to slide down over the leader onto the leader swivel.
- Both rigs can be used with various baits and set-ups depending on the carp's location and feeding habits.
```

instruct00729.title: Cheap and Easy Reusable Swiffer Wet-Jet Pads
instruct00729.text: Hi. This is my first Instructable. This is very low-tech and very humble. Those of you (Instructabelers....Instructabilians...Instructabillys?).. ..that do these high-tech genius projects, man, you guys are so much cooler than I. I mostly like to find minute ways to make my life easier. I'm super cheap and lazy, and obsessive about arranging and automating my life as much as possible so I don't actually have to be present. So if I do any more of these, it'll probably be along those lines. This particular project was for me just filling a need. I like my Wet-Jet but I hate buying the disposable pads all the time. At about a buck a piece, cleaning the floor starts looking expensive to me. (I have 2 young children) There doesn't seem to be a generic brand of the pads that I've seen, and some other mop brands do make reusable pads but they're stupid-expensive too, they don't really fit the Swiffer, and the ones I've tried don't even work that great in my opinion. So I set out to make my own. A few weeks of supply hunting and experimentation and we have a winner! 1. A Swiffer Wet Jet 2. some washcloth-sized rags 3. dish-washing cloths with scrubbing mesh on at least one side. 4. two "binder clips" (I had to look up what those things were called) 5. scissors cost: a few dollars at most. I found a 3 pack of the mesh dish towels at a discount store for $2 and teh rest of the stuff I had around the house already. 1. Lay your dish towel with the mesh side down. 2. Fold your rag in half and lay in the middle of the dish towel. (this extra rag adds absorbancy. If the scrubbing towel you found is very thick, you may want to omit the rag. Don't be tempted to thicken it more than the 3 layers shown or your swiffer will rollaround on the pad and annoy you.) 3. Place the head of the swiffer so that the leading edge lines up with the edge of the folded rag and is pretty much completely covering that edge. You don't want any of it to fold up over the leading edge. 4. Pinch the cloth up around the top of the Swiffer's head, fold it over if necessary, pull it kinda tight, and clip with your super strong binder clips. Placement of the clips should be more or less in line with the "jets". 5. Feel for (or peek) for the jets through the cloth and use scissors to snip away the cloth covering them. If after you start using your new disposable pads your swiffer starts spraying wonky, you might try making these holes larger. Ohhhhh heck yeah. I made 3 of these and they are enough to keep me mopping the whole week through. Toss them in the laundry and reassemble. It's a bad picture, but if you stick them in like that, they stay there.

```markdown
# Swiffer Wet Jet Reusable Pads System Summary

## Process Steps

### START:
- Begin with the intention to create reusable pads for a Swiffer Wet Jet to save on cost and convenience.

### PROCESS: Gather Materials
- INPUT: 
  - A Swiffer Wet Jet
  - Washcloth-sized rags
  - Dish-washing cloths with scrubbing mesh on one side
  - Two binder clips
  - Scissors

### PROCESS: Prepare the Dish Towel
- Lay the dish towel with the mesh side facing down.

### PROCESS: Add Absorbent Layer
- Fold a rag in half.
- Place the folded rag in the middle of the dish towel.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the scrubbing towel thick?
  - IF YES: Omit the additional rag.
  - IF NO: Continue to the next step.

### PROCESS: Align Swiffer Head
- Position the head of the Swiffer so that the leading edge lines up with the edge of the folded rag, covering it completely.

### PROCESS: Attach Cloth to Swiffer Head
- Pinch the cloth around the top of the Swiffer’s head.
- Fold over excess cloth if necessary.
- Pull the cloth tight.

### PROCESS: Secure Cloth with Binder Clips
- Use binder clips to secure the cloth in place.
- Ensure clips are aligned with the “jets” of the Swiffer.

### PROCESS: Create Openings for Jets
- Feel for the jets through the cloth.
- Snip away the cloth covering the jets with scissors.

### DECISION [IF]: Does the Swiffer spray incorrectly?
  - IF YES: Enlarge the holes for the jets.
  - IF NO: Proceed with mopping.

### PROCESS: Use and Maintenance
- Make multiple reusable pads to last through cleaning sessions.
- After use, remove the pads and launder them.
- Reassemble the pads onto the Swiffer after washing.

### OUTPUT:
- A set of reusable pads for the Swiffer Wet Jet, resulting in cost savings and reduced waste.

### END:
- The process concludes with a supply of reusable pads ready for use and maintenance.
```

instruct00524.text: In this Instructable we are going to learn how to make a spider web!! For this instructable all you need is some yarn and a pair scissors. I used a blueish color for the yarn but you can use what you want. First you want to start with a basic frame of one vertical length of yarn and one horizontal. I started to weave the thread around in a spiral tying a overhand knot each time I got to one of the supporting strands. Me and my mom added more support strands at this part but you can add them earlier if you want to. Keep weaving... You are now finished make your web!! Now go make a spider!!

```markdown
# How to Make a Spider Web with Yarn

## Summary Representation

### START:
- Begin the process of creating a spider web using yarn.

### INPUT:
- Gather materials:
  - Yarn (color of choice)
  - A pair of scissors

### PROCESS: Create Basic Frame
- Lay out one piece of yarn vertically.
- Lay out another piece of yarn horizontally, creating a cross shape.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the frame stable enough?
- [Yes]: Proceed to weaving.
- [No]: Add more support strands to stabilize the frame.
  - PROCESS: Add additional support strands as needed.

### PROCESS: Begin Weaving
- Start weaving the yarn in a spiral pattern.
- Tie an overhand knot each time you intersect with a supporting strand.

### DECISION [IF]: Have you reached the desired size of the web?
- [Yes]: End the weaving process.
- [No]: Continue weaving in a spiral and tying knots at each support intersection.

### OUTPUT:
- The finished spider web is created.

### PROCESS: Create a Spider (Optional)
```

instruct00515.title: Tiny Catapults!
instruct00515.text: Construct your own miniature siege engines! 1. A couple of nasty looking boards. 2. A 1/2" diameter dowel. 3. A short piece of a 2x2. 4. A length of thin rope. 5. Two 1" wood screws. 6. A 1/2" drill bit. 7. A 3/4" spade bit. 8. A drill or drill press. 9. A table saw or circular saw or handsaw. 10. A miter saw or miter box or motorized miter box 11. Scissors. 12. A screwdriver 13. A lighter. 14. A pencil. 15. A roll of tape. 16. A ruler. 17. A miniature enemy. First, use your table saw to cut your nasty looking boards into two 7 1/2" x 3 1/2" rectangles. Once you've done this, tape the two boards together with the broad sides touching, then, with your pencil, mark the two longer edges: "top" and "bottom", and the two shorter edges "front" and "back". Measure 1" up from the "bottom" and 2" from the "front" and draw an X. Next, measure 1" down from the "top" and 3" from the "front" and draw another X. Next, with your boards still taped together, measure 1/2" up from the "bottom" and 1/2" from the "back" of the board and draw a V. Flip your taped boards over and draw another V in exactly the same place on the other side. Last, measure 3 1/2" from the "front" and 1 1/2" from the "bottom" and draw a T. Do the same on the other side. Fit your 1/2" bit into your drill. Drill the Xs all the way through. Drill the Vs to a 1/4" depth. Drive a screw into each of the Ts so about 1/4" sticks out. Separate the two boards. They should look like a mirror image of each other. Next, use your miter saw to cut your dowel into two 5 1/4" lengths and one 4 1/4" length. Cut your 2x2 to a 7" length. Cut one end into a triangle shape. With your 3/4" bit, drilla 1/4" deep hole on the end opposite, and the side perpendicular to the triangular end. Drill a 1/2" hole toward the triangular end. Then use your scissors to cut a 26" piece from your length of rope. If you're using braided nylon or another synthetic like I am, you'll have to use your lighter to melt the ends so they don't fray. Now that you have all your parts, you can start to assemble your catapult. Start by tying a knot in each end of your 26" piece of rope. I prefer to use a knot called a double half hitch for this. Then attach it to the screws. Next, pass one of your longer dowels through the smaller hole of your catapult arm. Fit each end into the lower holes on the sides. This dowel will be a pivot for the arm. Use the catapult arm to twist the rope around the dowel as shown. There should be a fair amount of tension. Slip your other longer dowel into the upper holes in front of the arm to maintain the tension in the rope. Finally, notch the shorter dowel into the shallow holes you drilled toward the back, and you're done. You now have a functioning mechanism with which to wage minuscule siege warfare! Don't stop there though. Embellish! For more home-made wackiness, check out Pariahcycle.Blogspot.com

```markdown
# Miniature Siege Engine Construction Guide

## System Overview
This guide outlines the process of constructing a miniature siege engine (catapult) using various tools and materials. The system inputs include wood, dowels, screws, rope, and tools for cutting and assembly. The output is a functional miniature catapult.

## Materials and Tools (Inputs)
- **Materials:**
  - Nasty looking boards
  - 1/2" diameter dowel
  - Short piece of 2x2
  - Thin rope
  - Two 1" wood screws
- **Tools:**
  - 1/2" drill bit
  - 3/4" spade bit
  - Drill or drill press
  - Table saw, circular saw, or handsaw
  - Miter saw, miter box, or motorized miter box
  - Scissors
  - Screwdriver
  - Lighter
  - Pencil
  - Tape
  - Ruler

## Process Steps

### START: Begin Construction
- Ensure all materials and tools are ready for use.

### PROCESS: Prepare Boards
- Use a saw to cut boards into two 7 1/2" x 3 1/2" rectangles.
- Tape the two boards together with broad sides touching.
- Mark the longer edges as "top" and "bottom", shorter edges as "front" and "back".

### PROCESS: Mark Drill Points on Boards
- Measure and mark an X at 1" up from "bottom" and 2" from "front".
- Measure and mark an X at 1" down from "top" and 3" from "front".
- Measure and mark a V at 1/2" up from "bottom" and 1/2" from "back".
- Flip and mark a V at the same location on the other side.
- Measure and mark a T at 3 1/2" from "front" and 1 1/2" from "bottom".
- Repeat for the other side.

### PROCESS: Drill Holes in Boards
- Fit 1/2" bit into the drill.
- Drill through both Xs.
- Drill Vs to a 1/4" depth.
- Drive a screw into each T, leaving 1/4" out.
- Separate the two boards; they should be mirror images.

### PROCESS: Prepare Dowels and 2x2
- Cut dowel into two 5 1/4" lengths and one 4 1/4" length.
- Cut 2x2 to a 7" length and shape one end into a triangle.
- Drill a 1/4" deep hole on the end opposite the triangular end using a 3/4" bit.
- Drill a 1/2" hole toward the triangular end.

### PROCESS: Prepare Rope
- Cut a 26" piece from the length of rope using scissors.
- IF the rope is synthetic:
  - DECISION [IF]: Is the rope synthetic?
    - Yes: Use a lighter to melt the ends to prevent fraying.
    - No: Proceed without melting.

### PROCESS: Assemble Catapult
- Tie a knot at each end of the 26" rope.
- Attach the rope to the screws protruding from the boards.
- Pass one long dowel through the smaller hole of the catapult arm.
- Fit each end of the dowel into the lower holes on the sides of the boards.
- Use the catapult arm to twist the rope around the dowel, creating tension.
- Slip the other long dowel into the upper holes in front of the arm to maintain tension.
- Notch the shorter dowel into the shallow holes toward the back.

### OUTPUT: Complete Miniature Siege Engine
- Verify that the catapult mechanism functions properly.

### END: Construction Complete
- Embellish the catapult as desired for aesthetics or additional functionality.
- For further projects, refer to Pariahcycle.Blogspot.com.
```

instruct00486.title: Ink Removal From Soda Cans
instruct00486.text: Soda cans are involved in all kinds of "reuse" projects. If you have no idea just use the search bar on the instructable homepage desktop and type in "soda cans" and you received various results with projects where soda cans are reused. However, if you need the can for some more decorative purpose the inprints on the outside wall of the can makes it useless. Therefore, this instructable demonstrates an easy method for ink removal on soda cans. As a result, you will end up with a can having a nice shiny outer surface as given on the picture. In this instructable a vase for flowers was built (see last step). Only few materials are needed for this project:Soda cans Nail polish remover Cotton pads Pressure cooker Hot platePlease use various types of soda cans for your first project. Even so the procedure worked for almost all cans some did resist to the procedure. Surfing through the internet you will find some procedure using sandpaper to remove the ink. However, with this procedure you will never end up with the polished shiny outer surface that you want for your decorative reuse project.During the first attempts, various solvents were used e.g. nail polish remover or pure acetone directly. But as you can see in the attached video none of them did work.Here is the trick: Put the cans in a pressure cooker for around 20 minutes.Attention: ONLY ADD EMPTY CANS IN THE PRESSURE COOKERUse the procedure that comes with your pressure cooker for sterilizing liquids. In my case I have to add a little bit of water to cover the bottom of the sterilizer. Then place all soda cans inside and close the lid. On the hot plate, I use maximum power to start (level 6 of 6). As soon as the pressure indicator reaches the second mark (2 of 2) power of the hot plate is reduced immediately to level 2 (level 2 of 6). Sterilize it for around 20 minutes. After 20 minutes take away the pressure cooker from the hot plate and wait until the pressure is released. Then open the cooker carefully (hot vapor) and take out the cans.Add some drops of nails polish remover to the cotton pad and start removing the ink. As shown in the video the bottom part of the soda can was removed and the lid was opened using a tin-opener. A 300ml PET flask was found that fitted directly into the polished soda can. The PET flask was shortened to the correct length and then fixed into the soda can with hot glue.I hope you like this creative reuse of a soda can which turned into a vase for flowers.

```markdown
## Summary Representation

- Begin the process of removing ink from a soda can for reuse.

  - Nail polish remover
```

instruct00168.title: How to Make a Trebuchet
instruct00168.text: Hi Guys :) Please rate this Instructable and follow me if you liked it. Thank you. :) Here is a Simple Way to Build a Trebuchet. A trebuchet is a siege engine that was used in the Middle Ages to fling projectile ofup to140 pounds at enemy structures.Please Rate this Instructable and follow me for more cool step by step guides. Made By Manish Kumar What you need: 1. Popsicle sticks 2. Super Glue 3. Double-Sided Tape 4. Electrical Tape 5. Sharp Scissors or a Knife 6. Round Pencils (as an axle) 7. Washers 8. # Trebuchet Construction System

```markdown
## Inputs
- Popsicle sticks
- Super Glue
- Double-Sided Tape
- Electrical Tape
- Sharp Scissors or a Knife
- Round Pencils (as axles)
- Washers
- Counterweight (e.g., coins)

- A fully constructed trebuchet capable of launching a projectile.

## Process Steps

### START:
- Begin the construction of the trebuchet.

### PROCESS: Construct the Base
1. Use Popsicle sticks and Super Glue to build the base of the trebuchet as shown in the instructions.

### PROCESS: Fortify the Base
2. Add additional Popsicle sticks to the top, bottom, right, and left edges of the base.
   - Use Super Glue to secure.
   - Wait for the glue to dry.
   - Repeat to add a second layer for strength.

### PROCESS: Create Support Pillars
3. Construct two angled support structures using Popsicle sticks and Super Glue to act as pillars.

### PROCESS: Attach Pillars to Base
4. Use Super Glue to join the pillars to the base.
   - Allow time for the glue to dry and strengthen the structure.

### PROCESS: Prepare Axle Support
5. Place washers between the pillars, ensuring they are wide enough for the pencil axle.
   - Use a Popsicle stick to connect the pillars for additional support.
   - Apply double-sided tape if needed for extra stability.

### PROCESS: Insert Axle

   - Reinforce with small Popsicle stick pieces.
```

instruct00562.title: DIY Vanilla Extract
instruct00562.text: Recently I saw a post on Chocolate & Zucchini on making your own vanilla extract. Since this sells for nearly as much as HP printer ink at the super market I thought it would be worth looking into. As it turns out it's incredibly easy to make and totally worth doing. I followed this "recipe" from Chocolate & Zucchini. Homemade Vanilla Extract - 3 medium vanilla beans, or 1 1/2 fat ones - 1 cup rum or vodkaHomemade Vanilla Extract via Chocolate & Zucchini There really isn't much to this. I picked up a pound of "Grade B Extract Vanilla Beans" on eBay for $20 shipped and a handle of Vodka for $17.99. As it turns out a pound of vanilla beans is an incredible amount of beans. Recipes seem to recommend anywhere from 3 to 6 beans per cup of alcohol. I used 6 and still had enough beans to make this recipe 5 or 6 times over. Something to think about when making that eBay order. Figuring 3 beans per cup of alcohol I calculated out the amount of alcohol and number of beans needed (a lot). The steps for preparing this are pretty simple. 1. Remove vodka or rum from original bottle 2. Split vanilla beans in half 3. Sanitize bottle 4. Put beans in the bottom of the now empty and sanitized bottle 5. Pour vodka back into bottle 6. Cap it, date it and throw it in the back of your cabinet. Sanitizing the bottle may have been overkill but I'd rather be safe than sorry. Give the bottle a shake everyday for the first week and then once or twice a week for the rest of the infusion period. Your vodka/rum should be "extract" in 2 months but will continue to improve in flavor for at least another 4-6 months. One of the most fun parts of this project was designing an old timey label to go on the bottle. I settled on the name "Uncle Chris' fancy vanillin extract" which seemed sufficiently old timey. I sketched up a drawing of my label and handed it over to my girlfriend who did a great job making it into a vector image. She then applied an aged look to the label for printing. These were printed on sticker sheets for easy application. Below is the evolution of the label. I ordered the bottles from Amazon, having glass shipped is really expensive so using my Amazon Prime shipping was easily the cheapest way to get these. Eight ounces seemed to be the most practical size and I really liked the look of these brown bottles. After the two month wait is finally over your extraction phase has completed, now on to bottling! I did a little taste/smell test, comparing the home brew extract to a bottle of McCormick's Real Vanilla Extract. The homemade stuff smells sweeter and looks a little lighter. I find the McCormick extract to have a bit of a chemical odor when compared to the home brew extract. I started with two handles of vodka (added one the next day after seeing how easy it was!) and ended up with 12 8-ounce bottles of extract. Considering the cost of the ingredients I'd say it was a pretty good deal. I included a split vanilla bean in each bottle to continue extraction. This way the extract will continue to age and darken over time. In addition to labeling all the bottles I also numbered and dated them. Beyond just being OCD the dates are on there because according to my original recipe the extract should continue to improve for the next 4 months. The extract smells and tastes great, considering the price difference I can't imagine I'd ever buy vanilla extract from the store again. In general I'd say this is a pretty easy project worth trying. A++ would extract again.

```markdown
# Homemade Vanilla Extract System

## Inputs
- 3 medium vanilla beans or 1 1/2 fat vanilla beans
- 1 cup rum or vodka
- A bottle for storing the extract
- Sanitization equipment (optional)
- Sticker sheets for labeling (optional)
- Vector image software (optional)

## Outputs
- Homemade vanilla extract
- Labeled bottles of vanilla extract (optional)

## Process Steps

START:
1. Acquire vanilla beans and alcohol (rum or vodka).
2. Determine the amount of vanilla extract to be made based on the quantity of vanilla beans and alcohol available.

PROCESS: Preparing the Vanilla Beans and Alcohol
3. INPUT: Take the original bottle of vodka or rum.
4. PROCESS: Remove the alcohol from the original bottle.
5. PROCESS: Split the vanilla beans in half longitudinally to expose the seeds inside.
6. DECISION [IF]: Is bottle sanitization desired?
   - Yes: PROCESS: Sanitize the bottle using appropriate method.
   - No: Continue to next step.
7. PROCESS: Place the split vanilla beans into the now empty and optionally sanitized bottle.

PROCESS: Infusing the Alcohol
8. PROCESS: Pour the alcohol back into the bottle with the vanilla beans.
9. OUTPUT: The bottle is now filled with alcohol and vanilla beans ready for infusion.
10. PROCESS: Seal the bottle with a cap and label it with the current date.
11. PROCESS: Store the bottle in a dark cabinet.

PROCESS: Shaking and Infusion Period
12. PROCESS: Shake the bottle every day for the first week.
13. PROCESS: After the first week, shake the bottle once or twice a week.
14. DECISION [IF]: Has it been 2 months since the infusion started?
    - Yes: PROCESS: Proceed to OUTPUT step for the completed extraction phase.
    - No: CONTINUE the shaking and infusion process until 2 months are complete.

OUTPUT: Extract is Ready
15. OUTPUT: After 2 months, the vanilla extract is ready but will continue to improve for at least another 4-6 months.

PROCESS: Bottling (Optional)
16. DECISION [IF]: Is bottling the extract desired?
    - Yes: PROCESS: Transfer the extract into individual bottles, including a split vanilla bean in each for continued extraction.
    - No: END.

PROCESS: Labeling (Optional)
17. DECISION [IF]: Is labeling the bottles desired?
    - Yes: PROCESS: Design and print labels, then apply them to the bottles.
    - No: END.

END: The process of making homemade vanilla extract is complete.
```

```markdown
# Spider Snowflake Creation System

## Summary
This system describes the process of creating a spider snowflake inspired by "The Nightmare Before Christmas" movie, specifically the one made by the character Jack Skellington. - Begin the spider snowflake creation process.

  - Scissors

- Fold the paper in half as per the directions on the template.

  - IF 'Yes':
    - Proceed to carefully bend the paper to cut the legs.
  - ELSE:
    - Skip to the cutting along the black lines.

- Bend the paper slightly without creasing to make a slit between the spider's legs.
- Insert the scissors into the slit.

### PROCESS: [Cut Along Black Lines]
- Carefully cut along the black lines on the template to shape the spider snowflake.

### OUTPUT:
- The result is a Jack Skellington-inspired spider snowflake.

- The spider snowflake creation process is completed.
```

instruct00216.title: Modern Stainless Steel Home Numbers DIY
instruct00216.text: Just after we bought a house I discovered Pinterest. We had to wait six months before we got the keys so I had some time to pin interesting home ideas. Months of obsessive pinning passed before I finally worked out my own project. I really got inspired by this picture above, circulating on Pinterest and Instructables for a while.https://www.instructables.com/id/Modern-Industrial-House-Numbers/I decided to create my own version of this cool idea and I'm very happy with the end result. My first thought was to don't use the same kind of grid as the original idea had. Since my house number is 69, I wanted to try to make numbers have a nice curve.I did many tests in Photoshop with the spacing and different sizes for the screw heads, and also did trial and error tests on a wooden plank. For some reason i couldn't get the angle of the curve right to get a nice result. Since none of the results were satisfying, I gave the idea of using a fixed grid a go and I should of done that from the start. For this I eventually used Microsoft Excel and this really worked well. Just set the size of the cells at the same value as your screw heads. In my case that was 5mm. And then start designing your numbers by using capital O's to visualize your screws. After the many variations inspired on bitmap SEGA numbers, this was our winner. Luckily, I just had to turn around the 6 to get an identical 9. I replaced all the capital 'O's' with small round dots '.' which I centered in the cells. After printing and taping the two numbers on to the plank, I hit every dot with a hammer/nail to leave small marks in the wood. Make sure the alignment of the numbers is correct. In Dutch we have a rhyme "meten is weten", which means "measuring is knowing". Before I started with the bench drill, I cut the plank to the right size so it was more manageable while drilling. If you don't have an bench drill, try to drill with a straight vertical angle. Make sure that your drill isn't too small, because then you may get some cracks when you turn in the screws. Then all you have to do is treat it (multiple times) with paint or varnish so your wood will survive in all weather conditions. I used a clear varnish to keep the natural look of the wood. The final step was to turn in the screws. I did them all by hand because I didn't want to force the wood. Sometimes I had to redo complete rows because the screws had to much of an angle offset. When all 288 screws were firmly turned, all I had to to do was create a simple suspension method on the back, but this can be achieved in tons of ways. I used two keyhole shaped hangers on the back of the wood. The materials you need for this project: Screw driver Stainless steel screws (5 mm x 60 mm) Wooden plank Preferably a bench drill (or a hand drill with steady hand) Varnish or paint (paintbrush) Screw plugs, two keyhole hangers and screws to attach it to the wall (stone drill) Microsoft Excel or Apple's Numbers software. Patience Hopefully you liked my first project and post!Peter-Paul

```markdown
  - No: [ELSE] Consider using a fixed grid for better results.

## PROCESS: [Preparing the Wooden Plank]

- PROCESS: Cut the plank to a manageable size for drilling.

  - Yes: Continue to the next step.

- DECISION [IF]: Is the house number plank securely attached to the wall?
  - Yes: The installation is complete.
  - No: [ELSE] Ensure secure attachment before finishing.

## END:
- The DIY house number project is completed and the numbers are displayed outside the house.

## Required Materials:
- Screwdriver
- Stainless steel screws (5 mm x 60 mm)
- Wooden plank
- Bench drill or hand drill
- Varnish or paint (paintbrush)
- Screw plugs
- Two keyhole hangers and screws for wall attachment
- Microsoft Excel or Apple's Numbers
```

instruct00135.title: Chocolate Pudding Cupcakes With Strawberry Centers (Sweetheart Cupcakes)
instruct00135.text: I made these for my boys (and my daughter, too - can't leave anyone out!) and they were ALL GONE within 20 minutes of me putting them on the table. Super easy to make, super delicious, and super cute when you cut one in half!Ingredients: 1 package cake mix, chocolate 1 package strawberries, cleaned and hulled 1 package pudding, chocolate Fresh mint sprigs,optional but awesomeDirections: 1. Prepare cupcakes according to package and let cool. Using a paring knife, core out a well down into each cupcake, for your strawberry to fit into. Prepare your pudding according to the package. Let set until nice and pudding-y (solid - wet gloopy pudding will ruin the cupcakes, so don't be in a rush, let the pudding firm up!) 2. Stick the strawberry pointy side down into your cupcakes.Take the piece of the cupcake that you cut out, and place it on top of the strawberry, after you push it down into the cupcake. 3. Top liberally with pudding in leu of frosting. 4. Add a sprig of mint if you like. I think it adds a certain something, and my neighbor had some growing in her kitchen and sharedbut don't go out and buy some. 5.I cut each cutcake in half and set it on a plate, because presentation is everything with these suckers. They are DELICIOUS and super easy! We call them 'Sweetheart Cupcakes' because I made them for my sweethearts, and because the strawberry looks like a little symbol of love...before they started to shove them into their mouths, that is. ;)

instruct00323.title: How to Make a Very Berry Pie
instruct00323.text: A step by step guide to making a berry pie from scratch using fresh blueberries, raspberries, blackberries, and strawberries. Gather all the berries that you want to add to your pie. Gather all the ingredients that is needed. The berry filling: -2 lbs of fresh berries -1 oz of butter -3 oz of sugar -2 oz of water -1 oz of cornstarch -3.5 oz of sugar -1/5 tsp of salt -2 tsp lemon juice -.25 oz butter The crust: -1lb 4oz of pastry flour -14 oz of shortening -6 oz of cold water -.4 oz of salt -1 oz of sugar 1. Add the fruit into a saucepan. Place it on medium heat until the juices are released, then add the cornstarch with water. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Continue to simmer for about 10 minutes or until thick. 2. Remove from heat. Add the remaining ingredients and stir gently. Set aside and allow to cool. 1. Sift flour into a mixing bowl. 2. Cut shortening into flour. *For flaky dough, cut until fat particles are the size of peas. 3. Dissolve salt and sugar in water. 4. Add water to flour mixture. Mix very gently, just until water is absorbed. Do not overwork the dough. 1. Place dough in pans, cover and place in the refrigerator or retarder for at least 4 hours. 1. Roll out the dough to about an 1/8 of an inch. 2. Place the rolled out dough onto a pie pan. Fill the pie pan with the berry mixture. Cut the remaining dough into strips. Place the strips over the pie. Take strips and go under/over the strips that are already on the pie. Cut all the excess dough off. Here is what the pie should look like right before it is placed in the oven. Place the pie in the oven and bake at 425 degrees for about 30 to 40 minutes. This is what the pie should look like when it is done.

```markdown
# Berry Pie Recipe System

## Ingredients
- Berry Filling:
  - 2 lbs fresh berries (blueberries, raspberries, blackberries, strawberries)
  - 1 oz butter
  - 3 oz sugar
  - 2 oz water
  - 1 oz cornstarch
  - 3.5 oz sugar
  - 1/5 tsp salt
  - 2 tsp lemon juice
  - 0.25 oz butter
- Crust:
  - 1 lb 4 oz pastry flour
  - 14 oz shortening
  - 6 oz cold water
  - 0.4 oz salt
  - 1 oz sugar

## Process

### START: Making the Berry Pie
PROCESS: Gather all the required ingredients.

### Making the Berry Filling
INPUT: Fresh berries.
PROCESS: Add the berries to a saucepan and heat on medium until juices are released.
INPUT: 1 oz cornstarch and 2 oz water.
PROCESS: Mix cornstarch with water and add to the saucepan.
PROCESS: Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to simmer.
PROCESS: Simmer for about 10 minutes or until thick.
PROCESS: Remove from heat.
INPUT: 3.5 oz sugar, 1/5 tsp salt, 2 tsp lemon juice, 0.25 oz butter.
PROCESS: Add the remaining ingredients to the saucepan and stir gently.
PROCESS: Set aside the berry filling to cool.

### Making the Crust
INPUT: 1 lb 4 oz pastry flour.
PROCESS: Sift flour into a mixing bowl.
INPUT: 14 oz shortening.
PROCESS: Cut shortening into flour until fat particles are the size of peas.
INPUT: 0.4 oz salt and 1 oz sugar dissolved in 6 oz cold water.
PROCESS: Add water mixture to flour mixture.
PROCESS: Mix very gently, just until water is absorbed.
DECISION: Is the dough overworked?
  IF No: Continue to next step.
  ELSE: Stop and correct dough consistency.
PROCESS: Place dough in pans, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.

### Assembling the Pie
PROCESS: Roll out the dough to about 1/8 of an inch thickness.
PROCESS: Place the rolled-out dough onto a pie pan.
INPUT: Prepared berry mixture.
PROCESS: Fill the pie pan with the berry mixture.
PROCESS: Cut the remaining dough into strips.
PROCESS: Weave the strips over the pie creating a lattice.
PROCESS: Trim the excess dough off the edges.

### Baking the Pie
PROCESS: Preheat oven to 425 degrees Fahrenheit.
PROCESS: Place the pie in the oven.
PROCESS: Bake for about 30 to 40 minutes or until crust is golden brown.
OUTPUT: Finished berry pie.

### END: Berry Pie is ready to serve.
```

instruct00460.title: How to Wear a Wig With Long Hair
instruct00460.text: Wigs are awesome, but they can be hard to wear with long hair. This tutorial will show you how to tuck and hide all that long hair so you can wear a wig with long hair! *As shown by my picture, wigs make you happy!Just a warning, if your wig is tight (small) and/or you have thick hair, this still might not work with your hair, but try it out to see :) First, here is what I used.Supplies: Wig - The wig I used was a short black one I bought from ebay for my Halloween costume. Stay tuned to see it!Wig Cap - these are pretty cheap.Bobby Pins - Roller pins work really nice We are going to start by doing separating your hair right down the middle and doing two french braids. Here is a tutorial on how to do a French Braid. Now we are going to swirl and tuck those braids into a Heidi Braid hairstyle. I take the first braid and bring it under the opposite braid and up and around the front of my head. Originally I secured the braid at my crown, but this time I secured it a couple inches from the crown of my head. When it was at the front of my head it seemed to catch and hold the wig on better, but I feel it was more noticeable. You can put the braids wherever you want. I secured the braid with bobby pins around the front. I left it looser at the back, but you can bobby pin that if you want too. After securing the first braid, I took the next braid and crossed that under the opposite braid and brought it around the front of the previous braid. I, again, secured it with bobby pins. If you don't have a hair cap, that's fine. I used a hair cap to help hold the braids in place, to keep the bobby pins from sticking into the wig, and to help hold in those stray hairs. Try to tuck as much hair under the cap as you can. Time to put on your wig! Since I had the braids at the base of my skull, I found it easier to put the wig on starting from there. The braids help hold the wig so it doesn't try to slide right off as you stretch it over your head. Optional: once the wig is on, you can use bobby pins or other hair clips to hold the wig on. Mine had a hook at the back I could use to tighten it. Enjoy your ability to hide your long hair and wear a wig!

instruct00730.title: Gutterless Rain Barrel - a "Drain Barrel"
instruct00730.text: I wanted to share instructions on how to build a "drain barrel" for those of you who may not have gutters on your house. This project is most useful for those of us who have a clearly-defined gouge in our wood chips where the water pours off the roof. Purchase three cedar decking boards and screw them together in the shape of a trough. Seal all joined edges with a clear silicone caulk. Obtain containers in which the capture the rainwater; it would be best to find containers with about a 2" opening. Line up the containers and measure the distance between the center of the containers' openings. Leave about 1/2" per container for expansion. Measure the diameter of the container's opening and use a hole saw (attached to the drill) to make holes in the trough. Purchase a 10' length of PVC pipe. It should be slightly less in diameter than your hole. Count the number of holes and divide evenly. Cut the PVC into equal lengths. Purchase a narrowing PVC conduit to glue to the top of your pipes. Drill two holes in the widest part of the conduit and use a miter saw to remove the material between the holes. This will make a slit to help drain the water into the pipe and ultimately into your container. Construct some simple "feet" to attach to the ends of the trough. If you drill a hole in the middle of the end of the trough, you will be able to swivel the trough up-side-down on the lag bolt to prevent snow from weighing the trough down during the winter. Dig a hole on both ends for the "feet", level the trough, and add concrete to prevent the structure from moving during a hard rain. Rake the area under the trough so that you can remove the containers easily. Insert the PVC pipe, and add metal menders if you like to ensure the container's slit stays level with the trough. When it rains, the water will be directed from the trough, into the PVC pipe and then into your container. When the container is full, lift the PVC pipe out of the mouth of the container, remove the container, and water your plants. When the container is empty, put it back under the trough and slip the PVC pipe back down into the mouth of the container. If you like, you can purchase a rain barrel with which to pour the full containers.

```markdown
# Drain Barrel Construction Summary

## System Overview
The system described is a method for constructing a drain barrel to capture rainwater without gutters. It involves building a trough, preparing containers, and setting up a PVC pipe system to direct water into the containers.

## System Steps

### START:
- Begin the construction of a drain barrel system.

### INPUT: Materials Required
- Three cedar decking boards
- Clear silicone caulk
- Containers with approximately 2" openings
- 10' length of PVC pipe (diameter slightly less than the container openings)
- Narrowing PVC conduit
- Concrete
- Metal menders (optional)
- Tools (screwdriver, drill with hole saw, miter saw, shovel)

### PROCESS: Constructing the Trough
- Screw the cedar decking boards together to form a trough.
- Seal all joined edges with clear silicone caulk.

### PROCESS: Preparing Containers
- Line up the containers and measure the distance between the centers of the openings, allowing 0.5" per container for expansion.

### PROCESS: Drilling Holes in the Trough
- Measure the diameter of the containers' openings.
- Using a hole saw attached to a drill, create holes in the trough corresponding to the diameters measured.

### PROCESS: Preparing PVC Pipes
- Count the number of holes in the trough.
- Divide the 10' length of PVC pipe into equal lengths based on the number of holes.
- Purchase and attach a narrowing PVC conduit to the top of each PVC pipe segment.

### PROCESS: Modifying PVC Conduits
- Drill two holes in the widest part of each conduit.
- Use a miter saw to remove the material between the holes, creating a slit for water drainage.

### PROCESS: Constructing Trough Feet
- Construct simple feet to attach to the ends of the trough.
- Drill a hole in the middle of the end of the trough for the lag bolt.

### DECISION: Is it winter?
- IF YES: Swivel the trough upside-down on the lag bolt to prevent snow accumulation.
- IF NO: Proceed to the next step.

### PROCESS: Installing the Trough
- Dig holes for the feet at both ends of the trough.
- Level the trough.
- Add concrete to stabilize the structure.

### PROCESS: Final Assembly
- Rake the area under the trough for easy container removal.
- Insert the PVC pipes into the holes in the trough.
- Add metal menders to keep the container's slit level with the trough (optional).

### OUTPUT: Rainwater Capture System
- The constructed trough and PVC pipe system are ready to capture rainwater.

### PROCESS: Using the System
- When it rains, water is directed from the trough into the PVC pipes and then into containers.
- When a container is full, remove it and use the water for plants.
- Replace the empty container under the trough and reinsert the PVC pipe.

### DECISION: Is a rain barrel needed for storage?
- IF YES: Purchase a rain barrel to pour the full containers into.
- IF NO: Continue using individual containers.

### END:
- The drain barrel system is now complete and operational.
```

instruct00470.title: Dribble Castle Sandcastle
instruct00470.text: I was taught how to make dribble castle sandcastles when I was young. There was someone making one on the beach and they showed me the technique, which is easy to learn. In this Instructable, I will show you how to make a Dribble Castle, so next time you are at the beach, you can make one. You want to pick a spot on the beach where the biggest waves only just reach. It is better to pick a time of day when the tide is going out. This way your castle will hopefully survive a couple of hours. You want the big waves to be able to reach the hole to get the sand in the hole wet. Too high up the beach and you will not get wet sand. Too low on the beach and your castle will be destroyed by the waves. Make the base of your castle by making a pile of sand, that you dig out of the hole, by placing it on the uphill side of the hole. You want the hole to be closest to the ocean. Pack the sand down so that it makes a strong base for your dribble castle. Some beaches have smooth sand on top and coarse sand and shells further down. Once you get your hole and base the size you want, scrape some of the smooth sand from the surface into the hole. This smooth sand works best for the dribble castle. If you picked your spot well, a big wave will wash up on the beach and get water into the hole. Grab a hand full of wet sand out of the hole and drop it on top of the base. This blob of wet sand will give the wet sand, that you are going to dribble, a place to stick. If you try and dribble wet sand on to dry sand it does not work that well, and the wet sand may just fall off. Pick up a hand full of wet sand and make a fist. With your thumb pointing down, let the wet sand dribble off your thumb and onto the wet blob that you put there earlier. You can also let the wet sand dribble off your fingers, but I think it is easier to make accurate drips with my thumb down. Experiment with different amounts of sand. After a while you will figure out the right amount of sand and how wet the sand should be to make the best dribble castle. I made a video showing how to make a Dribble Castle. I was very lucky with the timing of the big wave.As always,Thanks for watching and enjoy.

```markdown
## Step-by-Step Process

- Yes: Continue the process.
- No: Wait for the tide to start going out or choose a different time.

### PROCESS: Making the Base
- INPUT: Dig a hole near the chosen spot, placing the sand on the uphill side to form the base.

- Yes: Scrape the smooth sand into the hole.

- OUTPUT: Place the wet sand blob on the base to create a sticky surface.

- No: Add more water to the sand or place another wet sand blob.

### PROCESS: Dribbling Technique
- INPUT: Pick up another handful of wet sand.
- PROCESS: Make a fist and let the sand dribble off your thumb onto the wet blob.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the sand dripping accurately?
- Yes: Continue building the castle.
- No: Try letting the sand dribble off your fingers instead.

### PROCESS: Experimentation
- PROCESS: Experiment with different amounts of wet sand and dripping techniques.
- OUTPUT: Determine the right amount of sand and moisture level for optimal castle building.

### PROCESS: Building the Castle
- PROCESS: Continue adding sand by dribbling it over the structure to grow the castle.

### OUTPUT:
- The final Dribble Castle Sandcastle is complete.

### END:
- The process of making the Dribble Castle Sandcastle concludes.
```

instruct00387.title: How to Load Film Into a 35mm Camera
instruct00387.text: This provides information on loading film and adjusting the main settings on a 35mm camera. Locate the Rewind Knob, on the left side of the camera, and pull up until the back of the camera opens. Cut a Leader for your film to load into the Take-Up Spool. The leader must be approximately 22mm to fit into spool. Place the film into the left side of the camera. Push the Rewind Knob down to create a snug fit on the film after it is placed into the pocket. Pull the leader of film over to the Take-Up Spool. Insert the narrow end of the film leader into the slot. Hold the spool steady with one hand and push the film deep inside until film is way inside spool or comes out the other side. Make sure the teeth are properly placed on both sides of the film. Use the rewind knob to take in any slack in the film, tighten the film to the camera. Then close the back of the camera and use the film advance to wind the film. Take 3 pictures. If the film has been loaded properly the rewind knob will turn ever time you crank the film advance lever. If not, make sure the slack has been taken out of the film by retightening the film to the camera. Make sure you take at least 2 pictures to clear out the exposed film and start with fresh film. Once you see the number 1 in the window, you are ready to take pictures. Now its time to set your ISO Film Speed. To set film speed, gently lift up the ISO speed ring and turn it to your desired ISO speed shown in the window. (this should rotate the numbers on the INSIDE window on the ring) To set Shutter Speed, rotate the shutter speed ring to desired shutter speed. The shutter controls the length of exposure, on this camera, the higher the number, the less the exposure time. (this should rotate the numbers on the OUTSIDE of the ring) To set the aperture, turn the aperture ring to desired aperture. The larger the aperture number, the smaller the aperture opening will be and less the light will be transmitted to the film. (the dial closest to the camera) This camera has a built in meter. When you press the shutter release button down about one third of the way, you will activate the meter. While the meter is activated, rotate the shutter speed dial or the aperture ring until only the green o LED is lit. when you see the red + LED light, this means your subject is too bright. To fix this, change to a higher shutter speed or aperture. When you see the red LED light, this means your subject is too dark. Change to a lower shutter speed or aperture. The goal is to achieve the green o LED light for best results. To set a timer, push down on the self-timer lever until it stops. When you are ready to take the photo, push the shutter release button completely to activate the timer. The photo will be taken in 10 seconds. (the length of the timer could depend on the make and model of the camera) Once you have completed the roll of film, you must rewind it back into the canister. To rewind your film, press the film release button on the bottom of the camera. Fold out the film rewind crank and turn it in the direction of the arrow until you feel no more tension on the knob. Pull up on the film rewind knob until the back cover of the camera opens. The film should be rolled back inside the film canister and it is now ready to be developed.

```markdown
# 35mm Camera Film Loading and Settings Adjustment System

## Film Loading Process

### START: Initiate the Film Loading Sequence
- INPUT: Locate the Rewind Knob on the left side of the camera.

### PROCESS: Open the Camera Back
- Pull up the Rewind Knob until the back of the camera opens.

### INPUT: Prepare the Film
- Cut a Leader for the film to load into the Take-Up Spool, ensuring it is approximately 22mm.

### PROCESS: Insert the Film
- Place the film into the left side of the camera.

### PROCESS: Secure the Film Canister
- Push the Rewind Knob down to create a snug fit on the film after it is placed into the pocket.

### PROCESS: Attach the Film Leader to the Take-Up Spool
- Pull the leader of film over to the Take-Up Spool.
- Insert the narrow end of the film leader into the slot on the spool.

### PROCESS: Ensure Correct Film Placement
- Hold the Take-Up Spool steady with one hand and push the film deep inside.
- Ensure the teeth on the spool engage properly with the film on both sides.

### PROCESS: Remove Slack from the Film
- Use the Rewind Knob to take in any slack in the film and tighten it to the camera.

### PROCESS: Close the Camera Back
- Close the back of the camera.

### DECISION [IF]: Is the Film Loaded Properly?
- Use the film advance lever to wind the film and take 3 pictures.
- IF the Rewind Knob turns with each crank, OUTPUT: The film is loaded properly.
- ELSE: Retighten the film to the camera and repeat the process.

### PROCESS: Advance the Film to Unexposed Frames
- Take at least 2 pictures to clear out the exposed film.

### OUTPUT: Camera Ready to Take Pictures
- Once the number 1 is visible in the window, the camera is ready for use.

## Camera Settings Adjustment

### PROCESS: Set ISO Film Speed
- Lift the ISO speed ring gently and turn it to the desired ISO speed shown in the window.

### PROCESS: Set Shutter Speed
- Rotate the shutter speed ring to the desired shutter speed.

### PROCESS: Set Aperture
- Turn the aperture ring to the desired aperture.

### PROCESS: Activate the Built-In Meter
- Press the shutter release button down about one-third of the way to activate the meter.

### DECISION [IF]: Adjust Exposure Based on Meter Readings
- IF the green o LED is lit, OUTPUT: Exposure is correct.
- IF the red + LED is lit (too bright), PROCESS: Increase shutter speed or aperture.
- IF the red - LED is lit (too dark), PROCESS: Decrease shutter speed or aperture.

### PROCESS: Set a Timer (if applicable)
- Push down on the self-timer lever until it stops.
- Push the shutter release button completely to activate the timer for a 10-second delay.

## Film Rewinding Process

### PROCESS: Rewind the Completed Roll of Film
- Press the film release button on the bottom of the camera.

### PROCESS: Engage the Film Rewind Crank
- Fold out the film rewind crank and turn it in the direction of the arrow until there is no more tension.

### END: Remove the Film
- Pull up on the film rewind knob until the back cover opens.
- OUTPUT: The film is rolled back inside the canister and is ready for development.
```

instruct00296.title: How to Stop People From Using Your WIFI Using Cmd
instruct00296.text: In this instructable, I'm going to teach you how to stop people from hogging your WIFI using cmd. This can be used if they are watching Youtube, Netflix, or doing other Bandwith activities while you are trying to watch Youtube, Netflix, play online games, etc. and you want them to stop. Or if you really just hate someone. First, open cmd. If you don't know how to do this, hold the Windows Key + R, type "cmd" in the box that comes up, and then hit enter or type "cmd" in the search box. Type "ipconfig" into cmd then hit enter. If you are using wifi find your wifi adapter and if you are using ethernet, then find your ethernet adapter. Next, find the IP listed under default gateway. This is your WIFI router's IP. Copy it down. Mine is 192.168.1.1 This is a common IP for a router. Now go to your internet browser. In the address bar type the IP we just found. Most routers come with a default username and password needed to log on. To find your default username and password go to http://www.routerpasswords.com/. Once you are logged in, find where your connected devices are displayed. Mine are in a section on the home page. Then find the IP of the person you want to kick. I will demonstrate this on my phone. It is named "robyn-HP" and it's IP is "192.168.1.16" (Yes I know that doesn't sound like a phone's name, but I have it named like that for a separate reason) Next, create a new text document. I have an editor named Notepad++ Which isn't required, but it is a better alternative to the standard notepad. In that text document, type "@echo off" and then "ping (THE IP YOU FOUND) -t -l 65500" as shown in the photo. So for me, I would type "ping 192.168.1.16 -t -l 65500". This will be our kicking device. Save this as a .bat file by clicking save and typing ".bat" after your file name as shown in the photo. Lastly, run the .bat file as quickly as you can about 20 or so times. If you have a better computer you can do more. Now, sit back and wait. DON'T CLOSE THE PROGRAMS. In the first photo, I took a speed test before I started the programs. My phone got a download of 20 MB/s and upload of 12 MB/s. In the next photo, I did a speed test just 15 seconds after I started the programs. It then had a download of 11 MB/s and upload of 6 MB/s. In the last photo, I did a speed test about 4 minutes after I started the programs. It showed a download of 0.5 MB/s and upload of 0.9 MB/s. At that speed, the person will be wasting their time, and will probably stop using your wifi because it is now useless to them. Thank you, and have a great day!

instruct00409.title: Pumpkin Lifter Assistive Technology
instruct00409.text: You say it is difficult to balance while lifting pumpkins from the ground to waist level? The pumpkin/squash lifter helps people who cannot bend down to pick up melons, squash, and other bulky items from the ground. It is built with conduit and pitchfork tines. It is a piece of -inch metal conduit 36-inches long with a 6-inch bend in it. We spread the tines of a pitchfork wider and slightly up so the make a slight bowl shape. We slid rubber hose over the tines, so they are soft on the melons. The pitchfork tines are bolted into the conduit. An arm support handle is clamped on with hose clamps to give better control with one arm. It works very well picking up watermelons and cantaloupe. The handle can be lengthened, or the angles changed to make it more comfortable for individual workers. A cutter could be added on it for clipping the pumpkin vines in the future. You will needsome old pitchfork tines4-feet of 1/2" metal electrical conduit or an old tent pole with a 90-degree bend.4-feet of 1/4" vinyl tubinga robo handlea clip or small bolt.If you are not repurposing an old pitchfork, then purchase the refuse fork with 90-degree tines instead of a pitchfork and conduit.Tools you will need are:a torch to heat and bend the pitch fork tines,a hack saw to cut the conduit to length, anda drill to drill through the conduit and tines. Clamp your pitch fork or refuse hook tightly, then heat and bend the edge tines outward so the tines form a basket shape to hold round objects from rolling off the side tines. If you purchased a refuse fork with 90-degree tines you can skip to line 3 and attach the robo handle.Purchase a section of 3/4-inch metal electrical conduit with a 90-degree bend from a local hardware store.Cut the conduit with 90-degree bend so it is a comfortable length for you to reach the ground. Usually about 48-inches-long.Purchase a robo handle ergonomic handle from an online arthritis supply retailer and clamp it onto the conduit to make a comfortable handle. After the tines have been bent and cooled,Slide vinyl tubing over the tines so the sharp points are covered and they are cushioned for the items being picked up. If necessary heat with a heat gun so the vinyl flexes around the corners easily.Insert the tines handle into the short side of the bent conduit. Drill a hole through both the conduit and tines handle and insert a small bolt or pin to secure the tines to the conduit. Adjust the robo handle on the conduit with the tines facing toward you. Adjust the robo handle so you can comfortably grip it and lower the tines to the ground without bending over. Walk to the melon or squash or pumpkin needed.Lower tines to the ground and nudge the melon onto the tines with your toe.Lift the melon to waist height and remove it from the tines with your other hand or carry it to the crate.

```markdown
# Pumpkin/Squash Lifter System Summary

## Overview
The system is designed to aid in lifting pumpkins, melons, squash, and other bulky items from the ground to waist level without the need for bending down. It utilizes modified pitchfork tines attached to a piece of metal conduit with an ergonomic handle for better control.

## System Process

### START:
- Begin the process of creating a pumpkin/squash lifter.

### INPUT: Gather Materials
- Old pitchfork tines or a refuse fork with 90-degree tines.
- 4-feet of 1/2" metal electrical conduit or an old tent pole with a 90-degree bend.
- 4-feet of 1/4" vinyl tubing.
- A robo handle (ergonomic handle).
- A clip or small bolt.

### INPUT: Gather Tools
- A torch for heating and bending the pitchfork tines.
- A hacksaw for cutting the conduit.
- A drill for drilling holes to attach the tines to the conduit.

### PROCESS: Modify Tines (If necessary)
- Clamp the pitchfork or refuse hook tightly.
- Heat and bend the edge tines outward to form a basket shape using a torch.
  - [IF] A refuse fork with 90-degree tines was purchased:
    - [OUTPUT] Skip to attaching the robo handle.
  - [ELSE] Continue with bending process.

### PROCESS: Prepare Conduit
- Purchase a section of 3/4-inch metal electrical conduit with a 90-degree bend.
- Cut the conduit to a comfortable length (usually about 48 inches) using a hacksaw.

### PROCESS: Attach Robo Handle
- Purchase a robo handle from an online arthritis supply retailer.
- Clamp the robo handle onto the conduit to make a comfortable handle.

### PROCESS: Cover Tines with Vinyl Tubing
- Slide vinyl tubing over the tines to cover sharp points and cushion them.
  - [IF] Necessary:
    - Heat with a heat gun for easier flexing of vinyl around corners.

### PROCESS: Attach Tines to Conduit
- Insert the tines handle into the short side of the bent conduit.
- Drill a hole through both the conduit and tines handle.
- Insert a small bolt or pin to secure the tines to the conduit.

### PROCESS: Adjust Robo Handle
```

instruct00513.text: Parts list:3" Bamboo (or PVC) pipes, 5' tall (2 count) 10gal Aquarium (50 Qt. Add your pump to the container/fish tank and connect the 1/2" threaded barb to the pump and black tubing.2. Add your media (aquarium pebbles, etc).
```markdown
# Structured Summary of DIY Aquaponics System Blog Post

## System Overview
The system is designed to create a DIY aquaponics setup using commonly available materials. The goal is to construct a system where fish and plants can symbiotically thrive, with the plants benefiting from the nutrients in the fish waste and the fish benefiting from cleaner water as a result of the plants filtering it.

## Materials List
- START: Begin by gathering all necessary materials.
  - INPUT: Materials required include bamboo (or PVC) pipes, an aquarium or plastic storage bin, a water pump, tubing, PVC fittings, aquarium pebbles, a heater, ball valves, and plastic bottles or net pots.

## Building the Grow Pipes
- PROCESS: Measure and prepare the bamboo or PVC pipes.
  - INPUT: Measure the height of the fish tank or plastic container.
  - PROCESS: Mark the pipe at the height of the fish tank.
  - PROCESS: Drill holes 8 inches apart from the center point of each hole, starting from the mark.
  - DECISION [IF]: Is there a hole drilled below the mark for fish movement?
    - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
    - No: Drill the necessary hole.
  - PROCESS: Use a file or sandpaper to smooth off any plastic burrs.

## Preparing the Lid
- PROCESS: Trace and cut holes in the lid for the pipes.
  - INPUT: Trace the pipe ends onto the lid of the container.
  - PROCESS: Use a jigsaw to cut the holes, ensuring a snug fit by cutting 1mm inside the lines.

## Setting Up the Pump and Media
- PROCESS: Install the pump and connect it to the tubing.
  - INPUT: Add the pump to the container or fish tank.
  - PROCESS: Connect the 1/2" threaded barb to the pump and the black tubing.
- PROCESS: Add the media to the system.
  - INPUT: Introduce aquarium pebbles or similar media.
  - OUTPUT: Ensure that the media volume is at least 10% of the total system volume for bacteria colonization.
- DECISION [IF]: Does the pump come with an attached filter?
  - Yes: Proceed to the next step.
  - No: Create a filter using a net pot, sponge, and zip tie.

## Assembling the Drip System
- PROCESS: Measure and cut PVC pipes for the drip system.
  - INPUT: Measure the distance between the centers of the grow pipes.
  - PROCESS: Cut two pieces of 1/2 inch PVC pipe to fit between the T-Shape drippers.
  - PROCESS: Connect the pieces to the T-Shape drippers.
  - PROCESS: Cap the two ends with PVC end caps.
- DECISION [IF]: Is additional water flow control needed?
  - Yes: Add 2 ball valves to the drip outlets.
  - No: Proceed without adding ball valves.

## Preparing Plant Holders
- PROCESS: Repurpose plastic bottles as plant holders.
  - INPUT: Reuse plastic bottles with holes cut into them to hold seedlings.
  - PROCESS: Ensure enough holes are made for proper water flow and root growth.

## Finalizing the System
- PROCESS: Add water and prepare for fish.
  - INPUT: Fill the system with water.
  - PROCESS: Use a dechlorination product or let the water sit for 24+ hours.
- PROCESS: Introduce fish to the system.
  - INPUT: Add 1 or 2 small goldfish to the tank.
- PROCESS: Plant the seedlings.
  - INPUT: Add seedlings that have developed 3-4 true leaves.
  - OUTPUT: The system is now operational with both fish and plants in place.
- END: The DIY aquaponics system is complete and ready for maintenance and observation.
```

instruct00580.title: HDTv Antenna on a Direct TV Mount.
instruct00580.text: I got my Tv converter Box (with the Government program Coupon). I hooked up with a regular rabbit ear antenna and although the signal and quality are waaaay better that the analog ones, I couldn't get all the stations and some where a bit erratic. I went on Google and start looking for HDTV antennas and I found several easy to make DIYs setups, but they can be big and ugly to keep in my living room. So, I build the antenna but and I use an old Direct TV dish mounted in my garage (I don't have the subscription and I don't want too), the dish has been in my place since I move, and the best thing, it's wired to my living room. Note: The antenna works independently from the dish, I'm just using the dish as a mounting device and since it's already wired to the living room works great for me. Wire , can be romex or cloth hanger wire. Screws and washers, assorted ones Standard wire mesh or similar wire screen, can use a metal rack shelves, chicken wire, etc. mine is 24" x 14" Coaxial cable connection plug. 1 piece of wood, can be 2"x2" ir 2"x4" 14" to 16" long. and of course a used Direct Tv or similar Dish. soldier gun and electrical tape. Note: I did mine with only 3 pairs of "Vs" (or ears if you may) but I have seen other antennas with 4 or 6 pair, which I guess incresses the reception. The configuration of the antenna is quite simple, lumelab.com used to have a page with the plans and measurements but it's been down for a long time now. The idea is basically to have 2, 3 or more sets of pair of wires in a "V" shape interconnected together in a cross series. Make sure that the cables connecting the "V"s don't touch each other, so is better to use isolated wires. I spread my "V"so 7" apart, screwed in the piece of wood of 2"x2" and 14" long, using washers to keep them in place and as good contact point to the antennas and the bare wire. Finally I soldier the end of the wire to a regular Tv male connection. The antenna needs a "screen", I used a regular wire screen for landscaping but any type of screen will work (I have seen cardboard wrapped with tin foil as screen). I took down the Dish and rip all the wires and receivers that I wont use anymore. The mounting was quite easy, I measure the middle of the dish to make a hole for the mounting. The dish is made out of plastic or fiver glass so is easy to drill a hole in it. After that I placed the wire screen on top of the dish and I centered. The antenna came later, to attach the antenna, basically the piece of 2"x2", I use a electrical pipe hanger, as shown in the pictures, and bolted to the dish it kept the screen and the antenna in place neatly. After that it was just to put the Dish back in place, hooked up the cable and it's done. The only thing left was setting the direction of the antenna to get a better reception, I'm Berkeley Ca, and facing the antenna to the southwest works better for most of the channels. from almost 30 channels, some with a weak or none signal, it went up to almost 40 with noticeable improvement and quite happy that I don't need an antenna in the living room anymore.
